R' Leib Sarahs's Seven-Year War with the Austrian Emperor Joseph II (A Folk Legend)

[History — folk legend.] Moshe Feinkind.
R' Leib Sarahs's Seven-Year War
with the Austrian Emperor Joseph the Second.
(A folk legend).

When the Austrian Emperor Joseph II in the year 1781 (5541) granted the Jews certain civil rights on condition that the Jews send their children to the schools, the pious Jews at once began to raise an uproar, regarding it as a dreadful decree by which the government intended nothing but to lead the Jewish children away from their faith.
The maskilim of Mendelssohn's "heder", with R' Naftali Hirtz Wessely at their head, on the other hand rejoiced greatly at this imperial decree. Wessely even wrote out of joy a "song of praise and thanks" in honour of the Emperor for the kindness he was doing the Jews by taking into account [sic] his demand regarding the schools for Jewish children.
Wessely also came out at once with an open struggle against the Orthodox, in word and in writing, in his well-known letters "Divrei Shalom ve-Emet", which aroused the anger and wrath of the fanatics still more. And seeing that all their efforts in the ruling circles to annul the "school decree" met with no success, the "pious" turned to R' Leib Sarahs, and he at once declared war on the Austrian Emperor himself[?] and announced his defiance of him until he would annul this decree...
No sooner said than done...
Every Friday before candle-lighting R' Leib Sarahs harnesses his horse and wagon, from his little town [—?] to Vienna. The coachman sat down with his face turned towards him, and as he took the reins into his own hand, the little horses flew like an arrow from a bow and drove with him straight to the imperial palace.
And when R' Leib Sarahs steps down from the wagon, he ordered the coachman to drive to one side and wait for him until he came back...
And R' Leib Sarahs then strides freely and openly through the park into the palace. The sentries standing there do not notice him. He passes through all the rooms and nobody disturbs him; nobody asks him what he wants or whom he is looking for here...
He enters the throne room, where Joseph II sat comfortably on his throne with all the ministers around him, and still nobody notices him.
But the Emperor suddenly sees standing before him an old Jew with a long white beard and a big stick in his hand. Joseph II is frightened by the strange figure of the old man and asks the ministers who allowed this old beggar to cross the threshold of the palace...
The ministers shrug their shoulders, look around in astonishment into every corner, but they see not even a shadow...
The frightened Emperor goes on shouting: there he stands, there he goes, seize him, lock him up in prison; "save me from his hands," the poor Emperor begs his ministers, "I no longer have the strength to bear his blows"...
At the Emperor's cries all the courtiers also came running, but nobody sees R' Leib Sarahs. The courtiers think to themselves: it can be nothing else but that the Emperor has lost his mind or that someone has bewitched him.
The courtiers try to calm the unnerved Emperor; meanwhile the Sabbath approaches, and R' Leib Sarahs hurriedly leaves the palace, and just as nobody saw when he came in, nobody saw when he went out. A "ro'eh ve-eino nir'eh" (one who sees but is not seen) was our R' Leib Sarahs.
And he got back to his little town in good time before candle-lighting — he had "kfitzat ha-derekh" (the miraculous shortening of the way)...
And so for seven years on end, every Friday before Kabbalat Shabbat, R' Leib Sarahs took a ride with his little horses to Vienna, paid a visit to Emperor Joseph II and carried out on him with his stick the "sentence"[?] in his usual manner...
It did not help to reinforce the sentries around the palace and inside the palace itself: exactly at the appointed time [printed "בו", apparently for "צו"] R' Leib Sarahs would appear in the imperial rooms, give the Emperor a good beating and then vanish again.
Nobody else saw or heard him, only the unhappy Emperor himself. So Joseph II set out on the road to seek out R' Leib Sarahs and make peace with him. He wanders from town to town, wherever the world has an end, and wandered so long until he reached the town of Yaltushkov [Jałtuszków], where R' Leib Sarahs was staying at the time.
Here the Emperor goes from house to house until he hits upon R' Leib Sarahs's home. But he does not find him at home; his household tell him that he has set out on a long journey and when he will come back they too cannot know...
Joseph II becomes sad and prepares to make his way back on foot to Vienna. On leaving, however, he asks the household to tell R' Leib Sarahs, as soon as he comes home, that he no longer has the strength to bear the terrible torments he inflicts on him, because of which he will have to leave the world before his time. But — the Emperor begged — tell him also that he should know that he too will then have to depart this life because of him...
And hardly had the Austrian Emperor managed to step over the threshold of his residence when he fell ill. The doctors had no proven remedy for him and therefore they had already given him up entirely...
Meanwhile R' Leib Sarahs also came home, and his household at once told him that some "Deitsch" (German) had been there looking for him and, not finding him, had told them to tell him that because of him he must leave the world before his time, but that in return he, R' Leib Sarahs, would also [—?] at once pay for it with his life...
Hearing this tidings from his household, R' Leib Sarahs at once rent his garment in mourning and wept bitterly, crying aloud that since this impurity had been in his house, he must already take leave of the sinful world — for so it had been decreed in Heaven [printed "גגזור" for "נגזר"]...
And R' Leib Sarahs suddenly fell ill; he lay down in his broken-down little bed; no doctor in the world knew what the illness was, and consequently did not know what remedy to prescribe for him; and in the same night in which Emperor Joseph II died, our R' Leib Sarahs also passed away in that little town of Yaltushkov.
For seven whole years — the folk legend relates — R' Leib Sarahs waged a bloody war with the Austrian Emperor over the "school decree", and both fell on the battlefield, and neither would yield to the other.
And the "school decree" was not annulled. And had not the coachman, after the death of his holy master, revealed the secret of the journeys that R' Leib Sarahs made every Friday to Vienna, and that that "Deitsch" had been none other than Emperor Joseph II in person, nobody would know of this great secret to this day.
As such a[?] secret R' Leib Sarahs kept it during his lifetime — he wanted to keep the war for a mitzvah for the World to Come...
German Goods Are Stained with Jewish Blood! — Hitleriad. (S. Rotenberg)

[Essay — Nazi Germany; anti-Hitler protest.] S. Rotenberg.

Hitleriad.

For years Hitler and his gang played upon the basest instincts of the German people, and just as in bullfights the toreadors provoke the wild beasts with red cloths to make them eager for battle, so too did Hitler provoke the German mob with the slogan of Jew-murder and free, unpunished plunder. The smell of blood narcotised a large part of the German people, and it chose Hitler as its Führer.

It is a tragedy and a stain of shame on all of humanity that in the very heart of Europe, in the year 1933, seventeen million people chose as their leader and guide a small-brained demagogue, the core of whose programme consists of the extermination of the Jews and the annihilation of every free thought.

The autos-da-fé in Spain were, after all, trifling illuminations compared with the terrible conflagration that Hitler has kindled in Germany. Even the dark monks [?] of the Middle Ages, when they persecuted Jews, did so ostensibly in the name of love of mankind — in order to bring the "strays" back under God's wing and secure them a place in the "eternal kingdom". But for all their base hypocrisy they still gave the Jews a chance to save themselves through apostasy or by leaving the country. The degenerate Hitler rules out this alternative: he cannot even forgive those who have already been Christians for ten generations, and he digs out of old archives proofs of Jewishness against families that have not the slightest notion of their Jewish descent; on the other hand, he takes away from the Jews their foreign passports and makes it impossible for them to leave the country.

There is no doubt that in Germany we are dealing with a pathological mass psychosis that may lead the world to fatal consequences unless radical measures are taken immediately.

How ridiculous, then, is our century's boasting of the progress of civilisation and culture, at a time when millions of cannibals do their man-eating work in broad daylight, undisturbed by anyone. On the contrary: the [?] diplomats (printed "di vern") have worked out a plan for a Four-Power Pact in order to secure world peace — and as a partner they take in the bloody robber-ataman Hitler. A fine peace that will be, needless to say. It would truly be a comedy, were it not so tragic. No jester, no wit [?] at all could have devised a more refined joke than the one played by the "socialist" MacDonald, the first fiddler of the eternal concert. The most shameless prostitute would not have been capable of such baseness.

After all, it is not only a matter of Jews: in Germany, together with the latter, his own [?] comrades are also being exterminated; socialism is being strangled there so cruelly that one does not hear even a death rattle [?].

And where is the German Zola who would hurl his "J'accuse" into his people's face!? Why have the better German intellectuals (for such still exist) suddenly fallen silent, when before their eyes there is taking place not just one single St Bartholomew's Night, but an unceasing St Bartholomew's night and day?

Impossibility! Terror!

That is no excuse. Even prisoners, who find themselves behind the thickest prison walls and under the harshest conditions, can organise a collective cry of protest that is heard outside.

Why are all the better writers, academics and scholars silent when Feuchtwanger's [?] flat is raided and his manuscripts are destroyed, when a man of note [?] with a world reputation such as Professor Zondek — who has undoubtedly saved thousands of Nazis from certain death — is thrown out of the hospital and beaten bloody, when Einstein's home is searched for weapons? How does such vandalism differ from the invasion of the Huns in the grey Middle Ages?

It is highly probable that Spengler's prophecy, "The Decline of the West", is beginning to come true. The signal for it was given by his own people, and who knows whether the Hitleriad will not spread to other countries too, and the decline of Europe begin.

Should the Hitlerite plague spread over the whole European organism, it will mean the beginning of the end — that is, the announcement of a flood for which no Noah will manage to build an ark such as the one in which he succeeded in saving the living species. God may have [?] sworn never again to bring a flood of water, but a flood of blood will surely come if the world allows the Hitleriad to expand. Mankind will then drown in its own blood, and a time will come [?] when the word "Europe" will become a symbol of terror and "European" will be a synonym for savagery and cannibalism.

Is Europe still strong and vital enough to put up resistance to the threatening danger, or is she already old and degenerate, and will she let herself be dragged into the Hitlerite devils' dance?

The very near future must give us an answer to that.
A Land-of-Israel Lullaby

[Poetry — Land of Israel; lullaby.]
Leyzer Shikman

Sleep now, my little pioneer,
Sleep now, child, fall asleep quickly!
I must write a letter urgently.
There sails a ship with the morning star.

Our people weeps, weeps there in exile,
Thirsts for every single word,
The word from the one blessed land,
Where Israel is not held to mockery and shame.

There they long to hear more and more;
Our tear is their tear as well,
Our bit of joy — their joy! —
Their burning sorrow — our sorrow!

Quicker, quicker, shut your little eyes,
And I will write a loving greeting
To Grandma and Grandpa there abroad,
From their grandchild, the pioneer-to-be!

I have to write a letter urgently,
There sails a ship with the morning star.
Lyu, lyu, lyu! Close your little eyes!
I have much to write, so much...
What Are We Doing? (A Hasty Note)

[Opinion — Hitler and the boycott of Germany.]
You still think, Reb Jew, that we are up against Hitler like a fly against a lion?
First of all, a lion is indeed afraid of a fly too. You surely remember La Fontaine's fable!
But I have a nicer fable, also from a children's reader.
A rascal ("łobuz") saw a hunchbacked man in the street. So he took a little stone, aimed, and hit him right on the hump. The rascal wanted to "flee" ("va-yivrach"). But the hunchback beckoned him with his finger, called him over and handed him a kopeck, adding: "This you get for being a good shot. More than a kopeck I cannot give you, because I am poor; but there goes a big pot-bellied personage — if you aim right into his pointed belly, he, the rich man, will reward you well."
The boy obeyed and threw the stone; the rich man caught him and broke his bones — on the hunchback's account as well.
The moral is short. Little Israel is the hunchback, Europe the pot-bellied rich man, and Hitler the rascal. We can pay the rascal back only with a boycott, but Hitler will surely not stop there. He will throw a stone at Europe too. And she will settle the account with him for us as well.
Do not forget that the persecution of the Jews is a stick with two ends. After all, he does not persecute for the sake of a good deed, but for a livelihood — to hand the Jewish piece of bread to the blood-pure German. But around the Jewish department stores many German gentiles make their living, and if the Jewish professors are driven out, patients from all over Europe will travel to them wherever they may be, and the hotels will stand empty, and German businesses will lose their livelihood; and if there are no Einstein and Wassermann and Feuchtwanger, the gentile booksellers will also lose thousands.
So the "Yekke" will realise in the end that the whole business of Jew-cleansing is a bad bargain. Instead of profit, it will bring him nothing but loss.
And the 8 million unemployed stand with open mouths and shout: Give bread!...
Then Hitler will have to throw himself onto the external front. As it is written there: "Go and spread out as a troop"...
There is a supposition that in Danzig they are already preparing...
And there he will get his reward.
You ask, Reb Jew: if so, what do w e have to do here?
The answer is that we need only provoke the wild beast, so that it hurls itself right and left.
Our task is to hasten the end.

Pini Baal Lashon. — The Fifth Question... (A post-Passover feuilleton)

[Feuilleton — after Passover; exile and German Jewry.] Pini Baal Lashon.
(A post-Passover feuilleton)

The seders have been held, the Questions asked, the Haggadahs closed and put away for twelve months, until a year from now — may we all live to see it in good health.
And always, when the holiday of Passover comes, I marvel at the author of the Haggadah, who gave us only four Questions. We have no more than that, is that it?
We Jews, a people of nothing but questions, a people whose very private conversations are mostly just questions, and more than that — even its answers are, after all, almost questions too.
Here we ask a Jew we know:
— How are you doing, Reb Jew?
— What should I be doing?
We ask him further:
— How is business?
— How should it be?
And so on. We ask questions and we answer with questions, always...
In such a people, for whom questions are always so characteristic all year round, one is to ask no more than four questions?
And secondly, we are given the reason that one may say and ask only at the time when “matzah and maror” lie before us.
But that is an even bigger question: when are we ever short of maror? On the contrary, let us look over all the “seders” and “orders” [ordnungen — regimes] that are made whenever and wherever — will they ever fail to serve us “maror”?..
Take me, for instance: I would feel strong enough to ask and ask, but I would be content with just one question — the Fifth Question!
I would start precisely with the old, official [“skarbove”, from Polish skarbowy] formula.
I would start plainly and simply, the way we learned in cheder:
— Daddy, Father in heaven, I will ask you the Fifth Question! Why is this night of our last exile so different from all the other nights of the earlier exiles?
After all, we are no longer “beginners” in the matter of exile. Thank God, we have already tasted plenty of [?] dark and bitter exiles since we became a people among the nations.
And always we knew in advance how many years we would have to blacken and be laid waste there: for the Egyptian exile four hundred years were fixed. True, four hundred years of exile is no easy thing either, but still, when one knows the end in advance, it is easier to suffer! Then the Babylonian exile lasted some seventy years too — a mere trifle! Why, then, is this last exile longer than all of them?
And I would like to know, what do you mean to accomplish by it, Daddy, Father? If you are waiting for us to get better, I can vouch to you that the longer you keep us in exile, the worse we shall get.
Just take a look at your world. Wherever your little Jews were scattered, you will see what has become of them.
In Italy, for example, Jews have quite forgotten who they are; it is hard to find a Jew there any more.
In France, were it not for the newly arrived Jews, it would have been the same as in Italy.
In Germany — have you had your fine joy? The Hitlerites are preparing wild “surprises” for you there, they are preparing fine gifts for your people...
And if it lasts a little longer, the older ones will pass away and the younger ones will scatter over the world, and nothing will come of them either; they will dissolve like salt [printed “valts”] in water...
And scatter the Jews must, they have no other choice. The Land of Israel is still not ours, because for the Land of Israel one needs huge capital, and the big capital you have pushed into the hands of such Jews as would rather build “temples” and “museums” in ancient Egypt, or colonies in Russian swamps and God knows where — anything but give it for the Land of Israel...
And after all, sweet Father, what do you have against us? I don’t want to speak about your other children, but in truth, are we worse than others, heaven forbid? Believe me, if the same story had happened to another people — if you had driven another nation into exile for so long — there would long since have been no trace of it left in the world.
Who could have endured [doubtful reading] and borne so much burning suffering and stayed alive? Another nation would long ago have ceased to be a nation, “turned over” and done with it — gone, and go look for me... How many nations have indeed perished just like that.
And we, your little Jews, live on and drip along [kapen — barely hanging on], we bow our little heads, the waves pass over us one after another and we swim out again, and thus we hold on with our last strength. We seek various means of rescue, each finds a remedy according to his understanding and conviction: some strengthen religion, others — nationalism, and still others — Yiddishism, but all of them, poor souls, mean well, in order to prolong our existence...
Is it not time already that you put an end to this long, bitter, ugly exile?
And how much is the measure of waiting and how much the measure of punishing? It seems to me that if one whips a child for two thousand years in a row, that is enough, no?...
Yes, this Fifth Question is what I would ask our Father in heaven, nothing more.
In short — our new Haggadah would turn out a masterpiece, upon my life.
But just try to stir, do something, when we grown-ups may not ask!...
— — —
My dear Jews, we ourselves must give the answer to this Fifth Question.
If only we will it, the Almighty will help us.
As Herzl said: if we will it, it will be no legend...
Jews, boycott German goods as long as Hitler torments the Jews in Germany!

Spring.
(Travel talk in the railway carriage).
By Y. Moszkowicz

The train winds its way between damp, black fields; since the region is hilly, it toils, poor thing; the locomotive puffs and groans until one feels bitter pity for it.

Through the open window a stream of fresh, warm air bursts in. It is a bright, sunny day.

The beginning of spring. From the fields, which are already turning green here and there and look as if they had been washed, a light vapour rises; somewhere at the side there is still an orphaned remnant of snow, and it looks[?] — may all our enemies fare so — riddled[?] by the warm sun like a nut and smeared with mud, so that it is, poor thing, more black than white.

Behind horse and plough a little peasant drags himself along. Black, glossy clods of earth rise into the air and fall back again, clearing the way for peasant and iron.

And you envy that little man for being so close a kinsman of these broad, endless fields and hills. A light breeze plays and tousles the hair on his head and tugs at his coat-tails. But he does his own thing: he walks calmly and composedly behind the plough, as if it were not him that is meant. That is how people walk whose ground under their feet is their own, who are sure that the ground is firm and will not slip out from under their feet.

And involuntarily I recall the words of the Polish student who has just left the carriage and who wanted at all costs that I should believe him that he is, God forbid, no antisemite, has no connection whatever with the green-ribbon people [the Polish nationalists, Endeks], and is expressly against anti-Jewish excesses — nothing more; but since we are talking about Jews, it is really regrettable that of all the seventy nations nobody lives so easily (in his language it is called „lekkim kosztem“ [at little cost]) as they, the Jews, that is to say...

The train stopped, and my thoughts were interrupted by a few Jews who entered the carriage with a rush and a clatter. It was just before the holiday [Passover]; people were hurrying home with packs and parcels — sweaty, out of breath, frightened — having very nearly missed the train.

Having taken their seats in the carriage, one Jew groans: — Oh, a bitter exile, it is hard to be a Jew — and looks in my direction with a questioning glance, meaning: do I too have something to say about it.

— Of course I do! Oh, do I ever! Clever people say that there has to be someone on whom to vent one's anger, a scapegoat [kapore-hen] has to be found — so we are it. An understandable thing. That one must have somebody to torment — there is no arguing about that. Torment us, inflict troubles on us as much as your heart desires — it would not bother me, God forbid. What annoys me is only the constant noise around us, and the fact that we are always on everybody's lips; if I want to forget my „pedigree certificate“ for just one minute — they won't let me.

All the others have birth certificates too, but with them they lie tucked away deep in the pocket, and when a Frenchman, an Englishman and the like has to identify himself once in a blue moon, he recalls on that occasion who his father was, his grandfather, etc., and this recollection happens as rarely as a person thinks about his other characteristics — about, let us say, the colour of his hair, his eyes and the like.

The feeling is also almost the same, for what difference does it actually make — Englishman, Frenchman or Pole — as long as one is not a savage cannibal; it is no disgrace and, conversely, no distinction either; one is what one is and gives it no thought at all.

We too would like to think as little as possible about our pedigree, but how can we, when all around us people talk and make a racket about it day in, day out; we are always on the „wokanda“ [the court docket], somebody always has something to say about us.

Clever people say that „at a big inn many dogs bark“; but what comes of it is that my head cannot stand this barking. I would like to run away, if only [bodaj] to close the inn and so be rid of it once and for all — rid of brooding over my pedigree certificate and of wanting at all costs to get to the bottom of whether my being the scapegoat is merely chance, or whether I have really earned it honestly; even more: whether I have not sometimes earned even bigger blows...
We shall tell our children...

We shall tell our children and our children's children.
Remember it yourselves and pass it on to the generations to come:
There is a German people in the world, and the Jews of the world held it in esteem.
And this very people fell upon the Jews and tortured them with gruesome cruelty.
There is a German people in the world, and Jews learned from it and through its culture went out into the wide world.
And this very people went wild and tore Jews to pieces...
There is a German people in the world, and Jews carried the fame of its culture across the whole world.
And this very people hurled itself upon the Jews with savage ferocity.
There is a German people in the world, and Jews from all over the world flocked to its doctors and took cures at its spas, and left behind with it their hard-earned groszy.
And this very people ran amok [?] and let Jewish blood flow in its streets.
There is a German people in the world, and Jews sold its goods, its machines, all over the world and made it rich, made it sated.
And this very people suddenly went wild and began to beat Jews in every corner of its land.
There is a German people in the world, and Jews in its land denied their very selves for its sake: thousands upon thousands tore themselves away from their people entirely; thousands upon thousands became so steeped in its culture that they were partly torn away from their people; thousands upon thousands were torn in two — the greater part of themselves they gave to the German people, and for their own people they left only a scrap, a crumb of themselves.
And this very people, one fine morning, became bloodthirsty and shed innocent Jewish blood.
There is a German people in the world, and the Jewish people did it nothing but good; Jews were the brokers of its culture, the brokers of its civilisation.
Then the unclean blood boiled up [?] in this very people, and its children trampled Jewish bodies underfoot...
*
Remember it yourselves, Jews of the whole world, and hand it down to the generations to come.
Remember that for good you were repaid with evil; remember that for devotion you were repaid with base treachery; remember that for loyalty you were repaid with vile hatred.
Remember, and put up the proper resistance to the mad gang of murderers and robbers in Germany.
Let us feel ourselves a people and show the murderer Hitler that we can wage a fight and that we cannot be led to the slaughter like sheep.
Across the whole world, wherever there are Jews, in every corner of the world, let Jews rise up against their enemies run wild.
May the hand of the murderer and torturer receive a blow, and may its weapon fall from it.
Our weapon does not poison people. Our weapon does not pierce human bodies, our weapon does not cripple people, like the weapon of the "decent" Hitlerites and the clean German nationalists.
Our weapon is a different one.
But it is as dangerous to our adversaries as their poison weapon.
With our weapon we have already defeated many barbaric governments.
And we are strong enough to fight the dog-like Hitlerism — only fight we must, fight for our honourable existence in the world!
Fight today, and tell our children and our children's children what the German people did to us before the eyes of the whole world...

A Queen Who Dies for Her Sins

Tragic story of Queen Mary of Scotland, her loves and political intrigues.
2.
Brief summary of Chapter 1:
Queen Mary of Scotland was crowned after her father's death, when she was about ten months old. At 6 she was betrothed, and at 15 she married the crown prince, son of Henry II and Catherine de' Medici.
Mary's ambitions were great. The proposal of the English Queen Elizabeth to sign the Edinburgh agreement, so that she might have free passage through England — she rejected. Travelling home, she was received at the Scottish port with great honour. The Scottish burghers, who had persuaded themselves that the queen was a dissolute woman, saw before them a youngish, graceful, naive[?] woman, and[?] out of great enthusiasm the Puritan pious folk sang chapters of Psalms in her honour.
Now read on:
When Mary arrived in her residence city and took the helm of the kingdom into her hand, the friends and confidants[?] of Mary's mother were firmly certain that she would call them back to power.
But they were mistaken. As chief advisers Mary named two from the Protestant camp, her half-brother Lord James and William Maitland. Knowing that her sympathies for the Protestants would provoke resentment[?] among the Catholics, the queen issued a proclamation in which she warned the Catholics not to dare make any change whatsoever in the religious status that was established[?] in the land. For herself she was content with being allowed to conduct the Catholic divine service in the private royal chapel, and to prevent possible hostile demonstrations and attacks on the part of the fanatical Protestants, her chief advisers stood on guard at the door of the chapel during Mass, and Mary's other brothers guarded her priests.
When the Puritan noblemen heard this, they were filled with anger and came to the royal palace to make scandals. But when Mary appeared before them in her enchanting figure, they fell silent and calmed down.
All the sympathies that Mary showed the Protestant wing were only outward, for the political aims; inwardly, however, she remained a faithful Catholic; in Mary burned a Catholic heart. She therefore sent for the reformer of the Protestant faith, John Knox, with whom she had a conversation face to face.
— How now — Mary said to him — how did you dare persuade the people to accept another faith and not the faith that their rulers hold?
To this Knox answered her that this was no proof; the true faith — he said — does not come from the rulers, but from God alone.
— And the people may set themselves against their rulers? — Mary asked angrily.
— Yes, my sovereign[?]! — Knox answered — yes, if the rulers overstep their bounds, one must stand up against them and not stop short of the most far-reaching consequences. Even deposing them, too.
The conversation took on a sharp character, and Knox allowed himself to call the Catholic Church "the whore of Rome."
Some years after the wedding Mary's husband, who was the sickliest of Henry's children, died. From all sides people began[?] to propose matches to the charming Mary. Among others she was offered as husband the Spanish heir to the throne, Carlos.
The match pleased Mary; she wanted to become the wife of the Spanish heir to the throne in order to be able to realise her great ambitions.
Into this match the reformer Knox interfered; he saw in the match a danger to Protestantism and began to work so that the match would not be carried out.
When Mary learned that Knox was the one hindering the match from being realised, she sent for Knox and asked him in great anger:
— What have you to do with my marriage, and why are you in this country at all?
— A subject am I; in this country I was born — Knox answered calmly.
Of the match with the Spanish heir Don Carlos nothing came in the end — not because of intrigues, but Mary herself later did not want the match, because the bridegroom-candidate was by nature very wild. The older he grew, the more his wildness intensified. The wildness came from the fact that his brain had been damaged by a fall, and this affected his way of life. He had a terrible appetite, he was never sated, he gorged without measure and it was always too little. Besides this he displayed various wild deeds, so that even his own father, King Philip, trembled before him.
From all sides matches were proposed to Mary — even her rival, Queen Elizabeth, who herself ought to have married, wanted to match her with her own lover, Lord Radley [sic, = Dudley]. This dandified lord had removed his wife from the way, so as to be able to marry Elizabeth, and in the end Elizabeth wanted to hand him over to her rival Mary...
Meanwhile the Chastelard affair took place.

Let Us Leave the Street Outside.
Jews who go to the theatre may read this.

[Theatre — culture; article.] A Polish newspaper has raised the question: why have we no respect for the theatre? Why do we walk inside in our overcoats, galoshes, hats, and even with a walking stick or an umbrella in hand?
Just as if it were not a theatre but a market. Or a Luna Park.
That newspaper, of course, means the Polish public at Polish performances. Let us then try to recall what the Jewish audience looks like at Jewish performances.
The Jewish theatre has bad traditions. At the moment of its rise the stage did not create around itself any aura of respect and reverence.
A Jew knew that when he came to a Polish theatre he had to behave like a decent person, throw off [?] his outer garments and enter as into a salon. Consequently he had to dress decently already at home, in front of the mirror, so as to look respectable. For the Jewish theatre no preparations were needed, except perhaps to get a few sunflower seeds [semechki] ready in one's pocket...
Times have changed. The Jewish theatre began to cleanse itself, to rise culturally. The human material of the actors themselves also became different, and respect for the theatre also began to grow.
But the theatre did not stay at that height for long; it began to sink again, and respect fell again.
And so in those 50 years the Jewish theatre has not managed to create around itself the atmosphere of a temple of art.
The first demand in a theatre, the most elementary and most human, is that there be quiet during the acting, that the actor be listened to. True, the audience is often activated by applause, or even by the contact which the actor wants to create artificially when he makes the audience sing an easy refrain along with him; but the audience must be cultured enough to understand that all this is only to stir enthusiasm, and that the next moment, when the storm and the [uproar?] are over, one must sit quietly again, concentrated on what is taking place on the stage.
This level we have almost reached already.
Today we have serious actors who know measure and tact, and who consequently influence the audience in the same direction.
In our theatre one can sit through a performance and enjoy it.
But the audience must know when to come! The posters do indeed state the minute of the start — but are people punctual?
In this particular our present-day theatre is not a great sinner. True, it starts a whole hour later, not at 9 but actually at 10, and the reason is understandable: while the Polish audience consists mostly of civil servants, who live normally, work and rest by the hour, by the minute, the Jewish theatregoers are mostly shopkeepers, or simply overworked people who often forget to glance at the clock. But at the announced hour the stage is punctual; the curtain rises almost exactly at the announced time.
Why then is the audience not punctual? Why does everyone gather precisely at the last minute and push into the hall when it is already dark, so that each has to crawl over the other's feet?
And moreover: even during the interval [entr'acte], when everyone is already in place, no signals help. The audience is too lazy to go back in, and at the start of every act at least one scene must be lost. That, surely, is the fault of the audience's lack of upbringing.
Nobody cracks sunflower seeds among us any more, but people still snatch a quiet chat; in the gallery it even sometimes happens that people trade gutter phrases and wild shouts — this must certainly, certainly be rooted out.
And here is an ugly disease that has fastened onto the Jewish theatre in particular.
At a Polish performance everyone knows his seat, and the ushers have no need to keep order in the hall. But when the play is in Yiddish, hardly anyone knows where he is supposed to sit, and when the stage is already lit and the hall dark, only then does a commotion begin in the hall: ushers run around, lead people out of their seats, a veritable migration of nations is under way, people with corns grit their teeth — and what is happening on the stage nobody knows any more.
And now comes the very main point: people bring the street into the auditorium. They sit "with staff and knapsack", as in a bus.
In short, we have already been privileged to have a quite fine theatre; the actors work honestly and give art according to their strength. Let us then show respect for this theatre, respect for ourselves; let us behave as befits a temple of art. Let us leave the street outside, the outer garments in the cloakroom [szatnia], and inside let us be able to immerse ourselves in the pure atmosphere of art.
Ch. N. N. [?]
She Got Her Way...

[Sosnowiec — satirical feuilleton; Passover.] (From the homely Zaglembie [Zagłębie] tales)

As Passover drew near and everywhere people were already toiling and getting ready for the holiday, our Madame M. of Sosnowiec would not lift a finger for anything. She dug in her heels: she would not make Passover anymore now[?]. She would not allow any Seders to be held. "It isn't proper," she gave her husband to understand, for her intelligence and her "postępowość" [progressiveness] to busy herself with such "zabobony" [superstitions]; she no longer wants to know the Jewish customs. Enough that she has been a fool up to now, and she wants no more of it.

The husband of our Madame, Mr. Sh., was left standing as if thunderstruck[?]: Ha, what is this? What does it mean, not to make Passover and not to hold any Seders? What on earth has happened to his so-and-so, who herself is no great educated lady at all, can barely read through a newspaper, a quite simple Jewish woman, who by origin comes from a small shtetl — and here, all of a sudden, such an intellectual has sprung up, who has even dared to go on strike against the Haggadah and the kneidlach.

Mr. Sh. thanks God if he manages to earn enough for the holiday: he roams the street with his little cane, wheels and deals, moves heaven and earth, works his head like a motor — and she, our Madame, knows nothing of all this. She leads a fine life, lives[?] richly, dresses in the finest, has a "szlachetne[?] pochodzenie" [noble descent] — now what more does she want? Why can't she let her husband enjoy Passover, why should she hinder him in his Jewish traditions?

Mr. Sh. shrugged his shoulders and could not get to the bottom of what his little wife was after with her anti-Passover demonstration. It annoyed him greatly, but still he hoped that she would not be so wicked, that she would yet think better of it. Anyway, he hit upon a device: he would win her over with a hundred [złoty note] for a new dress. He believed that all she wanted was more, and that this alone was what her "postępowość" consisted of. True, it is indeed so that lately she has gone completely off the straight path: she holds with no Jewishness, sits constantly at Przybyszewski's[?], dances at all the dancings, and has countless admirers, whom she invites home and treats to good suppers. He knows all that, but that she should renounce Passover — that he had not believed; that she would already have gone so far, he had not imagined.

So Mr. Sh. plucked up courage, and right on the eve of the holiday he laid a real hundred on the table before her and thought he was done. But it doesn't even begin; "What do you think," she took a higher tone, "that you'll buy me off with pennies? No. That won't work. Right after Passover I must go to a spa, and afterwards to a dacha. If you want me to make Passover and you to be able to hold the Seders, you must grant me that. For myself I need no Passover and no Seder; I can manage without all those ceremonies. You know very well that I am one of today's modern women. If I make Passover, I do it only for you, and I don't want to be your servant."

Mr. Sh. begged his little wife for mercy, gave her to understand that times are hard now and that even he feels the crisis, and that it is hard for him to earn even a single gulden [złoty] — but all this was of no help at all. Madame M. would not even listen; once she had dug in her heels, it was a lost cause. Mr. Sh. knew it, and he had to swear an oath (on his bare word she would not believe him) that immediately, right after Passover, she would definitely go to the spa and the dacha. And Madame M. made Passover — may it be said of all Jewish children — and the Seders were held with great pomp.

P. Polier.
Important News for Radio Subscribers

[Radio.] Be careful with the aerial during a storm!
Spring and summer are rich in storms and thunderstorms. When a rainstorm approaches, the Raszyn radio station has to stop broadcasting and earth its aerial, so that the electric charges in the air can flow off freely to the ground.
A thunderbolt is an electric charge that is located in the clouds. This electric charge constantly seeks the shortest way to unite with the earth. That is the reason why lightning usually strikes objects that stick up high above their surroundings, as for instance trees, houses, towers, etc. Lightning also strikes radio aerials, if the latter are n o t connected to the earth.
What do the statistics say?
Several lightning strikes that have hit aerials in recent years caused a panic among many radio listeners, and they regard the aerial as a thing that necessarily causes lightning to strike their house. This opinion is absolutely wrong, because, as the statistics have established, out of 100 lightning strikes that hit various objects there were only 4 cases in which lightning struck aerials — aerials that were not connected to the earth. On the other hand, not a single case has occurred of lightning entering an aerial that is properly connected to the earth.
Besides this, one must take care that the wire leading to the "earth" is in order, i.e. it must not be worn through and must have the necessary thickness; in any case the wire to the "earth" may[?] not be thinner than the wire of the aerial on the roof.
The role of the aerial switch.
Between the earthing and the radio set there must be an aerial switch, so that one can at any time disconnect the aerial and connect it to the earth.
This aerial switch must always be kept clean and in order. All contacts and screws must be firmly screwed tight. At the place where the aerial passes through [through] the window it must be insulated in a rubber tube.
If we observe all these rules and check from time to time whether the "aerial" and the "earth" are in order, one can be sure and calm that lightning will not enter our home.
The main thing, however, is to remember the announcer's saying: "Before going to sleep, disconnect the aerial"...
—
The radio licence fee is not being raised.
In several newspapers a report appeared that the radio fee would be raised by 30 groszy from 1 April.
As it turns out, these reports arose from a misunderstanding. As is known, 10 per cent for the benefit of the unemployed is added to the monthly radio fee. This supplementary fee was levied on the basis of a decree of the Ministry of Posts which expired on 31 March of this year. Now the Minister of Posts has again extended this decree for one year.
So the radio fee remains as it was — 3.30 zł. a month.
—
Television and fashion.
The big English fashion houses already intend [printed "bre'ah", misprint for "bede'ah"] to make use of the achievements in the field of television and to begin sending pictures of the models to their regular customers by means of television.
The president of the English Fashion Chamber, Simon Halm[?], announces that very soon it will be possible, with the help of television sets, to hold fashion shows simultaneously all over the world.
The ladies of South America, who until now, poor things, have lagged behind in fashion, are already waiting for this news with impatience.
—
The radio programme and the listeners.
It is clear and self-evident that it is an impossible thing to compose the radio programme so that it pleases everyone without exception.
It is enough to attend a theatre performance to convince oneself that almost every theatre-goer leaves the theatre with a different opinion. One must remember that a theatre play is a uniform, self-contained thing lasting about two hours, whereas the radio programme lasts 10–12 hours and consists of many different broadcasts. It is therefore no wonder that the broad masses of radio listeners take a more or less critical attitude to the radio programme.
The urban radio listener is not satisfied when he has to listen to a lecture on agriculture, or when folk music is played. In doing so the urban radio listener forgets that in an hour or so he will hear things that interest him most.
The main reason for the dissatisfaction of radio listeners lies in the fact that every radio listener would like, at every moment when he switches on the loudspeaker, to hear played what he likes.
In general, however, one must state that the majority of radio listeners have already understood the enormous difficulties with which the radio management has to struggle in composing a radio programme that must simultaneously satisfy both the inhabitant of a peasant cottage and the inhabitant of a palace.
One cannot treat the radio as one treats a theatre or cinema performance. The radio programme lasts much longer than in the theatre. It hardly ever happens that one goes to the theatre without first finding out what is being played there.
Unfortunately, a bad habit has taken root with the radio — to go up to the set without first taking an interest in the programme. That is indeed the reason for the frequent disappointments.
—
A Soviet giant in the ether.
For several days the first trials of the new radio station "Komintern" have been under way in Moscow; it is to work with the fantastic power of 500 kilowatts (the Polish radio station at Raszyn works with 160 kilowatts).
Because of its close neighbourhood in the ether to the Raszyn radio station, the danger arose that the Moscow radio station would drown out the Warsaw one, and all of Europe would hear on valve sets[?] only Moscow instead of Poland.
Fortunately it turned out that the Moscow danger is no danger at all. For reasons not understood so far, the reception of this station is [very?] weak, even much weaker than that of the central German radio station "Königs Wusterhausen", which works with a power of only 75 kilowatts altogether. One must therefore assume that the Moscow radio station does not use such a giant power at all as was announced by them to the world.
Będzin — Conscription of the 1912 Year-Class.

[Będzin — military conscription.] Announcements by the Magistrat (town council) state that on the 2nd of May the pobór (conscription muster) of the young men born in the year 1912 begins.
In Będzin the conscription will last from the 2nd of May to the 12th of May.
In Dąbrowa — from the 30th of May to the 6th of June.
In Sosnowiec — from the 3rd to the 28th of June.
Those who were classified in category "B" must also present themselves at this muster.
The voivode's announcements regarding the conscription also state that the men of the year-classes 1912 to 1883 (inclusive) who acquired Polish citizenship from the time Poland became independent must present themselves.
The Magistrat asks us to point out that the conscripts must bring with them a document furnished with a photograph; without it a conscript will not be accepted by the conscription commission.
The Monument on Third of May Square Will Be Unveiled on the 11th of June.

[Będzin — municipal and state events.] A meeting took place under the chairmanship of the Starosta (district governor), Mr. Baksa[?], at which the question of finally fixing the date for unveiling the monument on Third of May Square in Będzin was considered.
The unveiling was to have taken place on the Third of May, but for technical reasons the unveiling will take place on the 11th of June of this year.
A committee was elected, which is to organise a series of festivities in honour of the holiday of the unveiling of the monument.
The Penalty on Shochet Weizman Annulled.

[Będzin — ritual slaughter and the courts.] A few weeks ago the shochet (ritual slaughterer) Yechezkel[?] Weizman was punished by the starostwo (district office) with one day's arrest, on the basis of a letter from a certain party, which complained that Mr. Weizman was causing damage to the gmina (Jewish community).
Mr. W. appealed against the sentence, and this week the case came before the Sosnowiec District Court. After the speech of Advocate Dr. Rechtman, the court annulled the sentence of the Starosta.
Which Budget Will Be Valid — the Council's or the Board's.

[Będzin — kehilla and budget.] On Saturday night a meeting of the kehilla board took place, which considered the Starosta's demand that the gmina (community) inform him of the changes regarding shechita (ritual slaughter) and other items that had been made in the budget of the council.
A heated discussion developed about this. The Agudah dozór members[?] (board members) declared that, "in order that the Starosta be informed", he should be sent the budget of the board. Dozór member[?] Mr. Liwer[?] came out sharply against this, relying on an earlier resolution that the board's budget should not be sent, but only the council's budget.
In the end no resolution was adopted on this, and it will be considered at a further meeting.
The Conduct of the Shochtim — Handed Over to the Starosta.

[Będzin — kehilla and shechita.] As is known, the shochtim (ritual slaughterers) do not wait until the gmina (community) pays them their fees, but take the slaughter money for themselves straight away at the slaughterhouse. The gmina, and also the rabbinate, have called on the shochtim to stop this practice, but the shochtim will not hear of it and take the income from the shechita for themselves.
The question was dealt with at a meeting of the board, which resolved to hand over the conduct of the shochtim to the Starosta.
Starosta Demands the Shochtim Return the Income-Money from Shechita.

[Będzin — kehilla and shechita.] On Wednesday a delegation of the gmina (community) conferred with the Starosta about the practice of the local shochtim, who take the slaughter money for themselves at the slaughterhouse without the permission of the gmina.
To this the Starosta declared that the shochtim will at once be called upon to return the money they have taken from the shechita. If they do not carry out the order, they will be punished with a fine and possibly also handed over to the prosecutor's office.
Meeting of the Commissarial Council.

[Będzin — municipality and budget.] At Thursday's meeting the budget for 1933/34 was again on the agenda. The budget, which was altered in the voivodeship office, amounts, together with the extraordinary budget, to a sum of 1 million 670 thousand złoty.
A series of statutes was approved at the meeting. The tax statute on entertainments was reduced by 30 per cent.
A Jubilee Committee Formed.

[Będzin — Zionism.]
In the premises of the “Mizrachi” a meeting took place with the purpose of creating in Będzin a united jubilee committee. Represented were: on behalf of the Zionists, the comrades Wygodzki and Liwer; “Mizrachi” — Petal[?] and Silberberg; the left groupings — Kołoszski[?] and Aryeh Liwer; the Revisionists — Langnaus and Jaskrowicz.
After a lengthy discussion the committee was constituted: A. Liwer was elected chairman and treasurer, secretary — Mendel, and assistant secretary — Langnaus; one more seat for an assistant secretary was reserved for the left bloc, which made a declaration that they do not accept the office.
The Courses of the League for Defence against Air-Gas Have Ended.

[Będzin — air defence.]
On the initiative of the local committee of the L.O.P.P. [Liga Obrony Powietrznej i Przeciwgazowej — Air and Anti-Gas Defence League], courses were organised for tramway workers and for the workers of the Polish zinc works. The courses, in which 80 men took part, were conducted by the instructor of the municipal committee and by members of the O.P.G. instructors' circle in Będzin.
The courses for the workers of the Polish zinc works took place in the premises of Public School No. 1, with the permission of the school inspector and of the Będzin magistrate (municipality), who allowed, free of charge, the use of the electric light as well.
How the Jewish Soldiers Were “Provided” with Food for Passover.

[Będzin — Jewish soldiers.]
Messrs. J. Glicksman, M. Alter and L. Melach, former Jewish soldiers, report to us the following:
On the initiative of a group of Jewish reservists a committee was founded to provide the Jewish soldiers with food for Passover. Unfortunately, little was done on the part of the kehilla administrators[?] so that the Jewish soldiers might spend the festival days in a fitting manner and in a homelike environment. In particular, the Jewish soldiers in Żary were left abandoned and had to eat leavened food (chametz) on Passover. Only on the second day of Passover was an intervention made about this with the Będzin rabbi, who sent them matzot and eggs.

Sosnowiec
A Festive “Eretz-Israel” Seder in Sosnowiec.

[Sosnowiec — pioneers.]
On the second night of Passover a festive “Eretz-Israel Seder” took place in the “Angielska” hall, arranged by the organising committee at the “Mizrachi” in Sosnowiec, for 70 halutzim and halutzot (pioneer men and women) who are here in the hachshara (training) kibbutzim of HeHalutz HaMizrachi and of Gordonia. The hall was splendidly decorated with blue-and-white ribbons and various inscriptions. Before a packed hall of the most prominent persons of the town, with the participation of M. A.[?] Hager, the [up to?] 70 pioneers, men and women, march into the hall and take their designated places at beautifully laid tables. Amid the greatest suspense of the assembled, the seder is opened by Mr. Shimon Blum (chairman of the Torah va-Avodah movement in Sosnowiec).
After the whole audience sings “HaTikvah”, the seder is continued by Mr. Shabtai Jungster. The special choir of HeHalutz HaMizrachi performs the Four Questions in song, and then the floor is given to Rabbi Hager, who delivers a very witty lecture on the Festival of Freedom. With this the official part is closed. In a very elevated mood, with singing and Eretz-Israel horas, the seder ended at about 3 o'clock at night. During the whole time of the seder the street around the hall was besieged by people listening to the joyful melodies and the Eretz-Israel dances.

A Terrible Gas Outburst at the “Renard” Mine.
14 Workers Poisoned.

[Sosnowiec — mines.]
On Tuesday at half past ten in the morning a rumour spread that in the depths of the “Renard” coal mine several dozen workers had been poisoned by gas.
The news caused an enormous panic, and in front of the mine the families gathered, wanting to learn the fate of their near ones.
As it turned out, a gas outburst had occurred in the mine, but fortunately it was still possible, with the help of rubber masks, to rescue 14 unconscious workers.
After they were given quick aid, some were taken to the outpatient clinic (ambulatorium) and some home.
A Brawl in the “Warszawianka” Confectionery.

[Sosnowiec — antisemitism.]
In the “Warszawianka” confectionery (café) a brawl broke out between Polish students and Jewish young men, from among the “Łapaczes”[?].
The resistance of the Jewish young men greatly enraged the gentlemen of the Endek (National Democratic) organ. Also, several lawyers of that camp have declared themselves ready to conduct the trial.
4 More Performances by the Great Artist-Actor Baratow in Będzin and Sosnowiec.

[Będzin, Sosnowiec — theatre.]
Owing to the great success that Dr. Baratow and his ensemble had in Będzin, 4 more performances will be given: Monday the 24th and Thursday the 27th in Będzin; Tuesday and Wednesday in Sosnowiec.
To be performed are “The Father”, with Dr. Baratow in the leading role, and, for the first time in Zagłębie, “The Bourgeois”.
The performances take place in Będzin at the “Światowid”, in Sosnowiec at the “Pałac”.
Dąbrowa

"Kimcha" campaign at the Jewish kehilla.
Thanks to the initiative of the kehilla presidium, a "Kimcha" [kimcha de-Pischa, Passover flour relief] campaign was carried out this year for the first time. About 1,700 zł. were collected, which were distributed to respectable [?] needy persons.
—o—
Fight against illegal slaughter.
The starosta, through the gmina [municipality], ordered the shochet Wolf Krakauer of Gołonóg not to engage in illegal ritual slaughter. For violating the order the shochet's slaughtering knives will be confiscated and he will be punished with a fine.
—o—
The Jewish kehilla takes leave of the president.
At the farewell session of the president [mayor] of Dąbrowa, Dr. Marejski [?], a farewell letter was read in the name of the Jewish kehilla, expressing thanks to the president for his tolerant attitude toward the Jewish citizens.
At the reception (raout) too the kehilla was represented by its chairman Mr. Gejfeld, vice-chairman Mr. Rechnic and board member Mr. Birnbaum.
—o—
Kehilla employees dismissed.
The kehilla collector and the beadle (shammes) of the synagogue (both Krimilov (Kromołów) Hasidim) have been given notice of dismissal from their posts.
As we are informed, the dismissal is a result of the fact that some [?] parnassim, Krimilov Hasidim, complained to the starosta that "there is no order in the Dąbrowa community."
The "disorder" in the kehilla consists in this, that the majority of the board is against the moreh-tzedek whom the Krimilov "tzadi[k]" wants to bestow [?] upon Dąbrowa...
—o—
A scandal in the synagogue.
Last Shabbat HaGadol the rabbi did not come to the synagogue to deliver the traditional sermon but sent his son-in-law. Some of the worshippers, realizing that the sermon of the rabbi's son-in-law was connected with the "vacant" post of a moreh-tzedek for Dąbrowa, disrupted the sermon, and as a result a scandal broke out in the synagogue.
The kehilla board has handed the guilty parties over to the courts.
—o—
A bandit attack in Gołonóg.
In Gołonóg bandits with knives attacked the passing traveller Wojtasiński [?] of Sosnowiec, whom the bandits severely wounded with a knife.
Zawiercie

Revisionist circle.
On the initiative of Mr. Pinchas Zylbersztajn a Revisionist circle named after Ze'ev Jabotinsky has been formed. Members were elected to the provisional committee, which the following persons joined: Pinchas Zylbersztajn, Grynblat, Chmielnicki and Kajzer [?].
—o—
62 "Yes" — 4 "No".
The plebiscite proclaimed by Ze'ev Jabotinsky for the 16th of this month was held in the premises of the Revisionists. There were 4 "No" voters; all the rest were "Yes" voters only.
—o—
"Masada".
A school-youth organisation "Masada" has been founded in our town; its task will be to draw in broader strata of the assimilated youth, which attends mainly the Polish gymnasia.
—o—
Urgent aid.
Thanks to the initiative of the school principal Mr. Lejzerowicz and Dr. Melcer, members of the Social Welfare [Opieka Społeczna], urgent Passover aid was given to poor children up to 14 years of age. The campaign consisted of 1 kilo of matzah and 1 kilo of sugar. 230 kilos of matzah and the same number of kilos of sugar were distributed.
Six million złoty fine.

The Upper Silesian inspectorate has discovered a series[?] of abuses committed in the enterprises of Graf von Pless (the Prince of Pless), as a result of which the state treasury suffered a loss of about 260 thousand zł.
The tax office has therefore imposed a fine of six million zł.

On Sienkiewicza Street in Bobrowniki, 3-year-old Bienański was run over by a cart. The child was trampled[?] to death on the spot.

From the sports world.

"Sarmacja" – "Hakoach" 1:1.
This championship match of Class "A" between the two local clubs, which aroused great interest, ended in a draw after a fairly interesting and ambitious struggle. "Hakoach" played disastrously in this match — not a single thought-out move. We saw no combination play whatsoever among the players. It was surprising to note that the "Hakoach" team is poorly prepared for the current championships.
"Sarmacja" kicks off and immediately sets a strong pace, holding a slight advantage in the first half. During this time the "Hakoach" defence had a great deal[?] of work. In the 35th minute "Sarmacja", through the fault of the defence, scores the first goal. The Hakoach men put more effort into the work. In the 40th minute, for a foul in the penalty area, the referee awards an eleven-metre kick (penalty) to "Hakoach"; Gutman shoots it and... 1:1.
After the half-time "Hakoach" was very weak. The half-back line barely keeps up the pace and "Sarmacja" has a slight advantage all the time. Referee Dulas — good. The best man on the field was Nunberg in goal, who saved the team from certain defeat.
"Gwiazda" – "Kraft" 4:2.
The friendly match between the above-mentioned two clubs ended in a sure victory for "Kraft" with a score of 4:2. The goals for "Kraft" were scored by Wekselman, Rapaport and Rozenberg; for "Gwiazda" by Tuchszneider and Wajgrib.
"Hakoach" – "Maccabi" 4:3.
A ping-pong match took place in the "Hakoach" club rooms, which ended in a defeat for the Hakoach players. The points for "Maccabi" were won by Bukes, Nazarski, Dafner, Brandes; for "Hakoach" — Rubinlicht, Urbach and Gutman.
"Hakoach" – 23 P.A.L. [23rd Light Artillery Regiment] 0:1.
Despite the victory that "Hakoach" gained in this match, it again displayed weak play. The players of "Hakoach" must know that if they want to save the prestige of Jewish sport and to come out of the further championship matches with honour, they must absolutely take up training seriously. It would be advisable for the management of "Hakoach" to bring in a coach for the team.
In the first half the military men had a slight advantage, but thanks to Nunberg in goal they did not manage to score a single goal. In the 35th minute Motl Rozen scores the only goal of the day.
In the second half the game is already more even and "Hakoach" attacks more often, but the forwards can by no means bring themselves to take a shot at the opponents' goal, and so the result of the match remains unchanged.
Referee Plesner — good.
"Hakoach" – "Maccabi" 1:2.
The traditional holiday match between these two clubs did not this time attract as large a public as in the past; this is perhaps because the two strongest Jewish clubs of Zagłębie can please nobody today with their style of play. Both teams play much weaker today than before. The atmosphere on the field is now somewhat calmer. But the "Locarno" spirit still does not reign among the players. And if the players would show as much fighting spirit and play with as much ambition in the championship matches against the Polish teams, the results of the championship matches would be much more favourable for them. Both teams have strong points in their goalkeepers. Both Hirsz and Nunberg are in a class of their own. To the eye Hirsz makes a better impression with his leaps and dives, but tactically Nunberg is much better.
"Hakoach" kicks off and immediately leads an attack on the left wing, and within the first 3 minutes, from a corner[?] taken by Jankielewicz, "Hakoach" scores the first goal. "Hakoach" is constantly on the offensive; in a collision Jankielewicz is injured and leaves the field. "Hakoach" plays with 10 men, yet attacks constantly. In the 25th minute Motl Rozen scores the second goal with a splendid header. In Jankielewicz's place Berl Sziwek appears on the field. 5 minutes before half-time Safer breaks through the defence and scores the only goal for "Maccabi".
After the half-time "Hakoach" has a strong advantage throughout, but the forwards do not exploit many favourable moments, and with a strong advantage of "Hakoach" the match ends — a match that toward the end was played somewhat brutally.
A. Wrocławski.

Legal Answers

[Law — legal answers to readers.]
Mr. A. S—n. — The payment order (nakaz zapłaty) can serve as security for your claim, i.e. you can have a provisional attachment (tymczasowe zajęcie) made on the debtor.
Your claim is not time-barred, because the bill of exchange is valid against the drawer for 3 years.
Mr. “Dąbrowa reader” [Dąbrowa Górnicza]. — We have already written about this: in civil matters one must, within 7 days of the judgment, file with the court a written request for the judgment to be reasoned; you then receive the reasoned judgment by post, and from the moment you have received the judgment you may appeal within 2 weeks. If you did not request the judgment, you have lost the right to appeal.
Mr. X. — Your debt does not fall under the moratorium, because it is a commercial debt which you secured on the mortgage.
The moratorium covers debts which, by agreement, were entered in the mortgage registers.
Mr. “Tenant” (Lokator). — We have touched on the question of the water charge from the legal standpoint; on the basis of the existing laws we regard the question of relations between landlord and tenant as an individual matter: thus, for example, if you rented a flat with water and all conveniences only a few years ago, you can demand that the water charge be borne by the landlord; this will be easy to carry out when the charge is collected from the house-owners.
Mr. “Manager”. — As manager of the enterprise you have no right to demand pay for overtime.
The matter has already been clarified several times by the Supreme Court.
Mr. Sh. G. — The judgment, being a judgment by default (zaoczny), will be served on you officially, and then you will be able within 2 weeks to file an objection (sprzeciw) and to demand that the case be heard once more.
R. R.

Elections to the Będzin City Council
will take place in October (październik), or only in May 1934.
We are informed from an authoritative source that talk of city-council elections is still premature. In the best case the elections will take place in the month of October; if not at that date, the elections will become topical only in May 1934...

Wages of the Tram Employees Cut
The Zagłębie tram directorate has decided to reduce the wages of the tram employees by 6 percent.
The reduction applies from next month on.

„Italian“ [sit-down] Strike at the „Juliusz“ Coal Mine in Kazimierz [Kazimierz Górniczy].
400 workers are in the depths of the mine.
At the „Juliusz“ mine in Kazimierz an „Italian“ strike broke out on Monday, because the directorate imposed a three-month leave.
The first-shift workers, 400 men, went down into the mine, but they threw down their work, demanding that the directorate withdraw its decision.
On Monday a conference took place at the labour inspector in Sosnowiec with the participation of workers' delegates and representatives of the directorate.
The conference produced no result whatsoever. The representatives of the mine declared that the decision can in no way be changed.

Old Bill-of-Exchange Forms Valid until 1 May.
As is known, from 1 May the old type of bill-of-exchange forms is withdrawn. For issuing a bill after 1 May on an old form, a fine of 25 times the price of the form is threatened. Merchants who have old forms lying about can exchange them at the tax office.

Caught at the Critical Minute.
The flat of Mr. Dimant on Potocki Street in Będzin was broken into, and the thieves wanted to get down to „work“. But at the critical minute they were disturbed. 2 managed to escape; one fell into the hands of the police.

Swindles at the Expense of Hungry Unemployed.
A group of swindlers, posing as agents of large firms, recruited workers for public works. There is no shortage of people wanting work nowadays, and from every worker registered for „work“ a certain sum had to be paid, supposedly as a deposit (kaucja).
The fraud, however, was soon discovered and the „agents“ are already in the hands of the police.

At the well-attended meeting a board of 9 persons was elected, which has set about registering all the male and female graduates of this school.

From the Hitlerite Hell.
There arrived in Będzin these days Mr. Avraham Stopnicki with his family, who have been expelled from Germany. Mr. Stopnicki lived for 11 years in Bad Nauheim [printed „Goyheim“], kept a boarding-house (pension) there and lived like everybody else [respectably]. Suddenly he received a notice that he and his family must leave Germany within 8 days. At the set date a group of Nazis came in, sealed Stopnicki's flat of 3 rooms and kitchen, and took the family away to the railway station. Stopnicki's wife, who suffered a nervous attack from the „visit“, was taken to hospital, from where, several days later, she[?] too was expelled from Germany.

The Jews in Germany Are Living Through a Cruel Inquisition!

[Germany — persecution of the Jews; testimony in Sosnowiec.] A conversation with a Sosnowiec Jew who escaped from the German hell.
These days a well-known Jew, who has been living in Berlin for several years already, arrived in Sosnowiec. He gave us horrifying details of what the Jews in Germany are going through.
"First of all," our informant declared, "it must be established that the situation in Germany is much worse than the press reports. What Jews are now going through in Hitler-land is truly indescribable. The pogroms in Russia were a miniature compared with the present hooligan deeds in Germany. People live in unusual fear and panic. The Nazis come into all Jewish homes and search, supposedly, for weapons; when they find none, they drag the Jews off to the party barracks and beat them murderously there."
At 12 at night a gang of wild Hitlerites broke in on a certain Berl Apter, on König-Straße, and beat him till he bled. Then they robbed him of a sizeable sum of money and vanished.
Into the beth-midrash of the Polish Jews at Grenadierstr. 26, 5 armed Nazis came on Tuesday and demanded weapons from the worshippers. No weeping or pleading helped; the barbarians fell upon the worshippers and tore out their beards.
In the Jewish homes there are many wounded and even dead, but one cannot know the number of victims, because every Jew is wary of saying a word even to an acquaintance. The streets are full of the gangs, which run wild undisturbed and do whatever their heart desires. There is no one to turn to for protection. The building of the Polish consulate is teeming with thousands of Jews, Polish citizens, begging for help. Among them one sees hundreds of wounded with bandaged faces.
"In a word," our informant concludes, "the Jews in Germany are living through a terrible and cruel inquisition. World Jewry must raise the loudest outcry against these atrocities; our unfortunate brothers in Germany must be rescued!"
Open Letter to the Board of "HaKoach" in Będzin

[Będzin — letter to the editor; youth and sport.] Esteemed Mr. Editor!
Allow me to print in your esteemed paper the following letter, which touches on a topical and painful[?] question.
In one of the latest issues of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" I read a letter which touched on the new "sport epidemic" of ping-pong among the young generation, among young schoolchildren. Unfortunately this question too has remained, as every time, "a voice crying in the wilderness". None of our parents found it necessary to take further steps to stop the ping-pong game and uproot it from the little ones' camp.
This time, however, I turn to the board of the Będzin "HaKoach", which allows small children to spend whole days at ping-pong in the club premises. Your motto is, after all, "a healthy soul in a healthy body" — so why do you allow the little souls of these small fry to be spoiled so early? Why do you tolerate that children, instead of going to school, go to "HaKoach" to play ping-pong?
I believe, however, that hundreds more parents agree with my words, spoken in the columns of the newspaper, and they demand this of you:
— The ping-pong game at "HaKoach" must stop!
With great respect,
Izydor Lewinski.

In Mokre [?] ("Makrem") the murdered 4-year-old Piorecka [?] was found in a forest. As it later turned out, the child had first been raped and then murdered.

Selling the costliest possessions for 70 marks, just to escape the Hitlerite hell

Last week a certain Mr. W. arrived in Będzin from Berlin, having escaped from the Hitlerite hell.
This week Mr. W. received a letter from his wife, which lists a whole roster of well-known families who have been thrown into German prisons.
The wife also writes that masses of Jewish families are abandoning all their goods and chattels, selling their costly clothes and furniture, just to save themselves and escape as fast as possible from the German Inquisition.

Bloody fight between peasants and a bailiff and the police

At a peasant's in the village of Iwieska [?], near Ząbkowice, a bailiff (sequestrator) wanted to take away a cow for a tax debt.
A group of peasant women gathered on the spot and, sticks in hand, did not let the bailiff take the cow from the peasant.
Because of this the bailiff went off to the nearest police station, and escorted by 3 policemen he came back to carry out the distraint.
Meanwhile the number of those gathered grew larger, since all the peasants of the village took up the cause [?] of their "comrade", and a brawl broke out. In the end the bailiff gave up and did not carry out the distraint.
A terrible act of revenge by a peasant

A peasant from the village of Kąs-ałka [?] near Pilica, on account of his bad material situation, sold his farm (majątek) to a neighbour of his. Unable to bear that his neighbour had bought up the whole property at an auction, he killed him with a stone on the spot.
