Talking Among Ourselves. (A Letter to a Friend).

[Zionism — opinion; assimilation.]
1. First letter.
...You want, dear comrade, to combat me with your arguments that you are right.
— For 30 years now you have argued that we propagate our idea; what means have we not used? Our best energies, our free time we give away to the Zionist idea; a solid part of our income, too, we give away for this purpose. We pay the shekel, we pay to the Keren Kayemet, we pay to the Keren Hayesod. The dunam campaign, the forest campaign, the Golden Book campaign — we give and give, and yet... and yet we are still right at the very beginning.
"Who, then, is to blame for this, if not the rotten[?], sleepy Jewish people, which cannot be awakened from its lethargic sleep even with iron rods[?]"?
And you, you conclude with the following phrase:
— We Zionists have done everything; if the whole Jewish people would follow our example, redemption would have come long ago.
Allow me, dear comrade, to pour a few bitter drops into the cup of your self-satisfaction. The whole thing is a dream: not only the people, but you and I too have not yet done anything at all; not only in achievements are we still at the very beginning, but in our work as well...
In the course of our thirty years of work the idea has reached the brain, partly also the pocket, but the spiritual strings of the heart have hardly been touched. We are the same as before; our way of life has not changed a hair. The thought is Zionist, the soul — assimilated, as with everyone else. Each of us is "one who immerses while holding the unclean creature in his hand", and if it goes on like this, we may lose our banner along the way...
One cannot spread an idea with words alone, however hot, however flaming they may be. The bearer of the idea must embody in himself the deeds which he preaches.
In what, then, truly speaking, do we, the bearers of the idea of redemption, differ from the popular masses sunk in the swamp of assimilation? Just like them we blur our Jewish face, just like them we bathe in the hundred-percent mud of exile; just like them we lick the plates of a foreign culture. Our homes are ruled by foreign languages, foreign content, foreign customs, a foreign way of life. We build the altars, our children gather the kindling and our wives offer up the sacrifices to the idol of assimilation.
And do you know who the sacrifices are?
— The best, the dearest thing a people can possess: the little children.
We educate our children in foreign schools, in foreign languages. And even those who do not do so look, among us, like idlers...
Not only to the people have we not yet found the language, but even to ourselves. True, we are better than others, we donate more than they do. But what sense does it have? For example: the generation of the desert gave both for the Golden Calf and for the Tabernacle, but we give the largest part for the Calf and the most minimal part for the Tabernacle. And even that minimum we give with trembling hands; we give out of shame, we give out of necessity, we give because one cannot lag behind others — but in all these givings the soul takes no part whatever, because it is not in our possession, because it wanders in foreign worlds...
Oh, dear comrade, all your words about the revival of the people, about building our own land, about the renewal of our culture are worth a pinch of snuff as long as you say them only in the street and not at home; as long as you are a Zionist outside and a "gentleman" at home; as long as your wife and your children are strangers not only to your people but even to you yourself.
Shut your mouth, dear comrade, and do not pour salt on the wounds of your people... And if you truly grieve for your people and thirst for its redemption, then bring the small but true sacrifice — nationalize your own home, and do not fear if your assimilated friends, your assimilated surroundings call you an idler.
The misfortune, however, is that you are not capable of bringing such a sacrifice. You are too practical for that; the "career" of your children is too dear to you, and you understand the word career no differently than your assimilated wife, for whose sake you often have to run "from the director to the factor [middleman]".
But what will happen when your own children ask you later... But no! They will not ask you at all, because they will know nothing and will want to know nothing about the great past of their[?] ancient people. They will know nothing about the great culture which was created by generations of giants and destroyed by a generation of dwarfs. They will know nothing about the rivers of holy blood of fathers, of mothers, who were burned at the stake, of holy children who were slaughtered for that very culture which we now throw into the dark cellars together with all the other useless rags — yes, your children will cross the border, will go away to where one no longer returns from.
And what if they do ask something after all? — That will be much worse still. — It may well be that the very people to whom we now sell our children for a pot of lentils will teach them the questions — what shall we answer then?
Yes, dear comrade, the answer to this question must come in good time. We must answer while we are not yet too late.
N. Berman.
Jewish Shepherds in the Land of Israel

[Land of Israel — settlement and agriculture; letter.]
Jeruchem Lewin.
(A letter from the Land of Israel).
In the Bible, the "Song of Songs" — "the song of all songs" — belongs to the shepherds, Shulamit and her beloved. In the life of the Diaspora, sheep-herding was in non-Jewish hands, and in the folk language the term "shepherd" became a synonym for a "coarse fellow". In the Land of Israel Jews come with the desire to take all the "gentile" trades into their own hands, so intelligent pioneers (halutzim) also took an interest in sheep-herding as a branch of work for themselves.
This occupation already has a history. The first were the Galilee colonists, who in many respects took the Arab village as the model for their farming. The colonists, however, on the whole stopped halfway. The sheep did belong to the Jewish owner, but it was the Arab shepherd who looked after them. The first Jewish shepherds emerged among the members of the "HaShomer" organisation. For some of them it was a means to an end. Their interests and tasks were to stand on guard and to find out about everything going on among the neighbours: among the fellahin in the villages and among the Bedouin in the tents. Herding sheep gives the opportunity to meet and talk with fellow shepherds in the hills and around the wells. In this way one can find out about everything that happens in the neighbouring camp.
Others from "HaShomer" regarded it as an end in itself. For them the striving held good — to return to the life of the East. If one wants to strike roots in the soil of the new land, one must adapt to its life. One must free oneself from the Europeanness one brought along from the countries of emigration. It is necessary to learn from the Arabs their customs and manners and to take over their livelihoods. Just as among the Arabs the sheep occupies an important place in economic life in every village and every nomadic tribe, so the immigrant Jews too must give this occupation its proper place in their colonies.
In the most remote corner of the country, in Upper Galilee, where "HaShomer" built a nest for its members — in Kfar Giladi and its surroundings — the Jewish shepherd appeared in Arab dress. There he wandered with his sheep, seeking where to still their hunger and where to quench their thirst. At first it was a matter of romance. If a comrade fell in love with the Eastern way of life, if he longed for the sounds of the idyllic shepherd's pipe, if he wished to make friends with Bedouin and village "free birds" — he took up the shepherd's trade.
In the settlements which the national capital, the "Keren Hayesod" and "Keren Kayemet", created after the War, with their mixed farming, sheep-herding began to become a part of the farm economy. The romantic veil, which had attracted only individuals, was taken off it, and it became accessible to many. In some of the kvutzot of the Jezreel Valley flocks of sheep appeared right from the start (in the moshavim keeping sheep is much harder). Just as Jewish colonisation gave a different face to all branches of the economy, so changes were introduced in this field too. The cattle in the Jewish cowshed cannot be compared to the local "birger"[?] cow. The poultry in the Jewish henhouses is quite different from the birds that roam around the Arab houses. In sheep-breeding, too, new systems and methods have been introduced. Special pens have been built for the sheep. On rainy days they are not forced to stand in the downpour. At a certain time of the year they are fed at home. Right after the grain is cut, the sheep are let out onto the fields, which are thereby manured — an important detail from the economic point of view.
Sheep-raising has lately become important as an economic factor. Through the agricultural producers' cooperative "Tnuva" a market has been created in the towns for the special sheep's cheese. The meat, too, which Ashkenazi Jews indeed do not like to eat, sells well among the Sephardi Jews. In the processing of the cheese it is especially women who find employment, which is important for the balance of the farm economy. The young lambs, too, have lately been sold through "Tnuva". It is worth noting: the farms of "HaShomer HaTzair" have proved to be faithful "hasidim" of sheep-herding. There is not a single settlement of theirs based on mixed farming that has not acquired a flock of sheep.
The shepherds are no longer "coarse fellows" but people who can and want to occupy themselves with the scientific problems of the trade: how to organise feeding rationally, how to treat the animals in case of disease, how to regulate breeding, etc. There exists an association of all sheep-shepherds on a country-wide scale. Once a year they all come together to discuss the questions that have arisen over time. The veterinary doctors also take part with lectures and in the debate. The time is spent merrily, in order to create a compensation for the many lonely hours in which the shepherd finds himself only in the company of his flock. From among the shepherds folk singers have also emerged, who themselves composed the songs and the tunes to them as well. The songs are sung throughout the country, and rarely does anyone know who their author is. Sheep-herding now synthesises[?] within itself economics together with romance.
A “Hitlerite Woman” (A Picture from the Rabbinical Court Room)

[Sketch from life — rabbinical court, divorce, poverty.] (A picture from the rabbinical-court room.)
A little woman with a child on her lap, 2 older children at her side; a little girl and a little boy on one bench at the side of the rabbinical-court room.
Opposite them, a tall man, evidently a porter, with a bandaged finger.
This is a couple who have come to get divorced.
The whole family goes about in rags. The little boy in a little velvet dress, the girl with a holey kerchief on her shoulders. The mother in clothes patch upon patch.
The father of the family sits with his head bowed and is silent; the mother, however, does not rest for a minute.
What is she saying?
— The children I will not give him for any money in the world. Twelve years after our wedding, we have already been 5[?] times at the rabbi's to get divorced. But back then nothing came of it; today it has to come to an end.
He earns no money; yesterday he hit me on the head with his fists [“kilakes” — kułaki?]. I did not keep quiet to him either — I crippled his hand, which is why he now goes about bandaged.
The rabbis ask me for money for the get. The carters [“furmanes”] have collected 5 złoty. And here they still say it is too little — I will not move from here.
The children have not yet had so much as a spoonful of water in their mouths today; today they evicted me from the flat; I have to go and look for somewhere to sleep for a night, and here my husband still drags himself around after me. A get and nothing more.
A get has to cost money. So one of the rabbis advised her to go to the kehilla and ask for money for a get.
But she would not move, and the scribe — with the goose-quill behind his ear, under the big Hasidic hat from which a velvet skullcap peeks out — called her a “Hitlerite woman.”
— Hitler wants to take things by force, — the scribe grew angry. — With us there is no such thing.
What Hitler, which Hitler — the downtrodden woman stares at him.
The youngest child has fallen asleep, and women who came to ask ritual questions about pins [“shpilkes”] and gizzards [“pupik”] began to collect five-groszy coins to buy a piece of bread for the hungry mother with the three children.
Yud Resh [Y. R.].
Important for Small Traders

[Merchants — taxes.]
We are informed by the Small Traders' Association:
The “nakaz” [assessment notice] for the turnover tax for 1932 is now being sent out.
What the slips state: first, how much turnover the shopkeeper made in 1032 [misprint for 1932] (e.g. 20000 guldens [= złoty]); second — how large the tax percentage is and how much one must pay (e.g.: two per cent — 400 zł.); and third — how much one must pay in as advances for the year 1933.
As is known, each of the four advances amounts to 20 per cent of the entire tax assessed for the previous year. If, for example, a tax of 400 guldens was assessed for the previous year, one must pay in the current tax year four advances of 80 guldens each.
And it is precisely with the advances that one must take good care, because this year — from 1 January 1933 on — shopkeepers have to pay not two per cent turnover tax, as hitherto, but only 1 per cent. That is, in fact the advances for the year 1933 should amount not to 20 per cent of the 1932 tax but only to 10% per cent. If, for example, the tax in 1932 amounted to 400 guldens, each advance should now amount not to 80 guldens but only to 40, because the whole tax has altogether been reduced by half.
So when the “nakaz” is brought to you, take a good look at what is written in the place where the advances are entered, because a mistake may sometimes happen too — in that case one must immediately file an appeal (reklamacja).
Heard and Seen.

By Ben Amotz.

"Jestem przyzwyczajona..." ["I am used to it..."]
Into a Jewish drugstore (apteka-skład) in Będzin comes a Jewish "pani" [lady].
— "Proszę puder" [Powder, please] — she says.
The owner of the drugstore hands her domestically made powder.
— "Nie chcę tego" [I don't want this] — she screws up her made-up little face — "ja chcę niemieckiego" [I want German].
— What, don't you know that the whole Jewish world is boycotting German goods! How dare you let such words out of your mouth? We Jews are forbidden to use any blood, and in German goods there is, after all, Jewish blood...
— "Prawda" [True] — she says — "but ja jestem przyzwyczajona do niemieckiego" [I am used to German]..
When the pani had left the shop, the merchant remarked to me that the pani was telling the truth: she is used to German goods, to the German officers.
— "Jestem przyzwyczajona."

"Elech ve-emsor..." ["I shall go and inform" — printed "אלף"]
— God, look at the troubles they make for us, thanks to our own little Jews — with this preamble a dishevelled Jew bursts into the editorial office, holding in his hand the freshly baked
— "nakaz płatniczy" [tax payment order].
— Calm down, why are you so upset, so unnerved?
— You still ask why? Look here, the tax office has informed me that last year my turnover increased by 50 thousand zł. It is simply unbearable — the Jew shouts — everyone knows that this year I was ruined, carried on no trade at all, and here you are:
— a surcharge on the turnover...
— But why do you come to us? We are not to blame for this; we don't assess you.
— I have come to you so that you raise the alarm, not against the tax office, but against our informers.
They, the informers, are destroying the remnant that survives among the Jews; they are a new plague upon the Jewish people. When I was at the tax office to complain about the high and incorrect assessment, I was told clearly and plainly:
"We know that you are not able to pay such podatki [taxes], but proszę pana [my dear sir], what can we do, when your Żydki [little Jews — pejorative] have 'raised [an outcry]' and waged a campaign that you make big turnovers, that you are very rich and that you can pay big taxes"...
Yes, it is sadly a bitter truth that the most shameful libels against Jews originate only with Jews; all information about us in the non-Jewish world is carried there by Jews. Informing has already become an everyday matter: hardly has one man some quarrel or grievance with another, when he immediately threatens to inform
— "I shall go and inform"...

Funny facts...
In the residence of the Sosnowiec rabbi, Rabbi Hager, a distribution of money is taking place. The second fact concerns a Hasidic fellow. He too was favoured by the lot and won a good sum in the lottery, such as tens of thousands of Jews wish for themselves.

The right ear...

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion. Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Acharei-Kedoshim
The Portion
a) "And he shall take the two goats" (16:7)
Both goats had to be equal in height, in appearance and in value — so says the Gemara.
This was to show that outward appearance means nothing. One can be equal to the goat "for the Lord" in every outward respect, and yet, by one's inner essence, belong to Azazel, to the devil... Orach Chayim.
•
The goats — says the Gemara (Shevuot 2) — atoned for "the defilement of the Sanctuary and its holy things."
Yes, even between Sanctuary and holy things, at the very centre of holiness, there is sometimes plenty of hidden impurity... It is precisely there that impurity gets in. Hegyonot El-Ammi.
b) "After the doings of the land of Egypt" (18:1)
Not "the doings of the land of Egypt you shall not do," but "AFTER the doings," because everything you do is only in imitation of your neighbours, like parrots... Imrei Chen.
c) "Love your neighbour as yourself" (19:18)
Rabbi Moshe Leib of Sassov used to say:
I learned love of Israel from a peasant. Once I happened to be among peasants in a tavern, and one peasant says to another:
— Do you love me, brother?
— Very much.
— Then tell me what I lack.
— How should I know?
— Ha-ha! — laughs the peasant — if you don't know what I lack, how can you say you love me?
— Now — said Rabbi Moshe Leib — I know that to love a Jew means: to know what he lacks...
Eser Tzachtzachot.
• • •
The Midrash tells a wondrous legend (see also Tosafot, Menachot 37[?]a):
Ashmedai once brought before King Solomon a man who had two heads. This man had a normal brother. The two quarrelled over an inheritance. The one with two heads claimed that two shares were due to him. So Ashmedai brought them before Solomon.
King Solomon gave this ruling: pour boiling water on one head, and if the other one feels it, it is a sign that both heads are one head — — —
The moral:
The Jews have more than two heads. The German Jew is far from the Polish one, yet when water is poured on one head, the other one feels it at once — proof that both heads are in fact only one head...
Hegyonot El-Ammi.
d) "Just balances... I am the Lord" (ibid., 36)
If one trades with just balances and a just hin, one has to come to "I am the Lord"; by the natural course of things it is hard to live from honest trade, unless God helps... Arono shel Yosef.
e) "You shall surely rebuke your fellow" (ibid., 17)
The prophet Hosea laments the sins of the world and that no one rebukes the sinners any more, and he cries out: "Yet let no man strive, and let no man reprove" (Hosea 4).
Meaning:
Thus no one rebukes the other; no one cares to improve his fellow's deeds; only when he quarrels with him does he become a reprover and list his sins... But when "let no man strive" — then "let no man reprove": then no one wants to improve another's deeds... Yedi'ot ha-Ohel.
• • •
The author of "Tiferet Shlomo" once rebuked a rich man, an informer. The man, however, made nothing of it. Seeing that his words left no impression, the rebbe fell at his feet:
— Forgive me, forgive me...
— Forgive what? — the man asks.
— One may not revile any person; one may only rebuke him so that it has an effect. But with you I see it does not help at all, so I have shamed you for nothing, reviled you for nothing — forgive me...
Haftarah
f) "And I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations" (Amos 9)
God says: I will push the Jews from one place to another among the nations, so that they cannot take root anywhere and cannot assimilate with the others. Ahavat Yehonatan.
g) "And I will plant them upon their land."
Cedars and fir trees can be broken by the wind, because a human being planted them. By contrast, the little water reeds, which grow by themselves, bend under the wind but do not break.
"And I will plant them upon their land" — I will plant them on their own soil, then "they shall no more be plucked up out of their land," just like those soft reeds. R' Yehonatan Eybeschütz.
Avot
h) "Anyone with whom people are pleased" (3)
The criterion by which one can measure a person's piety — whether "God is pleased with him," whether he is truly pious before God — is: when "people are pleased with him," when he behaves towards people well and honestly... Sha'ar Bat Rabbim.
The Kibbutz Movement in Zagłębie | —o— Expansion Work for the Middle-Class Aliyah

[Zagłębie — HeChalutz and the hakhshara (pioneer training).]
It is 2 years since our kibbutz penetrated there, where people did not yet know that a pioneering kibbutz exists in Jewish Będzin: but times change. Various factors have driven towards this movement, which gives redemption to the Jewish youth that sees no future whatsoever before itself. This youth has today no other way out than only [printed „גור“] to come to "HeChalutz" and to make aliyah to Eretz Israel. But "HeChalutz" is no emigration society that should enable everyone to emigrate to Eretz Israel. No, "HeChalutz" has a more important task to fulfil. A national mission lies on its shoulders — to make the Jewish people healthy, and that is the hakhshara movement, which tears the Jewish young person away from his home and family and forges out of him a conscious working man for Eretz Israel, because the epoch is long gone when we were regarded as good-for-nothings, incapable of physical work. Today every Jewish employer can already convince himself how naturalized [?] we have already become in work, because by work we live, and with it we want to make the Jewish people healthy.
Here in Zagłębie, in the largest industrial centre of the country, we came precisely in a time of unemployment, but thanks to our perseverance and stubbornness we have succeeded in growing from 2 points, Będzin—Modrzejów, with 27 men on 1 August 1932 — to, today, 9 points with a number of nearly 250 men. We have set up work-shops — carpentries, shoemakers' shops, tailoring shops — and we are undertaking to set them up in the places where they do not yet exist. We have already penetrated into various trades — unskilled ("black") work as well as domestic service. We value every work; every work is important, if only humanity requires it. We are already proceeding to set up our central bakery in Będzin, which will supply the baked goods to all the units (plugot).
A few days ago the confirmation for aliyah to Eretz Israel took place with us.

A Queen Who Dies for Her Sins

[Historical serial — Mary, Queen of Scots, part 4.]
The tragic story of Queen Mary of Scotland. Her loves and political intrigues.

4.
Summary of the previous chapters:
Queen Mary of Scotland was crowned after her father's death, when she was about ten months old. At 6 she was betrothed, and at 15 she married the crown prince, son of Henri the Second and Catherine de Medici.
Mary's ambitions were great. The English Queen Elizabeth's proposal that she sign the Treaty of Edinburgh so as to obtain safe passage through England — she rejected. Travelling home, she was received at the Scottish port with great honour; the Scottish burghers, who had been told that the queen was a dissolute woman, saw before them a very young, graceful, naive [?] woman, and in their great enthusiasm the Puritan zealots sang chapters of Psalms in her honour.
On arriving in her capital, Mary appointed chief advisers from the Protestant camp. This aroused great resentment among the Catholics, and the queen issued a ban on Catholic demonstrations.
At that time people began proposing matches to the queen, who was a widow.
Among others, the French poet Chastelard courted the queen, and the queen [showed] him friendliness [?]. Once it happened that Chastelard hid in Mary's bedroom, and when she began to undress he threw himself upon her. For this Chastelard was condemned to death, and as he was being led to the execution he sang love songs in the queen's honour.
Her second victim was the Italian Rizzio. But she married her cousin, Lord Darnley. There was no domestic peace between the couple, and her husband prepared a conspiracy against her.
Now read on:
The conspirators organised a strong army, which besieged the royal palace. There, just then, was the Italian Rizzio, Mary's lover, who had been the real destroyer of the domestic peace between Mary and her husband.
The raging soldiers arrested Rizzio, dragged him by force out of the palace, and before the eyes of his beloved Mary they killed him.
After Rizzio's murder Parliament was dissolved. Lord Darnley, Mary's husband, who had led the conspiracy, issued a proclamation to the people. In the proclamation Lord Darnley declared himself King of Scotland, and the Protestants, who had been enslaved under Rizzio's rule, only now came to power.
This return to power caused Mary to make peace with her husband, whom she also persuaded to withdraw from his comrades.
Escorted by two thousand cavalrymen, Mary and her husband fled to "Ranbak" [?] [probably Dunbar]; from there they returned to Edinburgh.
The peace between Mary and her husband did not last long. The new conflict between them arose from the fact that Lord Darnley would not acknowledge the only child Mary bore on 19 June 1556 [sic; should be 1566].
Lord Darnley suspected Mary of being unfaithful to him, of having carried on love affairs with other men during the time she was his wife. Darnley's greatest suspicion, that the child born was not his, arose because while they were estranged Mary had taken as her lover the commander of the cavalry regiment, Bothwell, who later became Darnley's murderer and afterwards Mary's lawful husband.
The non-acknowledgement of the child aroused great bitterness against Darnley in royal circles; the fire and the hatred flared up even more when Darnley refused even to take part in the christening ceremony, and his place was taken by Bothwell, Mary's lover.
In connection with the disgrace Darnley had brought on Mary and on the monarchy in particular, a conference of Mary's intimates took place, among whose participants were also Bothwell and Mary's brother Moray.
At the conference the question was discussed of what to do with Darnley, who had stained the royal dynasty. There were various opinions, but the majority decided that Darnley should not get a divorce, but rather be murdered.
Darnley, learning of the decision that they wanted to kill him, fled to Glasgow, but even there the hand of the conspiracy reached him. After a few days in Glasgow he suddenly fell seriously ill, and doctors established that he had been poisoned at a meal.
While Darnley lay in hospital, Mary came to him and by various false means persuaded him to agree, for the sake of his health, to travel with her to Craigmillar palace, where he would receive proper and better medical care.
Darnley [printed "Dagli"] did not suspect that his wife was preparing a sinister [?] plan for him, and let himself be persuaded to travel with her to her palace. But instead of taking him there, they carried him off to a village outside Edinburgh, where everything was already prepared, and there indeed they murdered him.

Antisemitic agitation in Germany in the 19th century.

Philosophers, poets and historians take part in the agitation. — The financial crash in Germany in 1873 and the revenge on the Jews for it. — The blood libel in Konitz in 1900. — Germany gives the Jews rights and takes them back. — The "gebisene"[?] situation after the year '70. — Further depictions of Jewish-German relations.
By S. Rosenfeld.

1.
The equality of rights that the French Revolution brought to the French Jews struck terror into the Germans. They lived in one fear: lest, God forbid, the free spirit leap across the Rhine and bring it about that the German Jews too become citizens equal with the Germans themselves. That the Jews were striving for this was no secret — so what does one do against the danger?
And Germany began to save itself, and with what impetus, with what hatred! Suddenly all Germany was flooded with anti-Jewish literature. It began with an anonymous pamphlet, but with great success. Here begins the "proof" that the Jews are so corrupt that they cannot be good citizens. Freedom of conscience with regard to Jews is a crime. The government may gradually improve their situation, but only to the extent that they draw closer to Christianity. That began in the year 1794. But a year later we hear that even converts should not be given any rights, at least not until six years after the conversion; and three years later it is preached that Jews are harmful in any case. And "history teaches us that one must not have dealings with Jews". Even the great Goethe drives the Jews out of his ideal state. The reason: "How can we join them to the higher culture, when they deny its worth and its [—]?[?]". Even more strongly does one of the greatest German philosophers, Fichte, express himself: "Let the Jews, he says, be given human rights; but civil rights can be given them only if one were to cut off every Jew's head in a single night and put on another, in which there would not be a single Jewish thought. To rid oneself of the Jews there is only one means — to conquer the 'Promised Land' for them and pack them all off there." At that time, at the very end of the eighteenth century, there were even a few German writers who came out with pamphlets defending Jewish equality, but they made no impression whatsoever. People and government leave this literature unnoticed. On the contrary, every good word for the Jews immediately calls forth a sea of words against them. Professors and officials, philosophers and poets — all consider it their highest duty to save Germany from the Jewish danger. It goes so far that the chief of the Berlin police forbade the printing of "treatises" on the Jewish question. But that does not help, for what is forbidden in Berlin is allowed in Königsberg or Marburg, etc. And with what libels they come out against the Jews! With what abuse, insults and filth. All the Jews' friends among the gentiles [—] — they are literally thrown out of their graves. Lessing is reviled. The meanest little gentile considers himself greater than Lessing, because he never allowed himself to associate with a Jew... And the people swallowed it all and leaned on it in forming a political-civic worldview for itself. One such pamphleteer, Grattenauer, at the beginning of the nineteenth century (1803), had six printings within a short time and was spread in thirteen thousand copies (which in those days was a great rarity). The defence from the Jewish side helped little: first, because only Jews read it, and second, because it was written in such a pitiful tone that it could not command any respect among non-Jewish readers (Dubnow).
This ugly, wild propaganda stopped as soon as Napoleon began to rule in the German provinces. He gave the Jews equal rights.
But hardly had the five or six years of Napoleon's so-called world rule passed; hardly had his strong hand been lowered: the breath of the French Revolution evaporated, and once again the German peoples refreshed their hatred of the Jews. With one hand they fought for their liberation, and with the other they sought to enslave the Jewish population. Against the great principles of the French Revolution — "Liberty, Equality and Fraternity" — the Germans set up their age-old principles: protection of the Christian state, loyalty to the old traditions, and the monarch's solemn care for his subjects. And their ideal of a monarch was the wild Germanic ruler Frederick Barbarossa, a despot of the 12th century (see Philippson).
And the "Congress of Vienna" too (1814—1815), in which representatives of all countries took part and where the Jewish question of Germany was also dealt with, left the question of Jewish rightlessness unresolved. And every land and every free city continued its Jew-hating Jewish policy, as before Napoleon's conquests. There were a very few exceptions for the better, but for German Jewry as a whole they had no value (see Dr. S. Baron: "The Jewish Question at the Congress of Vienna" (in German), Vienna and Berlin 1920).

2.
And again the great national agitation against the Jews begins. An agitation — resting on lies, on libels and on preposterous old wives' tales — scholars and clergymen, philosophers and writers — all have only one theme for their writing and speaking: the Jews. And one approach: bitter hatred. Not even an effort is made to prove the accusations. Already the year 1816 brings a whole flood of antisemitic literature, written by people with popular names. It was said that Napoleon owed his dictatorship to the Jews alone — although everyone knew how energetically the Jews had fought together with the Germans in the war of liberation against Napoleon. The well-known philosopher Fries demanded that, if the Jews could not be driven out of Germany entirely, such harsh laws should be made for them that they would have to flee. What literature had not achieved, the theatre achieved. There, with success, they staged pieces in which the Jew was depicted as the most loathsome creature in the world. And the "Court" was so pleased with this that it found it fitting for such a play to be staged in honour of the Russian Emperor Alexander I, who was visiting Berlin at that time.
The great agitation had its consequences. In Bavaria the attitude to the Jews became so tense that a pogrom could be expected to break out at any minute. The Würzburg rabbi turned to the Bavarian parliament with a petition from the Bavarian Jews that their legal situation be improved. "A professor, a Catholic priest and a count supported the petition. The parliament decided to refer the petition to a commission. But as soon as it became known what the parliament had decided, petitions immediately began to arrive from all classes of the population, demanding not only that Jewish rights not be improved, but that the Jews be driven out of Bavaria altogether. On 2 August 1819 the Würzburg students attacked the professor (Brendel) who had defended the Jewish petition, and beat him badly. The students were joined by the shopkeepers and the artisans, and together they made a pogrom on the Würzburg Jews. And the next day four hundred Jews were driven out of the town because they had disturbed the public peace...
The Würzburg example was followed by Frankfurt, Bamberg, Danzig and a number of other towns. In Hamburg the Senate summoned the town's prominent Jews and told them to behave more modestly and not to arouse the anger of the people against themselves. And at the same time a pamphlet appeared, "Der Judenspiegel" (The Jews' Mirror), in which it is written explicitly that killing a Jew is no crime; it is no more than an offence against a police regulation. The same writer (Hundt-Radowsky, printed "Gundt-Radowsky") proposes: "The Jews should be sold to the English, who will trade in them as in Negro slaves. Moreover, the Jews should be castrated (mesares zayn) and the Jewish women distributed among all the brothels in the world"... And this work had enormous success throughout Germany. At the same time many other similar books appeared, in the same spirit. A real hell blazed throughout Germany. And when it came to discussing the extension of Jewish rights in the Saxe-Weimar parliament, none other than Goethe came out against the Jews, and this worsened the Jewish situation in that state. What happened in the smaller states happened also in the great state of Prussia. "Society and the governments had, as it were, a wager between them as to who would do the Jews more harm. And both won the wager.
And it all happened in the name of the "German spirit", in the name of the "great" titans who founded the great and pure, mighty German race.
At that time, at the end of the first quarter of the 19th century and the beginning of the second quarter, the defenders of the Jews also multiplied — both Jews and non-Jews. But it had no effect on the mood of the people, especially of the urban population. And the rulers of the lands, perhaps with a few exceptions, such as Baden, for instance, naturally side with the "people".

Hitleriade

(A humour corner, dedicated to the new wicked Haman, Hitler, and his gang).
Who is Hitler?
1. His coming into the world.
His mother had a hard pregnancy with him. According to the opinion of a doctor to whom she had turned, this was supposedly because he had a hard and heavy head. He came (unfortunately) into the world by accident, not fully carried to term. His mother, who had visited a zoological garden, had stared so hard at a wild donkey that, on coming home, she immediately lay down in bed and gave birth to this beast.
2. His upbringing.
Hitler's mother could not nurse him herself, because he was wild and vicious; he bit her breast, so she raised him on a bottle. That is why he was later so drawn to the bottle.
He began to speak very[?] early (at 4 o'clock in the morning). His first word was: "Jew". While still very small he already displayed warlike abilities: he used to fight and quarrel with all the children and make a cripple of each one. No whole dish dared to be found in the house.
3. His abilities at school.
In his studies he showed great abilities. Above all he excelled in mathematics, mineralogy, botany and astronomy: he would calculate mathematically how many windowpanes there were in the school.
Mineralogy: he knew with which stone the panes break more quickly.
Botany: when he saw a garden fence, he would jump over it and uproot everything.
Astronomy: he used to split the "stars" (pun: Yiddish "shterns" = stars and foreheads)... Even in zoology he was a marvel: he let no living creature pass...
4. His further progress.
On leaving (or rather falling out of — as people assure us, the teachers threw him out) school, with quite a few "distinctions" (that is, marks he received from his schoolmates), he did not know what to take up first. Becoming a shoemaker was against his principle (he did not like to bow before anyone), so he hit upon the idea of becoming a house painter: that way he would be able to climb from rung to rung. But he did not have much luck: whoever took him on once did not want to know of him a second time, until he got thrown out for [suing over?] a flat[?]. And since the one who threw him out happened to be a Jew, he swore to take revenge on all Jews. He would go from tavern to tavern pouring pitch and brimstone on all Jews. On and on, until he gained a large number of followers, some[?] cripples and idlers, who took him as their "head".
What came next I need not tell.
Knapvarger.
Pinyele Mazik's Political Speech

Delivered on the First of May.
Comrade lads!
What do you say to this grand racket[?] ("gran-doznik")! If "Jaś" Hitler has become chancellor, then I, Pinyele Mazik, must become emperor.
My father yells: why don't I go to cheder. Well, I ask you, comrade lads, isn't he, my father, a roasted fool! A thousand kapores — who needs to study nowadays! The educated "shmintelligentsia" lies in the ground and bakes bagels. Today, comrade lads, we have the power in our paws[?] ("lapkes")! Whoever can land a punch in the mug ("morde") becomes German Reich Chancellor; whoever can "chop a teakettle" (talk nonsense) and "bake" left and right ("ga lyekha un ga prakha") — he sits at the New Market number 4 and drinks tea "na szczot" (on the tab).
Comrade lads! Listen to what Pinyele Mazik tells you: if you are fools, you will have the same luck as all the merchants of Zagłębie, and you will have to stand in the queue ("ogonek") for a bit more soup ("juszka") from the Magistrate (municipality).
So says your friend,
Pinyele Mazik.
A Little Letter to Hitler

First of all, I can give you regards from a colleague of yours in the trade — a house painter who was already standing up high[?] on the ladder, at the very top — and he fell down and broke his neck. The same to be heard of you! As far as I can see, you are no small "genius" in the painting line, for with the brown paint you have blackened the face of all Germany — the same to be heard of you! From what I've heard, since you became chancellor you have thrown away all your painter's tools altogether... Only with the hand you used to paint with you have not broken off relations, and because of the boycott you are groping quite nicely for a hand... Secondly, you do as your heart desires. Throughout Germany you order people to talk to the hand...
I have seen, "Panie" (Mister) Hitler, a photograph of yours, and I noticed that the trousers you wear are too big for you. As I suspect[?], these are not your trousers — they surely come from a big man...
As for your anti-Jewish policy, I can tell you that if you beat Jews, the Jews will beat you back; no problem, our Jews know very well how to strike... What, you haven't yet tasted Jewish blows? Then just listen to me: Jews know very well how to "beat kapores". And this much is certain, that you too will be the kapore (scapegoat)...
As for your race-purification, there is a good piece of advice. Take, if you please, into the Hitlerite party only pedigree swine — and you'll have a pure Hitlerite race.
Yours, Yehuda Fridman.

A Zawiercie Jew Dies Suddenly on His Way to the Railway Station in Dąbrowa

[Zawiercie / Dąbrowa — tragedy.] On Tuesday afternoon the 58-year-old Lejb Isakow of Zawiercie died suddenly in Dąbrowa.
The tragically deceased had been in Sosnowiec that same day on business matters. Travelling back home, he paid a visit to his family in Dąbrowa.
At the critical moment, running to the station in Dąbrowa, he fell down and remained lying unconscious.
The crowd that came running thought he was an epileptic and did not want to touch him; and so, lying in the street, Isakow died.
Doctors established that while running he had suffered a heart attack.

The return match in ping-pong, which took place in the premises of the Sosnowiec "Maccabi", was won by "HaKoach" with a big result of 1:6. The victory came to "HaKoach" relatively very easily. The points for "HaKoach" were won by: Rubinlicht, Auerbach, Gutman, Ładyński, Strachlitz and Mauer. For "Maccabi" the only point was won by the best player, Nawarski.
"HaKoach" — "Zagłębie" 0:4 (0:1)
Again "HaKoach" won a great victory over the 1932 champion of Zagłębie, "Zagłębie" (Dąbrowa).
In this match "HaKoach" truly concentrated; all players without exception played with great ambition, just as if a fresh spirit had entered them; and had the right wing of the "HaKoach" attack played the way the left wing plays, the result of the match would surely have been twice as much.
Special recognition is earned by Berl Szywek, who played in this match with great ambition and helped much towards the victory of "HaKoach".
"HaKoach" kicks off the match and at once carries out a fine attack on the opponent's goal. Already in the 4th minute "HaKoach" has a chance to score the first goal from a corner nicely taken by Hamplen[?], but the ball hits the post and goes out. "HaKoach" is constantly on the attack. Kalman, who that day was in poor form, was very irritating with his play. A few minutes before the break Motil Rozen scores the first goal.
After half-time "HaKoach" gave the real "concert", attacking without stop. In the second half "HaKoach" had great superiority. In the 60th minute the referee awards a free kick ("wolny"), Gutman takes it and "HaKoach" leads 20 [sic, probably 2:0]; a few minutes later Gutman scores the third goal. The last goal is scored by Kalman, who broke through the defence on his own. Referee — Okularczyk.
Finally, a few words must be said to the esteemed match spectators: they should not leave the playing field before the match is completely over, because the commotion thereby created[?] on the ground can force the referee to break off the game, and then the match is lost by "walkover".
A. Chraclawski[?].

Appeal to the Jewish Population of Będzin!

[Będzin — relief for refugees from Germany; appeal.] "Our brethren, the children of Israel, who are in distress and captivity!"
You all know of the great, terrible tragedy which one of the finest Jewish communities in the world is living through. Tens of thousands of Jewish families in Germany have been thrust out, by the savage Hitlerite barbarians and by their merciless terror methods, from their well-founded positions, workplaces and businesses, and, finding themselves at the edge of the abyss, they are forced to take the wanderer's staff in hand and wander wherever their eyes carry them.
Because our town lies in the neighbourhood of the land of the tragic events, a part of the wandering victims has already arrived, and probably more such unfortunates will keep arriving.
— The moment has therefore come when we must show our brotherhood in feelings of compassion and give them substantial help and support.
We therefore appeal to you: help create the relief fund for the stricken victims; time is short and the help is urgently needed.
We are also well aware of the hard economic situation in which we Polish Jews find ourselves in the present time of crisis, but nevertheless we must demand of you that you exert yourselves and bring sacrifices on the altar of our unfortunate brothers, because it is a matter of saving lives (pikuach nefesh).
Remember: "The voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me!"

Dr. Weinzieher (Chairman).

Impressive Jewish Protest Meeting in Dąbrowa against Hitlerism

[Dąbrowa — the protest against Hitler.] On the initiative of the kehilla administration in Dąbrowa, an open-air protest meeting against the persecution of Jews in Germany took place last Sunday.
The protest on the part of Jewish Dąbrowa succeeded brilliantly. Such a popular demonstration has never yet taken place in Dąbrowa. Thousands of Jews, women and young people gathered in the courtyard of Mr. Rajchman's house on 3 Maja Street to express their anger against the Hitlerite government, which has in its programme the extermination of German Jewry.
Before the meeting began, a sharp incident occurred between the Betarists and "Hashomer Hatzair". The latter began attacking the Betarists because they had come dressed in the brown shirts. Thanks to the stewarding of the Dąbrowa "Maccabi" and the strict discipline of the chairman, Mr. Neufeld, it did not come to any serious clashes.
The meeting is opened by the kehilla president, Mr. Abraham Neufeld, who gives the introduction to the meeting, pointing out the deceitful deeds of the German government, and gives the first word to the lawyer Mr. Brand of Będzin, who makes a speech in Yiddish about German anti-Semitism.
Sharp speeches, which make the proper impression, are made by Messrs. Dr. Weinzieher (Będzin), councillor (ratman) of the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce, President Mr. Aliner[?] and Mr. Leibl Stuszegowski[?]. After the reading of the appropriate resolutions by councillor Mr. Bernard Rechnic, a street procession is formed, in which almost the entire Jewish population of Dąbrowa took part. In the synagogue Mr. L. Stuszegowski spoke again, and the cantor, after singing "Hanoten Teshua", made a memorial prayer for the new martyrs who perished in Germany.

A Sensational Safety Device against Disasters in the Coal Mines

Among the hardest and at the same time most dangerous kinds of work, in which a person risks his life every minute, is work in the coal mines. Despite all precautions, gas explosions still occur, and the workers who find themselves at the site of the disaster are suffocated or crushed by the masses of torn-loose rock.
Radio has now come to the aid of the coal miners.
After radio's brilliant achievements at sea and on land, after radio has saved thousands of people during shipwrecks or during great floods and earthquakes, radio has now descended into the depths of the earth, to bring help there too to the suffering and the unfortunate.
The first country to begin using radio in the coal mines is England. In the coal mines of Yorkshire a fully equipped radio station has been installed. All the corridors of the coal mines, which stretch for kilometres under the earth, have been fitted with powerful loudspeakers, which report every five minutes on the state of the gases in the shafts and warn the workers in good time to leave the threatened places at once.
The Children Saved Father and Mother from a Divorce — The Mother Does Not Want to Hand the Children Over to a Stepmother

A couple came to the Będzin rabbinate to get divorced. The reason — an ordinary one: until the wedding canopy love bloomed, after the wedding the warmth still held, after the first child it grew cooler, after the second child — already quite cold. And when the livelihood also ran out, love turned into enmity; they did nothing but quarrel and fight until they could no longer live together.
If one cannot live together, there is a divorce. But what does one do with the children? The wife argued that he must take the children; after all he is the father, so let him give them bread. The husband, however, argued: how will he be able to look for a living with the yoke of children without a mother on his neck?
In the end they came to an agreement that the children would stay with the father, and they had already set about writing the get.
The scribe writes, and father and mother talk quietly about the fate of their little children. The father is sulking and the mother wipes her eyes.
Suddenly she cries out hysterically:
— What? A stepmother for my children? May I not live to see it!
And he answers quietly:
— What choice will I have? I must look for bread for the children, I can't nurse them!
The little wife broke into sobs, saying that she would not let her two diamonds fall into strange hands, and finally cried out that she does not want a divorce — let them stop writing.
The scribe laid down his pen, and husband and wife were once again standing before the rabbinate. They regret it. They will try again to live together; perhaps it will get better.

When People Are Turned into Beasts

L. Szpigelman.
(The great distance from the Asia of old to the Europe of today. — How does the world react, and how do we react?)
It is a remarkable thing how mankind can get used to everything; we would never in our lives have believed to what things people can remain indifferent, and how one can make peace with the most tragic phenomena, with the most horrifying events.
The world shuddered on hearing what is happening in Germany; we were outraged when we saw what is being done there to Jewish families, only because they were born Jews. They may have the greatest merits towards their fatherland, they may be the greatest patriots and have made the most important sacrifices — as soon as they are not pure Aryans, as soon as pure Christian blood from generations back does not flow in their veins, they have become fair game in Hitler's land for every hooligan, for every outcast.
Under the prevailing situation in Germany all the Jews there have been condemned to ruin. But ruin is, after all, a zero[?] compared with the existence, compared with the degradation taking place there. When Jews are now being ruined and exterminated in Germany, one keeps silent; it is regarded as a respectable deed, that is, modestly, with dignity, and everything is hush-hush; nobody knows about the silent victims who are breathing out their souls. What strikes the eye are only the bestial murders, the most horrifying victims, the victims with whom one plays as with a toy until one lets them breathe out their souls.
One could never have imagined that people are capable of murdering in such a bestial way, that people can cut pieces of flesh from the living, that people can devise how to force parents to violate their own children. Granted, we Jews, who lived in the Tsarist times under the Russian yoke, were used to pogroms; but what a distance, what a long road of culture lies between those dark times and today? Thirty years ago, when they wanted to stage a pogrom in a single small town, they prepared for it for months, and they had to turn to the dark element, to the village peasant, and persuade him that the Jew is no human being at all, that he has no soul in him, that he is — so they tried to convince him — a spirit, a devil[?], and that he brings all evil into the world; and then they put[?] a great deal of work into it, and managed to carry out sometimes a bigger pogrom and sometimes a smaller one; but for this work they had to use half-wild creatures, and they[?] committed all the evil. The keepers of order and the Russian authorities knew how to step aside at such a moment, to hide in their holes, and their re-emergence was a signal that enough blood had been shed and that it was time to restore the town to its normal appearance. And after such a piece of "work" the Russian official circles were ashamed to raise their eyes; before the civilised world they were branded as Asiatics[?], and could find no place for shame.
And if we draw a parallel between that era and today's modern times, only then do we see[?] how far the world has "progressed" over time. How pale those pogroms are in comparison with the present mass murders in Germany! And then came our Bialiks and Frugs and poured out their bitter wrath before the great world, and it did indeed find an echo; and after them came the Tolstoys and Gorkys, who made the world resound with their voices, and the Russian government had to render an account of its deeds — deeds that are almost a zero[?] compared with the events now taking place in Germany, in which the ruling government officially takes part. They do not hide, they find no need to conceal themselves; on the contrary, they do it officially and legally, and use the most modern[?] technology for their barbaric deeds. With the help of the radio it is proclaimed throughout the whole country that the Jewish population must be exterminated not only in Germany but in the whole world; and these explicit words are heard plainly from official circles, and nobody is the least ashamed of it; on the contrary, it is said boldly, openly and loudly, before everyone's eyes, as if one were fulfilling a holy mission.
And it is characteristic that at the very time when all ingenuity is invested, when they study by what more horrible method to murder and violate mankind, at that same time they were seized with pity for a beast and for a chicken, lest, God forbid, it be slaughtered according to Jewish law, because that way it suffers more and longer than when its head is chopped off. See how sensitive the Hitlerite government is, and what delicacy and compassion they show towards the innocent, helpless fowl — is this not Mephistophelean laughter? Have not people been turned into real beasts? Would primitive beasts be capable of tormenting their victims the way the Aryans in Germany are now doing? And could one ever have imagined that now, after mankind has progressed so colossally in every field of its life and development, we would arrive at an era of the Middle Ages — when even then they were far from knowing how to torture people in such a bestial way as is happening before our eyes; and, however horrible it may be, we are assured[?] that we do not yet know everything, and that it is much, much more horrible, much, much more tragic — although we cannot understand what could be still more tragic, in what way one could torment the innocent human victims even more.
Yes, at first people were frightened, people were shaken, the world began to sympathise with us, in the English Parliament there was uproar, and the Germans were crowned as "heroic[?] barbarians", for which they lost their prestige and failed with their policy on all fronts. But is that enough for us? Is our satisfaction settled[?] by it?
The newspapers report that the atrocities in Germany surpass all imagination, and people have started to read it like any other news, like any other event. But the question arises: have we thereby done our duty? Has the ruling Hitler government in Germany already received a licence (hechsher) to annihilate all the Jews who are in its power, and nobody in the world has anything to say to it, because these are its citizens, its victims? Does it not have to give an account before the world, at least like the autocratic Russia of former days? And is there no power that would compel it, first of all, to stop the terrible slaughters of human beings — Jews, just as it did with regard to cattle and fowl? Let us not delude ourselves that the bloodthirsty beasts cannot be forced to stop shedding, after so many weeks, innocent blood in such a bestial way! If the world only wanted to, means would be found to stop first of all the murders and killings of innocent citizens, whose sin consists in being Jews.
Where are the great, mighty guardians of the world, who would bang on the table and order the bestial murders to be stopped? Where are the great philosophers and spokesmen, who have so much piety, esteem and reverence for the crown of all creation — for the human being?
But not only Jews are being killed in the Hitlerite hell. Everything and everyone who has the courage to think and feel differently is being stifled in a terrible way. Every free thought in Germany is now being exterminated like a plague; the government of the whip (nagaika) is employed with full force, stopping at nothing and taking no one into account.
Can the whole world really look on indifferently at what is now happening in Hitlerite Germany, and nobody is to say anything to it? Can one look on at all this with a quiet conscience and not grasp the great sin that is thereby committed against human beings? Where are they, those who know how to grasp the deep tragedy that is played out then in the human soul? When a person is devoured by a beast, one knows that a wild creature did it, from which one could not save oneself; but as soon as people devour one another in a bestial way, humanity is offended and violated — which man must not allow; and if he does it nevertheless, it is a sign that the humane has departed from him, that sanctity is being desecrated.
Human beings could not have dreamt that in the present era people would fall so low, and that there would be no one to cry out: Stop! The limit has long been overstepped, and one can no longer distinguish man from beast.
And if the world keeps silent, if the great personalities turn a blind eye to the matter, if they want the situation to be changed in a diplomatic way — then where, in that case, are the Jewish representatives, the great men who can make their way to the high windows? Why do they not burst in there, why do they not cry out that now is no time to conduct diplomacy, that first of all one must see to it that the blood which is being shed without end be stopped before anything else? Why do they not storm with all their strength, why do they not uncover the whole truth, however terrible and tragic it may be? Can one hesitate at such a moment? May it be allowed that the situation be brought to the point of a chronic disease, that they murder[?] down to the last one? The situation is terrible, and every delay is a crime from the human and the Jewish standpoint.
Between Ourselves

(A letter to a friend).
Second letter.
Yesterday I met your daughter Sarah's little girl out walking with her German governess. She really does speak quite fine German already. It surprised me: why German of all things? Why not French? After all, the children of your elder daughter study at the non-Jewish gymnasium; apparently the taste and sympathies for a language are not one and the same among your daughters. As long as it is not Yiddish. And an original thought came into my head: we Jews have taken up a new kind of peddling.
I do not mean to make fun of you, although[?] at times you look[?] very ridiculous to me. I remember how recently, while I was your guest, you with the skullcap on your head and your missus with the wig on her head and the "Tseno Ureno" in her hand struggled and twisted your tongues to speak to the grandchildren in their "mother tongue" — Polish. It was pitiful to look at you, and I thought to myself: pity these people: not only are their bodies in exile — their psychology, their reason, their sense of honour are also enslaved and crippled.
You then justified yourself to me and argued: what am I guilty of? I am a religious Jew, I sent my children to learn in the cheders, I taught my daughters Judaism, my home is a truly Jewish one: Sabbath is Sabbath, a holiday is a holiday, I pray every day, I keep all the commandments and taught my children to keep them too, and even my daughters I taught Judaism. So what am I guilty of, if the children go away from me? The gentile ways please them better, the surroundings are stronger than we are...
I know all this, dear friend, I know that assimilation has driven its sharp, dirty nails into the body of the people, has fogged its eyes and darkened its spirit. But how am I to notice[?] and not wonder at the sad fact that precisely in your pious, kosher, Orthodox home this assimilation holds greater sway than among the freethinkers? It is precisely in your house that Jewishness is going to ruin. Your elder daughters are dazzled by the glitter of rotten salon aristocratism; of your younger sons and daughters, some are devoured by the red assimilation, and the other part has fallen in with the so-called gilded youth and sunk into the forty-nine gates of impurity of the jazz band, the foxtrot and the rumba. All this flows together into a wild demons' dance, a black hurricane, in which your family, together with other such families, vanishes entirely from the Jewish horizon.
Where is the cause? Is it merely an accident, or is it simply a consequence of your way of life, of your — so to speak[?] — pious way of living?
I am inclined to maintain that the second reason is the true one. What I will tell you now will seem[?] a paradox to you, yet it is the truth: your piety is not a pure Jewish piety. Ahad Ha'am characterised the assimilationists with the concept of "slavery within freedom": having all civil and social rights, a man can remain a slave if he lacks the feeling of a national "I". For these, and for more like you, one can use the concept of "assimilation within religion". One can be pious, keep the commandments, and still not be a true Jew — or be a Jew with a Christian psychology.
The aim of piety, my friend, is the World to Come — the Kingdom of Heaven. You want to be one of the righteous who sit in Paradise with crowned heads and enjoy "the radiance of the Divine Presence". That is why you keep only the commandments between man and God, and even in giving charity you cannot rise higher than the narrowest philanthropy — giving a poor man alms, and sometimes also a lunch to a hungry one. But you are not capable of grasping that charity for the community, charity for the liberation of the Jewish people.
The tidings and the revival of your people reached only your ears, and did not touch your heart. When the people's children went in the vanguard to build the Jewish land of the Jewish future, you kept your children away from it. When Jews contributed their pennies to buy bricks for the building, you kept your pocket firmly pinned shut. And even here at home, in the exile you love so much, you see every day how your schools are on the point of closing, how your teachers, who do not let the Jewish spark go out, are perishing from hunger and cold — and your heart is not moved, and your spirit is not saddened. Your Messiah, about whom you tell a lie every day, that you are looking out for him to come at last, is suffering in his chains, which you strengthen and forge ever stronger through your indifference, through your pious egoism. To your ears there do not reach the groans of the Jewish Shekhinah, of the Jewish spirit, which is crippled and trampled even by your own children, over whom you have already lost your influence, who already listen to you the way Haman listens to the grogger.
And if your grandchildren throw your[?] "Tseno Ureno" into the rubbish bin together with your Shulchan Arukh and your tallit and tefillin; and if they leave you through mixed marriages, or simply convert — then do not ask, my friend: what am I guilty of? — it could not have been otherwise.
I. Berman.
The Way Out Is the Field

[Palestine — Jewish National Fund.] (Specially for the "Zaglembier Tsaytung".)
In the great tumult over the "prosperity" in the Land of Israel, over the great prospects opening up for the plantations, for trade and industry, all the quiet notes about the real ground under one's feet may get lost. New slogans arrive, and they must arrive together with the new time and with the changed conditions. No development at all could have taken place if time were not taken into account in every new initiative. Or else, no such development would have had any value in which time would have blurred and abolished the basic foundations, the first principles that led to the development in the first place.
In the work for the Land of Israel we must constantly, in the very midst of the stream of changes of the time, stop for a while in order to stress once again and yet again the old truths: the basic foundations — this principle of land ownership, this necessity of creating for the people a large landholding in reserve for colonisation purposes — may seem, in a stormy time, like remnants of a romantic era. Therefore one must from time to time return to this ABC of our Zionism, in order to plant in the hearts of the people the firm conviction that without [printed: "in"] the national land property there is no lasting and secure development of our work.
It is good that the National Fund from time to time develops propaganda for its aims. Through this propaganda the Zionist and his goals are refreshed in today's prosaic times. The new undertaking of the "Mif'al Meyuhad" [Special Project] deserves particular attention. Lag BaOmer, which has always been a day of "going out into the field", is the most fitting day for considering the role of the field in our new life in the Land of Israel.
One must go out into the field of Jewish labour in the Land of Israel and see what can still be done there in order to increase the tempo of our activity. Jewish labour in the colonies is far from being represented one hundred per cent. There are colonies, such as Petah Tikva, Ness Ziona and Rishon LeZion, where the number of Arab workers exceeds that of the Jewish ones. In order to settle the Jewish worker in the colonies and help him to a farmstead of his own, the National Fund bought land in the colonies and around them, on which the workers employed in the colonies were settled. This has made it possible to increase from year to year the number of Jewish workers who, with the help of their wages, can attain a farmstead of their own.
It must not be allowed that there should arise in the Sharon, over the whole plantation area, a block of expensive private plantations owned by a small number of Jewish proprietors in the midst of an Arab population, without a large, well-rooted Jewish population of small townsfolk and workers. But the land for this population can be acquired by these unpropertied individuals only through national means, only through the National Fund. For none of these individuals can attain landholding in that area, which is now valued very dearly on the land market.
Without a dense Jewish population that would support itself by wages from the colonies, by petty trade and cottage industry, living on a farmstead of its own on National Fund land, the great fortunes that the individuals' orange groves represent will not be secure. The National Fund must assist private initiative. It must provide land for the working man who can live around the orange groves, so as not to make this Jewish worker a wandering day-labourer, but a rooted citizen who builds himself up on his own and creates new opportunities of work and livelihood for the further immigrants.
More national land, more Jews planted on this land and more prospects for a further, increased aliyah. That is the meaning of the "Mahanot ha-Po'alim" — the workers' camps that the National Fund wants to set up on its land around the colonies. That is a goal that speaks not only to the heart of a Zionist, but also to the soul of every Jew who, in the Diaspora, goes out into a foreign field and dreams of Jewish redemption.
The law on offices for writing petitions.

In No. 31 of the "Dz. U." [Dziennik Ustaw, the Journal of Laws] the law on offices for writing petitions has appeared, according to which running such an office is permitted only on the basis of a permit from the administrative authority, which issues the permit at its own free discretion and if it recognises that such an office is necessary. To run such an office, which is to write petitions only to the administrative authority, a permit from the starostwo [district office] suffices; if the office will also write court papers, the permit must be issued in agreement with the president of the district court.
The permit is issued for 3 years only.
A permit may be obtained by a person who holds Polish citizenship, enjoys civil and civic rights, has not been punished for violating the military regulations, has not acted against the state and the like, possesses the moral qualifications and has passed the examination in Polish, certain administrative sciences and the principles of this law.
Petitions to the President of the State, the Ministry of Justice, courts, the public prosecutor's office and court offices may be written in those offices that have a permit from the district court. Every petition must bear the firm name of the office and its address, as well as the price paid.
The offices may not give legal advice, solicit clients through advertisements, conduct lawsuits or represent clients.
Whoever violates the above-mentioned regulations is punished administratively with up to a month's arrest and a 1000 zł fine, or one of these penalties.
For writing petitions without the appropriate permits and for giving advice, penalties of 1 to 6 months' arrest and up to 5,000 zł are provided.
Whoever is professionally engaged in writing petitions without permits may receive a penalty of 3 to 6 months and up to 10 thousand zł.
The law also provides penalties for "rufers" [touts] and punishes those who deliver clients to lawyers, notaries, offices or back-street ("corner") writers with arrest of up to 2 weeks or 1000 zł.
In addition, the injured party [?] is awarded compensation of 20 to 1000 zł, which does not exclude a claim for damages.
For violating the regulations of this law the office may be closed at any time.
The law does not apply to persons belonging to the bar, nor to societies whose statutes provide for giving legal aid to their members — within the framework of that aid.
The law provides for the issuing of an ordinance by the Ministers of the Interior and of Justice concerning the offices.
The law comes into force on the 4th of czerwiec [June] this year.
Dr. R. R.

A Queen Who Dies for Her Sins

[Serialized historical tale — Scotland, Mary Stuart; installment 5.]

The tragic story of Queen Mary of Scotland, her loves and political intrigues.

5.

Brief summary of the previous chapters:

Queen Mary "and" Scotland [sic; read: of Scotland] was crowned after her father's death, when she was about ten months old. At 6 she was betrothed, and at 15 she married the crown prince, son of Henry II and Catherine de' Medici [printed "Katerina de Medishi"].

Mary's ambitions were great. The proposal of the English Queen Elizabeth to sign the Edinburgh treaty, so that she would have free passage through England — she rejected. Travelling home, she was received at the Scottish port with great honour; the Scottish burghers, who had been told that the queen was a dissolute woman, saw before them a young [?], graceful, naive woman, and in their great enthusiasm the pious Puritans sang chapters of Psalms in her honour.

On arriving in her capital, Mary appointed chief advisers from the Protestant camp; this provoked great resentment among the Catholics, and the queen issued a ban on Catholic demonstrations.

At that time, the queen being a widow, people began to propose matches to her.

Among others, the French poet Chastelard courted the queen, and the queen showed him friendliness too. Once it happened that Chastelard hid in Mary's bedroom, and when she began to undress he threw himself upon her. For this Chastelard was sentenced to death, and as he was led to execution he sang love songs in the queen's honour.

Her second victim was the Italian "Ditsia" [sic; i.e. Rizzio]. But she married her cousin, Lord "Dargli" [sic; i.e. Darnley]. There was no domestic peace between the couple, and her husband prepared a conspiracy against her.

The royal palace was besieged by the revolutionary soldiers, who seized Mary's lover "Ditsia" and killed him.

Afterwards Mary made peace with her husband, but it did not last long before they quarrelled again, and in revenge he refused to acknowledge his child — the child Mary had borne. Because of the disgrace, Mary's brothers murdered him.

Now read on:

The murder took place as follows: it was on 9 February 1567. Mary took leave of her husband, telling him that she was going to Edinburgh to a ball.

Barely a few hours had passed after Mary's departure when the whole town was shaken by a gunpowder explosion.

The inhabitants ran through the streets; at first nobody knew what had happened, and only later did it become clear that the explosion had occurred in the royal palace, where the sick "Dargli", Mary's husband, lay — and he indeed perished under the ruins. His body was buried in a box in the palace. Thus briefly ended the life of the third victim of Mary Stuart's love games.

The inhabitants of the country were under the heavy impression of the tragic death of King "Dargli". It was no secret to anyone that Mary herself had contributed much to this calamity together with her lover, the commander Bothwell, who was the actual organizer of the murder and had himself prepared it. On that same night, when the explosion occurred, he had been with Mary at Dargli's, and when Mary drove off to the ball he drove back to the palace where Dargli lived.

Despite all the evidence he pretended that he knew nothing and displayed great sorrow over the calamity.

But nobody believed his hypocritical antics [?]. Bothwell was a real bandit, a reckless rogue; the only question was whether Mary together with him had prepared the devilish [?] plan.

The intimates of the murdered man took an interest in this question, and a packet of romantic letters that Mary had written to Bothwell fell into their hands.

Suspicion fell on her all the more when, barely three months after her husband's death, she married Bothwell.

Earlier, attempts had been made to prevent the match between the two. Pressure was applied from all sides, interventions by her neighbouring kingdoms, so that nothing would come of the match; but Mary declared that her love for Bothwell was so strong that she was ready to lose the sympathy of France and England and run away with her beloved to the ends of the earth in a single shift, if only she could marry Bothwell.

And she did indeed marry him. Soon after his wedding with Mary, Bothwell became the sole ruler of the kingdom; for the first time Mary Stuart became the slave of a man, instead of ruling over everyone as before, and she handed him all the power.
