Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Emor)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion; followed by an exegetical article by Hirsh Niebelski of Kielce.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Emor
The Portion
—o—
a) "And ye shall keep My commandments... and ye shall not profane My holy name" (Lev. 22:31 [printed "כר. לא."])
It turns out that even by performing commandments ("And ye shall keep My commandments") one can also desecrate God's name ("and ye shall not profane My holy name") — when one does not mean the commandments seriously, but exploits them for certain purposes... Beit Yaakov.
—o—
b) "These are My appointed seasons" (23:2)
The prophet Isaiah says: "Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hateth." When the holidays become "your feasts" — only your own holidays, and not God's and not the poor man's — then "My soul hateth". [Then] God hates them, because "these are My appointed seasons": the festivals must be God's alone and not merely yours; one must also take care of the poor man, so that he too may know of Sabbath and holiday... Orach Chaim.
—o—
c) "Neither shall they shave off the corner of their beard" (21:5)
Rabbi Eizel Charif travelled around the country with a work of his own. Once he comes to a small town and meets a maskil, a clean-shaven man, who needles him:
— Why do our rabbis keep on writing books? Are our old books too few, then?
Reb Eizel answers him:
— A Jew usually keeps the hairs of his beard in a book, and that is why so many new books are needed nowadays — because of the growing number of the clean-shaven...
* * *
The Kelmer Maggid [of Kelmė] once rebuked a group of maskilim for[?] shaving their beards. He asked them: What will you plead in the world to come?
One of the maskilim answers:
— We will answer: just as we came into the world without a beard, so we also come there without a beard...
— If so — answers the Maggid — pull out your teeth too, for you came into the world without teeth, after all...
—o—
d) "And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched corn, nor fresh ears, until this selfsame day."
We count the Omer from the day on which it became permitted to eat the new grain until the day of the Giving of the Torah.
For counting connects things, links them together, and grain and Torah belong together — "If there is no flour, there is no Torah". The Maharal of Prague.
—o—
e) "And ye shall take you on the first day."
"The first for the reckoning of sins." Tractate Sukkah.
Sukkot is called "the season of our rejoicing" — and if one begins on it to count the sins, what then is the joy in it? But the reckoning of sins is for a different purpose. Since around the Days of Awe Jews repent, and if one repents, then wilful sins turn into merits, transgressions turn into commandments; therefore one counts the sins of the Jews in order to credit them as commandments... and that is the joy. Or Yesharim.
* * *
In a similar way the Baal Shem [Tov] interprets the verse: "In that day the iniquity of the house of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none" (Jeremiah 50). Why will the sins of the Jews be sought "in that day"?
— In order to credit them as commandments... Maor va-Shemesh.
The Haftarah
—o—
f) "And they shall come near to My table, to minister unto Me, and they shall keep My charge" (Ezekiel 44)
"And they shall come near to My table" — why is it specifically the table that is mentioned?
Because the table symbolises — according to the Midrash — wealth, and that is why the table stood on the north side, for "out of the north cometh gold" [printed "צפון זהב יאתה"].
The prophet says that even those who will come to the table, to wealth, will also keep "My charge" — and this is indeed a prophecy for the future... Ahavat Yehonatan.
Avot
—o—
g) "And he who commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser" (4:13)
From every transgression — the Rebbe Reb Zusha used to say — an accuser is created, an evil angel; but I have seen these very angels that were created from the transgressions of Jews, and I saw that they are all cripples: one is without a hand, the other without a foot. For do Jews commit transgressions with their whole heart? And just as their transgressions are groaning and broken, so are the angels that are created by the transgressions... Butzina Kadisha.
—o—
Important Explanations of Today's Portion.
"Emor", chapter 21, on verse 1: "There shall none be defiled for the dead" — the Rashbam says, among other things: "For his brother and for his sister he shall not defile himself (in many Chumashim it reads "yitama") for them, and it is not said 'for them'" (in many Chumashim it reads "bahem"). The quoted passage in the Rashbam is quite incomprehensible, and it is a wonder that nobody has paid attention to it until today. In my opinion printing errors have surely crept in here, and it should read thus: "And for his brother and for his sister etc. for her he may defile himself, for them, although it is not said 'for them'". That is to say, the Rashbam joins the end of verse 2, "and for his brother", with verse 3, which he quotes in full up to "for her he may defile himself", and here he adds his own word: "for them" — stressing thereby that "for her he may defile himself" must be understood as "for them he may defile himself", although "for them" is not written, because he may defile himself not only for a sister but for all the relatives listed together.
"Emor", chapter 23, on verse 40: "And ye shall take you on the first day" — Ibn Ezra says: "And the exile from the land of Kedar to the land of Edom, if he has eyes, will know the secret of this commandment". Countless explanations have already been offered on this passage, none of which is satisfactory. In my opinion, however, Ibn Ezra is speaking here about himself; that is, he, who was driven from the land of Kedar — that is Spain — to the land of Edom — that is Italy — knows the secret of the commandment. And the words "if he has eyes" were added in later times by someone who did not understand Ibn Ezra's style and correct meaning, and afterwards it all got mixed together in the printing houses. As is known, Ibn Ezra was born and brought up in southern Spain, which in his books he always calls by the name "land of Kedar"; from there, for [certain] reasons, he fled to Italy, which he calls the land of Edom, and there he composed his commentary on the Torah.
In a similar way I also explain the passage in Ibn Ezra on the portion Acharei Mot, 16, on verse 8, where he says: "And when you are thirty-three years old you will know it". Various explanations were given on this passage many hundreds of years ago (see the commentary of Nachmanides, the responsa of the Maharam of Rothenburg, Daat Zekenim of the Tosafists, etc.). In my opinion, however, Ibn Ezra was 33 years old when he wrote these words, and he says to the young pupil or reader: when you are 33 years old like me, you too will know the secret of the scapegoat for Azazel. One quite often hears such a manner of speaking from older people to younger ones.
I hope that everyone who thinks logically and is versed in the style of our old commentators will acknowledge my explanations as the simplest and the most correct.
Hirsh Niebelski [?], Kielce.

[Der Kokh-lefl — humour, poem.] On the eve of the dacha [the summer holiday cottage].
(Dedicated to those who have already rented one, and to those who are getting "attacks" so that their husbands will go and rent one.)

It is already turning green.

It is slowly turning
green and green,
and kind mates
with kind.
The whole world becomes
a bridal bed,
a green mattress,
in pink and violet.

It is turning, oh, little people[?],
green and green.
And life acquires
a new meaning.
Now we already know
what we live for.
We live in order
to give ourselves away.

The warm[?] sun
awakens warm feelings.
Instead of hating one another,
we want to play.
(One cannot hate
on spring evenings,

We go out
[—] to the [—] wood[?],
we want to make

We are ready
to hug and to kiss

a little green blade of grass

and reaching out,

Who can still now

Who can think now
of blood and tears,

One feels like going out
into the wide streets

"Life is young,

the divine holiday

When I look up
to the eternal stars,
a hundred Hitlers
may be sent[?],

the horse-like[?] twins —

Where Does the Dacha Come From? — Scientific Discoveries

[Der Kokh-lefl — humour.] Scientific discoveries.
The dacha dates back to primeval times.
A group of married men came before the Lord of the Universe with a request. — Why, they argued, are we, Your children, worse off than all Your other creatures?
Lord of the Universe! Why have You punished us with wives, from whom we suffer more than all the other creatures, and we never have any rest from them?
So the Holy One, blessed be He, heard out the just complaint and created the dacha. Since then we men are redeemed from our troubles once a year...
Taken from a [sacred] book and retold by "Kokh-lefl".
A Little Letter to the Dollar

[Der Kokh-lefl — humour, economic crisis.] — You surely want to know, Mister Dollar, what is new with your friend [pshiatshel, Polish przyjaciel] — the złoty. Unfortunately I cannot pass on any regards from him to you — because I have not seen him for who knows[?] how long... and in general one sees him very little in the street... They say, Mister Dollar, that you have fallen under the pressure of the English pound... That is, you are sick with the English disease [rickets; a pun]. It seems to me, Mister Dollar, that falling is somehow no business, for in the end you will have to "fall in" [come to grief]...
All the young ladies [panienki], Mister Dollar, envy you your success [powodzenie], although the young men know your real age and see your greened face... and still they fall in love with you at first sight.. They, the young men, do not look at the bride at all, they only look at the dollar... That's what I call success!
Only one thing about you surprises me! You have been in America so long already, and yet you are still a "greenhorn"...
Yours, Yehuda Friedman.

Antisemitic Agitation in Germany in the 19th Century.

[History — antisemitism in 19th-century Germany; serialized article, concluding part.]
Philosophers, poets and historians take part in the agitation. — The financial crash in Germany in 1873 and the revenge on Jews for it. — The blood libel in Konitz [today Chojnice] in 1900. — Germany gives Jews rights and takes them back. — The changed situation after the year [18]70. — Further descriptions of Jewish-German relations.
By Sh. Rozenfeld.

End.
But the nearer the revolutionary year, the more boldly Jewish self-defence comes forward. And in the general German Landtag of 1847 the Prussian ministers are booed when they declare that "Jewish equal rights do not accord with the spirit of a Christian state." Even Bismarck speaks out for Jewish equal rights with only one condition: that they should not occupy such positions where "the Christian citizen would have to obey the Jewish official"...

3.
The revolution of 1848 brings Jews equal rights — but not for long. The heavily "fixed" [in quotation marks] Prussian constitution of 1850 even guarantees the Jews equal rights, but hardly has the constitution been published when a terrible agitation starts again against what had "destroyed the whole foundation of a Christian state" — and the agitation was led by a baptized Jew, Stahl [Friedrich Julius Stahl]. Other writers and scholars joined him. The air was full of theories and splinters of theories, with modern words and badly understood expressions, and everything argued that Jewish equal rights are the greatest misfortune for every Christian state. The wildest plans for how to get rid of the Jews are heard everywhere. The ministers listen to it and by circulars they order throughout the Prussian province that Jews be removed from the schools as teachers and from the courts — as judges and defence lawyers.
In the parliament of 1861 the majority expressed its protest against the ministers who had issued circulars contrary to the constitution, but the same parliament also showed how great a number of antisemites sit in parliament and express the will and the opinions of the German people. Against that one protest there were heard many, many fiery antisemitic speeches, wholly in the spirit of Stahl and his comrades.
But not only within the walls of parliament was the antisemitic talk heard, but also in the street, through literature. Books are written and daily newspapers appear, such as the "Kreuzzeitung", in which the Jew is the main subject. Besides the professors, the musicians of genius, Richard Wagner and Franz Liszt, also exerted themselves against the Jews. The former reproached the Jews that what they create in music smells of Semitism, of race; therefore their music is a misfortune for the kosher Teuton. And Liszt argued that the Jewish composer cannot express his national "I". And what Mendelssohn or Halévy wrote, a Christian composer could also have written. And because it is "nothing new", there is no need to give them equal rights [printed with a misprint]...
But despite the great all-German anti-Jewish intrigue, united Germany came and, through the Bundesrat and the Reichstag and the signature of the King — on the third of July 1869 — abolished all Jewish restrictions, and the German Jews became citizens with equal rights.
Barely a few years had passed, however, and again an antisemitic agitation against Jews began. The victory of the Germans in the Franco-German war (1870–1871) brings into Germany 5 milliard in money. The banks are full of free capital, the population begins to create various enterprises, to found various joint-stock companies. A great boom sets in; various securities and shares climb sky-high [lit. "into the world"]. People become rich overnight — a good time; but hardly had two years passed in the great tumult around the money-dust when there came a tremendous crash, as is known to us.
And who is guilty of the general crash? The Jews. And together with the Jews the government is guilty, which gave the Jews the right to trade and to swindle according to their evil will. The Jews, and with them the German liberals, are guilty of Germany's misfortune. New newspapers are created, new organizations arise and new people appear, and all together pour out their wrath and their patriotic hysteria upon the Jews. The people listen. Historians, clergymen and philosophers such as Treitschke, Stoecker and Dühring fire off the "big word", hold the most fiery speeches and write heavy books, and all this is meant to prove the worthlessness of the Jews and their depravity, and the importance [?; printed "vikhsikeyt"] of the Germans and their loftiness. And if other historians and other scholars come, like Mommsen and Virchow, and say a good word for the Jews, they are laughed at and decried. New antisemitic parties arise. They unite, crumble and gather again. Antisemitic literature grows and works and penetrates the whole people. The antisemitic party disappears only when every other party, except the Social Democratic one, is itself already permeated with the antisemitic spirit. And from now on German antisemitic literature, with its "principles" and "conditions", counts as a model for the theoretical and practical antisemitism of the whole world.
Thus the Jews enter the 20th century with curtailed rights, with injured honour, with a thick atmosphere of hatred around them and with the shadow of a blood libel (in Konitz 1900) behind them.
At the same time the German Jews fought with o n e hand for their rights and their honour; with the o t h e r hand they created a great literature of Jewish, chiefly historical, scholarship and a strong communal organization. And with b o t h hands they create and found the well-known assimilationist theory of "Germans of the Mosaic faith", which denies the national element of the Jewish people, because, they say, Jews are not a people but a religious sect within Germandom.
And the great majority of German Jewry is to this very day faithful to these theories with all their further implications.
———
And now people wonder: how can it be that the majority of the German people should hand itself over into the hands of such a scoundrel as Hitler is, and accept as good his man-eating, antisemitic methods of government? The answer is right at hand:
— An inheritance, friend reader, a sad inheritance has Germany received from her distant and recent past. An inheritance of philosophers, poets, historians, musicians and plain antisemites. A whole world could be poisoned with the fruits of the antisemitic culture that accumulated in Germany, even in the 19th century alone. In what Hitler preaches and demands now there is not a single original idea. "Everything has already been" and "there is nothing new" in the Hitlerite paradise. Even the boycott, even the "castration" that he demanded, he finds ready in the pogrom programmes of his predecessors. Even an elephant, if one stuffed it with the whole patriotic literature, would also go mad — so why should such a beast as Hitler is not go mad from it? And so indeed he did.. And there are no more wonders in the world and no more miracles. Everything has its cause. And everything has its historical-social explanation.
In the Children's World.

[Children's corner — special Lag BaOmer supplement; nature story.] A special section of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" in honour of Lag BaOmer, for our little ones. Compiled by Sh. Libas Zohn [?].

Spring in the Village.
By Mendele Moykher Sforim.

A beautiful, warm spring day. The golden sun, on rising, tore apart and scattered the big clouds in the air, and with her shining face looked down from the blue sky, gently, kindly, upon the earth. God's creatures, all of them, from great to small, shaking themselves out of the long winter sleep, have lively and merrily each set about their own business; fresh yellow flowers poke their little heads out from among the young green grass, peep out and look charming. The willows by the river hurry to put on their new green cloaks, mirroring themselves in the water — pure, clear and silver.
From the far-off warm lands, there in foreign parts, the birds come back here in flocks [?] to their rest; wild geese splash somewhere among the rushes here in the river, wild ducks whirl about the reeds, out and in, with a clamour, a twittering. Little swallows flutter, hover to and fro in the air; deeply absorbed in building, they repair new and old nests.
Welcome! The old familiar pair of storks is here too, luckily, in a good hour. She, the stork-wife, stands on one leg, her little head to one side, [still?], gazing at her old nest up on the top of a tree; and he, on his long stilts, strolls hoppingly [?] over the marsh there, looking on at a puddle where frogs jump and croak, and suddenly — peck-peck! — a snap, and into the red "Jewish" beak it goes...
There is life, joy, fluttering, buzzing, singing and twittering everywhere.
It is a holiday, it is springtime...
Daddy Is Sleeping. (A Story).

[Children's corner — story.] Etl's father is a dealer. He deals in old clothes. In the morning, when everyone is still asleep, he gets out of bed, dresses, takes his tallit and tefillin and goes to the beit midrash to pray.
When Daddy has eaten his breakfast, he takes the sack under his arm and sets off from courtyard to courtyard, calling out loud: "Handel! Handel!" [the old-clothes man's cry].
When Daddy already has a full sack of clothes, he goes off to a dealer in old goods and sells him the whole merchandise he has bought up during the day.
Towards evening Etele's father comes home very tired. He lies down to rest a little and slowly falls asleep.
Etele talks quietly and walks on tiptoe, so that Daddy will not wake from his sleep.
Etele loves her Daddy very much; every day she prays to God that Daddy should be healthy and strong and be able to support the family.

From the Jewish Legends

[Children's corner — rabbinic legends.] Collected by R.

1.
Once the government issued a decree that whoever put tefillin on his head would have his brain pierced. Now one man, Elisha, put on tefillin and went out into the market. He saw a government official, he ran away, and the other ran after him. When the other caught him, Elisha quickly took the tefillin off his head and held them in his hands. The official asks him: What have you got in your hands? Elisha answers him: — Dove's wings!
Elisha opened his hands, and indeed dove's wings were found there.
From then on he was called: "Elisha, the man of the wings."

2.
Rabbah bar bar Hana was once travelling with a caravan of Arabs; he ate, and forgot to say grace on the spot.
When the caravan had already gone some way, Rabbah bar bar Hana remembered that he had not said grace. He thinks to himself: What is to be done? If I tell the Arabs that I forgot to say grace and therefore want to go back to say it at the place where I ate, as Jewish law requires, they won't want to wait for me. They will say: Say grace here — it will reach God from anywhere. Better I shall say: Wait for me, because I forgot a golden dove at that place.
Rabbah bar bar Hana went back and said grace at the place where he had eaten, and found a golden dove there.
Good Qualities Befit Learning (from the Midrash)

[Children's corner — a parable from the Midrash.] A rich man once boasted to his friend that his wealth was very great:
— I have a thousand sacks of grain, a thousand jars of olive oil and a thousand barrels of wine.
His friend remarked to him:
— Do you have storehouses for all of this, to put each thing away in a safe place so that it will be preserved?
If you have room for all your wealth — he went on to tell the rich man — it belongs to you entirely. But if not, you own nothing, and the wind will carry off all your riches.
So it is when a person has learned much and is laden with much knowledge and Torah; one says to him:
— Do you also have good manners besides? Then the whole Torah belongs to you; but if not, you own nothing and your knowledge is going to be lost.
Every learned man who has good qualities in him is like a tree that is firmly rooted in the earth. And even if the strongest storm-winds come, they will not be able to move it from its place. Its leaves will always be green and it will not cease to bear fruit.
Będzin: Stormy annual meeting of the "Gemilut Hesed" loan fund

[Będzin — public institutions / the Gemilut Hesed loan fund.]
[Section heading:] What's new in Zagłębie? — Friday, 16 Iyar 5693 / piątek 12 maja 1933 [Friday, 12 May 1933].
Będzin
The agitation for the meeting was conducted under the slogan "Judaism is in danger".
On Sunday the annual meeting of the members of the Gemilut Hesed (G"H, interest-free loan) fund of our town took place in the hall of the "Merchants' Association" (Sokhrim-Fareyn). Interest in the meeting was the same as in the election campaign for the first kehilla elections. Already several days before, the "little Jewish world" had been boiling like a cauldron. Factions of every kind racked their brains over composing the lists of candidates. Every day brought new conceptions and new "cabinet crises". Besides that, a recruiting drive was conducted among the members. Every side mobilised its forces, if only to prevent a victory of the "enemy" who wants to "grab the bank"...
On the Sabbath agitation was carried on in the Hasidic "shtiblekh" that everyone who wants "the sinners not to grab the bank, so that a Sabbath-observer can get a loan — should come to the meeting and save Judaism".
It goes without saying that the agitation had the proper success, and such a number of members came as no society has yet been privileged to see... Both halls of the "Merchants' Association" were packed full, and very many more remained outside, unable to get in any more.
The mood in the hall — a tense one; the "air" smells of gunpowder, the smallest "spark" can cause an explosion, but "the devil is not as terrible as he is painted". The meeting was nevertheless carried through to the end, with small incidents.
———
The meeting is opened by the chairman, Mr. L. Rubinlicht. The chair is handed over to Mr. M. Gold, who invites to the presidium Messrs. A. Lidubarski [Lidzbarski?], L. Strobel, and as secretary — Mr. Żmucki[?].
After the reading of the minutes of the last general meeting, a series of formal proposals of the board concerning changes to the statute are considered. Among the changes is also the paragraph on the term of office of the board. According to a circular (okólnik) of the "Joint" the board is elected for 3 years. Those assembled, seeing[?] a "danger" in the change, rejected this change too...
Around the proposals a discussion develops that leads to absurdities. The "speakers" do not grasp the actual question, they voice such opinions as cause tempers to become even more heated, and during the "votes" shouting is heard as at a mass rally..
Then come the reports: the treasury report — Mr. Montag; the audit committee — Mr. Herciger; and on the activity — the chairman Mr. Rubinlicht, who speaks of the importance of the fund at the present moment, when a decline prevails in the financial institutions. In the course of 14 months — says Mr. Rubinlicht — the outgoing board issued 738 loans for a sum of 144 thousand zł. Such a sum was also collected back, together with another 29 thousand zł. of old outstanding debts.
The outgoing board does not stop short of the most far-reaching measures against debtors. 103 borrowers are in court and 59 already with the komornik [bailiff]. Mr. Rubinlicht censures the former management, which caused losses of a good many thousands of zł. out of the collected people's pennies...
On the motion of the writer of these lines a protest resolution against the persecution of the Jews in Germany was adopted.
After the reports the "real" discussion only begins, in which "whatever anyone had on his heart, he spoke out". Among the criticism was also the "injustice" that in the presidium "religious Jewry is not represented", that the members of the presidium go bareheaded... and that Mr. Montag with his partners from the "Światowid" cinema do not want to pay the "pauszeczka" [lump-sum fee]...
Mr. Feigenblat censures the activity of the board so far; he expresses himself negatively about the reports given and proposes that a committee be elected to carry out a precise audit of the books and only then publish an exact report in the press. Mr. Feigenblat criticises the board for increasing the administrative expenses at a time when reductions are being made everywhere.
Mr. Rosenberg speaks out against the fact that a member from the popular masses can be granted a loan only after 8 months.
Also speaking are Messrs. Aharon Berenblat, Tenenbaum, Herzberg, Baruch, Herszlewicz, Kartusz and others, and after the reply of Mr. Rubinlicht and Mr. Liwer[?] the old board is granted an absolutorium (discharge).
The budget ("budoshet") for a sum of 18,320 zł. is passed on to the new board.
— Elections! Elections! The word simply electrified those assembled. In the name of "strengthening the faith" (khizek ha-das) Jews sacrificed themselves and with awe and love (bi-dekhilu u-rekhimu) campaigned for the "kosher candidates"...
About 220 men took part in the elections, and the results are as follows:
L. Bauszykowski[?], L. Rubinlicht, J. Goldfeler, A. D. Balimowski, M. M. Janowski, J. Wygodzki[?], M. Rozencaft[?], A. L. Grünwald, M. Hampel, Z. Lemberg, J. M. Kurland, A. M. Szwarcbaum, J. Rozinker[?], Ch. Braner, A. Frachcwajg.
As we are informed, a larger number of members have submitted a protest: 1) to the chairman of the general meeting, 2) to the outgoing chairman Mr. Rubinlicht and 3) to the Joint. The protest points out that 1) persons without the right to vote took part in the elections, and 2) people have entered the new board — undesirable elements who may undermine the authority of the institution.
A forest guard beats young Jews from Będzin murderously.

Two young men from Będzin went for a walk in the Grodziec forest; there they were met by the forest guard, who demanded of them a fine of 25 zł. each for walking along the forest road. The beaten young men went to the police duty office [?], where a report was drawn up about it, and the hooligan guard is being handed over to criminal justice.

Sosnowiec
"That's for the wrong you did my mother".
Epilogue of a family drama before the local district court.

In its time the family drama that happened in the Brandes family made a great impression among the Jewish population.
On 14 September 1932, at 3 in the afternoon, several revolver shots were heard from a house on Pusta Street in Pogoń. Soon afterwards a young man ran out of the house holding a revolver in his hand.
The young man ran to the police station, where, on coming in, he cried out:
— I've killed!
Later it turned out that the victim of the family tragedy was the 33-year-old Tauba Schwarz, who rented an apartment in that house on the second floor, and whose lover was Mr. Sz. Brandes of Sosnowiec.
Eight years ago Miss Schwarz had been taken on as a servant by the Brandes family. In the course of time close relations developed between her and Mr. Brandes, until it went so far that Brandes abandoned his wife and children and settled with his beloved in Częstochowa.
Because of his poor financial affairs he later came back with the "sweetheart" ("kochanka") to Sosnowiec, where he rented an apartment on Pusta Street, where the tragedy took place.
On that critical day the elder son of Brandes came into the apartment of his father's beloved and, crying out: "That's for the wrong done to my mother", fired 3 times and wounded her seriously.
The epilogue of the family drama took place before the local district court. After hearing the witnesses the court pronounced the verdict, according to which Brandes is sentenced to 4 years' prison.

[Law — answers to readers.] Mrs. R. A. — You can go to court and demand the release of your belongings from the execution (distraint) on the basis of your intercyza [marriage property settlement]. Mr. Leuer [probably “Leser”, reader] K. — You can demand an eviction, because handing over bills of exchange for rent without redeeming the bills does not mean that the rent has been paid; it is only a prolongation.

Mr. “Official” — As you write, your working hours were not exactly fixed; you therefore have weak chances of winning the lawsuit over overtime, since you yourself disposed of your time.
Mr. “Merchant G.” — Under the present practice of the courts the date on which the cheque was issued is of no importance; it is enough that it had no cover on the payment date.
Mr. “Landlord” — If the tenant demanded that you cover the old rent with the money he sent, you cannot credit it against the current rent.
R. R.

„Cry out for help, so that the whole world will hear!“

An escaped Jew tells of the terrible tortures of Jews in Germany.
These days a Jew from Germany came here, with whom the writer of these lines had a conversation about the situation of the Jews in Germany. For understandable reasons we do not give his name or the place where he lived.
— What the newspapers write about Germany — our informant begins — cannot yet be compared to what is happening in reality. I will tell you only — he says — one of the hundreds of facts, and you will already have an idea of what the Jewish situation looks like.
In a certain town a group of Hitlerites entered[?] the home of a menaker [a porger, who removes forbidden veins and fat from meat] at the moment when he was wrapped in tallit and tefillin and praying. For this „sin“ he was arrested, and in a closed carriage (where on the way he was beaten murderously) he was taken off to the so-called „Green House“.
In the „Green House“ he was forced to stand bent double, and the wild beasts in human form beat him with rubber truncheons braided with wire.
When the menaker collapsed to the ground from the great pain, as punishment they stripped him naked, laid him face down on a long table, and after binding his head with the tallit they began — to beat him with large rubber truncheons on his naked body.
When the menaker lost consciousness, the beasts poured water over him and revived him in order to continue further bestial deeds.
Then the beasts poured salt into the deep raw wounds on his naked body and afterwards pressed the salt into the open wounds with pieces of wood.
After the inquisitorial tortures the Jew, who was writhing in agony, was thrown like a dog into another room, where he lay ill for several months.
German Jews — says the informant — are afraid to utter a word, but the Jewish press must tell the truth and „cry out for help, so that the whole world will hear“.

L.O.P.P. Celebrations in Zagłębie

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — air defence; kehilla.]
On Sunday the celebrations in honour of the 10th anniversary of the L.O.P.P. [Air and Anti-Gas Defence League] began. The celebrations opened with divine services and parades.
In Będzin a number of organisations and the school youth took part in the parade, with their orchestras at the head.
Great interest was aroused in Będzin on Sunday by the attraction of a gas attack on the town.
Already at 2 o'clock in the afternoon the L.O.P.P. detachments with their gas masks began to gather on the "Sokół square".
At the same time the gases were released. The buildings of the Starostwo and the Sejmik were covered with clouds of smoke and heavy shooting was heard. It was said that the enemy's aeroplanes were being fired upon.
At the signal of the "siren" the firemen also arrived at the Starostwo building and began spraying water.
First aid of the "Red Cross" stood ready.
In connection with the jubilee, on Tuesday evening, a consultation of the kehilla representatives took place in the premises of the Sosnowiec kehilla, with the participation of the chairman of the L.O.P.P. committee in Sosnowiec, Karamanik [?], and Mr. [?] Elster, who lectured on the great importance of supporting the campaign for the benefit of the L.O.P.P.

A Letter from Bystra

[Bystra — summer resort; letter.]
Bystra, which is known as the most beautiful area in the Beskids, is, thanks to its mild mountain air, recommended as a health resort for everyone, especially for convalescents who have gone through serious and light illnesses.
The local council in Bystra has lately been endeavouring to install various amenities for the guests staying here during the summer-holiday season. Besides the library that has existed until now, a library has also been opened which is supplied with the newest literature, for a minimal fee.
On the promenades the number of benches has been increased, so that the guests can rest.
There is also a cinema, a confectionery where dances are held, and Jewish guesthouses, among which the guesthouse of Mrs. Frenkel has made a name for itself among the Jewish intelligentsia.
The local population is very quiet. At the times when in some places disturbances took place on the part of the local inhabitants, Bystra was an exception in this respect, because the local population does not concern itself with "political" matters.
A considerable improvement as regards travel has also come about with the new timetable.
Ger ve-Toshav ["Stranger and Resident" — pen name].

"We Jews Swear!"

[Czechoslovakia — boycott of German goods.]
How Czech Jews are conducting the boycott against German goods.
We give an appeal to the Jews of Prague, which reads as follows: "We Jews swear"! Until full redress of the wrong that has been done to the German Jews and of the insult that has been inflicted on the whole of Jewry:
1) To travel to Germany only in case of the greatest necessity.
2) Not to buy any goods in Germany.
3) Not to use at all any German products.
4) Not to travel on any German ships and not to ship goods on them.
5) Not to insure ourselves even with the safest German insurance companies.
6) To copy this out and pass it on to acquaintances.
Jews, prove that you have character!

Thus, thanks to the przodownik [police sergeant] [?] together with the policeman Mr. Karch [?], the pogrom atmosphere was liquidated.
Afterwards a commission headed by the starosta came here in order to investigate the matter.
Zecharit [?] Esprajcher.

Protest meeting against the book-burnings in Germany.

Rabbi Dr. Chameides gave a long speech rich in content, in which he said among other things "that it is simply a disgrace for a cultured person to use the language of that barbaric nation.

The help of the Katowice Jews for the Jewish refugees from Germany.
The Katowice Jewish community convened a conference of all 16 Jewish communities, which are united in the general relief committee to help the Jewish refugees from Germany.
According to the report given by the vice-president of the Jewish community in Katowice, Dr. Abrahamer, there are about 200 fugitives in Upper Silesia, most of them people who had lived in Germany for 20–30 years. Before they managed to escape from the Hitlerite hell they had to endure cruel torments: they were beaten, tortured, and [suffered] various other sufferings and pains.
At the conference it was resolved to take practical steps to help the unfortunate refugees. Relief actions are being organised in all the communities and are meeting with due success.
The "B'nai B'rith Lodge" in Katowice has placed its premises at the committee's disposal, and a reading room for the refugees has been set up there. Jewish doctors and lawyers have declared that they will give them free medical and legal help.

A disaster in a coal mine in Siemianowice.
In a coal mine in Siemianowice lumps of coal and earth broke loose and buried three workers.
After a rescue action that lasted several hours, they only managed to bring one of them out, without any sign of life.
Heart-rending scenes are taking place at the site of the accident among the close relatives of the victims.

New dismissals.
This week the management of "Królewska Huta" announced that new reductions of workers will be made.
The voivode intervened so that the reduction plan be withdrawn.

Official of the starosty shoots his wife.
Cybel, 36, a clerk (referent) at the starosty in Bielsko, shot his wife dead.
Cybel came home at 5 in the morning from a binge; when his wife reproached him for it, he snatched out his Browning and shot her dead.
The murderer has been arrested.

In Katowice the police arrested one Szulim Himmelsztaub of Warsaw, who had been wanted by the police for a long time. The arrested man is an international swindler.

A child run over and killed.
Eight-year-old Getrura [?] Palka, while running across from one street to another in Katowice, was run over by a cart. The girl was killed on the spot.

While several sacks of money were being carried from the train to the mail van in Rybnik, a sack containing 28,570 zł. disappeared. In this connection several officials have been arrested on whom suspicion of the theft rests.
