The "Success" of the Gemilut Chesed Fund.

[Będzin — institutions and community; editorial.]
(What is good with others is bad with us. — May one allow it to come to catastrophe?)
With us it is always different from all other peoples. We have to conduct ourselves in a different way from other people. What can one do, what can one make of it — it is already such a lost cause, and every word, every effort is a waste.
Against what are we saying this? Against what has come to be talked about [?] — precisely against the general meeting of the "Gemilut Chesed" [interest-free loan] fund, which has just [?] taken place in Będzin. Among other people it is an accepted rule that where there is interest there is life, and life awakens and develops and progresses; thus, in this way, the institution grows and "must" [?] the fruits it brings in the public sphere. But when there is [n]o interest, when the general meetings are held with a [mini]mum of people, it is a sign that there is [n]o interest, and then one sees no life; thus [—] in this case the institution does not stand at the proper height and consequently does not bring the desired benefit to the community, to the society it is meant to serve.
Yes, that is how it is with other people, that is how it should be, and that is understandable. But with us it is quite different: with us it must be different from all other peoples; with us one cannot measure anything at all by common sense — on the contrary, it always turns out different from what logic dictates to us. With us, when a general meeting of whatever public institution takes place, one should actually pray that it be held behind closed doors, among a minyan of people, and that it arouse no interest whatsoever in anyone. As soon as it is otherwise — as soon as people begin to take an interest in the institution, as soon as they come to a general meeting, which is a sign that there is life, that there is interest in our life — our interest is, unfortunately, never used for the good of the community, for the best of society, but only to destroy, to bury, to suppress what exists, what is beginning to live and develop. Yes, that is how it is with us, unfortunately. We see it every time, and on every occasion we have to record it.
It is therefore nonsense when people complain here that this or that general meeting aroused no interest among the broad strata of the population, and that the meeting had to take place with barely a minyan of people. From now on we must adopt a rule: that it is good so, that the fewer people come, the less interest it arouses, the better; and from today on let us not complain that it is not good when the community takes no interest, when society stands aloof. This coldness, this frozenness, this indifference is a sign that it is good so, that it could not be better, and that we cannot demand more of society.
The last general meeting of the "Gemilut Chesed" fund aroused enormous interest. Everyone came, young and old, and there was an uproar on the table and on the benches. A blind mass came, and 90 per cent did not know what to demand or what was going on at all. The whole business consisted only in Shmerl saying the opposite of what Berl wants. One could hear people talking without rhyme or reason, without knowing what they actually wanted; one saw that these were creatures who had been wound up, and that they need do no more than act differently from what the other wants, and speak differently. Nothing did they want to understand with reason, and they did not want to make the effort to understand. That is the worst of it. We understand when people come because the institution is dear to them, because it is an ideal of theirs. We understand when people come to help develop the institution, when they come to rescue it, when one sees that it faces a catastrophe. But it is quite different when people come to fight, when they come to wage war, when they set out to turn a philanthropic financial institution into a party grocery-shop, and everyone wants to have that little shop in his own pocket. That is when, here, people come to a general meeting — that is when interest is aroused. Working for the sake of politics — by all means, all the more so; working for the sake of an ideal, for its own sake — that, no. That is a matter for idlers, for loafers. So when it comes to burying an institution, people get up on their feet, and it becomes a kind of holy work for which one must sacrifice oneself and bring offerings. Let the institution go to ruin — that doesn't matter either, as long as obstinacy carries the day, as long as Shmerl defeats Berl. And we know, after all, that just as people here are indifferent and apathetic towards practical work, just so are they productive and energetic when it comes to pursuing a policy of destruction. At such a moment you will find out everything; all secrets will then be revealed, everyone will then tell about various "good deeds". That is how far [printed: "how high"] lies and hypocrisy have gone. It would have been quite different had the truth taken the place of honour.
Why then — the question arises — should one learn of illegal acts only when people quarrel? Why should one not learn of such matters before they are carried out? After all, a Gemilut Chesed fund is not a private enterprise, and as a public institution nothing may be concealed in it that causes or can cause harm. In a public institution — let alone one that deals with financial matters — one may not let a single [—] [?] fall, and if something undesirable does arise, one may not make a secret of it; it must be uncovered at once, so as to uproot it before the situation becomes contagious, chronic.
Were not the Jewish banking institutions destroyed in just this way? People wanted to cover up everything, to veil everything, so that public opinion, God forbid, should learn nothing — and meanwhile. Meanwhile the air was poisoned behind closed doors, and there people not only did not want to save, not only did not want to improve, but on the contrary: knowing that the mass knew nothing, they committed fresh embezzlements and illegal acts; what should never have been allowed, they allowed — and so they broke the neck, and we lost one bank after another.
The banking institutions were buried in such a scandalous way that today no merchant has a public bank where he could get a bill of exchange discounted; now the middle class has become so impoverished that it must turn to a Gemilut Chesed fund, the only such institution in town. And the question arises: can we afford such a luxury? Can one now pursue a policy of destruction in order to remove this necessary institution from the Jewish street? Do responsible people realise what a catastrophe that would be for the town? And that they have set out on this path — one can see with one's own eyes.
Possibly many will say that the devil is not as frightening as we paint him, that things are not at all so catastrophic and the fear is groundless. To this, however, one must answer that we must already now look with open eyes, and looking thus, not wanting to fool ourselves, one foresees the catastrophe at its very beginning; for one can save only while it is still early, while it is not yet dangerous; but later, once it has entered the great "gedulos" [?], there is nothing left to save: then the whole body is already sick, and with the best will, with the greatest efforts, the catastrophe must come.
An institution is exactly like a building, like a house, which must be looked after and kept in order; if one does not do so, it becomes neglected. Of course the passer-by, the casual visitor, the stranger will not [see] the neglect; but it is worse when the innermost insider too does not want to see it and imagines that it will always look the same. That is the element that fools itself and thinks it is fooling the other. Meanwhile one brick after another begins to fall, and then people set about repairs — but by then it is too late: everything is already rotten through and full of holes, and there is nothing left to save.
If one wants to repair defects, it must be done at the very beginning, and one must not wait until the bricks start falling on one's head and one hole becomes bigger than the next; for such repairs one would then need too much strength, and as usual by then people are exhausted and have no possibility of restoring the building or the institution to the level at which it formerly stood.
Exactly the same happened with our financial institutions: when they could have been saved, a policy of extermination was pursued, and later, when everything was already rotten, people set about saving them — but then it was already too late and nothing could succeed. Had people become intensive and devoted at the very beginning, what was necessary for the rescue would no doubt have succeeded.
The same now holds for the Gemilut Chesed fund: it is a rescue institution, and its situation now is such that it must be rescued, and this must be done while there is still time, while the body is not yet rotten through.
Let people take account of all this, let them reckon the consequences that quarrels and back-alley politics can bring, let them take all this into consideration, let them be sincere and not allow this necessary institution to be brought to ruin — which would be a misfortune for the town — and those who led it astray would have to be branded as criminals.
R. Let.
Between Ourselves.

(Letter to a friend).

Third letter.

My dear friend!
The Endeks [Polish National Democrats] argue: how can the Jews be good Polish citizens if they do not want to break the habit of speaking Yiddish, which is after all nothing but a German jargon?

I am ready[?] to bet the richest Endek, ten to one, that even if we were all to speak like Słonimskis and Tuwims [Antoni Słonimski and Julian Tuwim, Polish poets of Jewish origin] and talk in the language of the "Wiadom. Literackie" [Wiadomości Literackie, the Warsaw literary weekly], it is precisely then that they would raise a cry to heaven that we are Judaizing the Polish language.

And why bet, when I have a living witness: Hitler's charge in Germany against our Heines and Börnes [Heinrich Heine and Ludwig Börne]!

And as for the Germanness of Yiddish — that is a genuine gentile's error.

Just now, walking in the street, I caught a Yiddish phrase: "ikh vel aykh zogn" [I'll tell you], and in German it would be: "ich werde Ihnen sagen"; but in the [—] case it came out as "glaykh [—]", and in German it comes out "bish[—]" — a fine[?] resemblance!

Certainly "table" and "house" and "chair" and "eat" and "drink" and "sleep" and similar homely everyday notions resemble each other in both languages; but if so, then Polish also resembles Russian, since both stem from one Slavic source, and "table" and "chair" and "eat" and "drink" and "sleep" and "man" and "God" and "angel" and "devil" and "paradise" and "hell" are exactly the same — a far greater resemblance than between Jews[?] and German!

When people here were expecting the German occupation any day [1915], the half-assimilated, Russified Jews laughed at us Yiddishists. Here comes the German — they said — and your Yiddish will vanish like smoke. You will turn "dos" into "das", "foter" into "Vater", "morgn" into "moyen"[?] — and you will become real Germans.

And how did it turn out?

Everyone surely remembers that it was precisely with the German that the Yiddish movement grew a hundredfold stronger. Why? Partly because of the freedom that came — there was no Hitler then — and above all precisely because only on coming closer to the German did people become convinced that Yiddish and German are two separate languages, that the German does not understand Yiddish and the Jew does not understand German.

And how is one to understand it? That apart from a few hundred ordinary everyday words, the two languages have gone their separate ways, as far apart as the Euphrates from the Tigris, since[?] they came out of one corner in the Book of Genesis.

For perhaps 40 per cent of our roots are Hebraic and Slavic and Romance and Latin-Greek; in the conjugations and declensions they are as far apart as east from west, and the sentence structure — God save us! Which Jew can get through even one single ten-storey German period without breaking his teeth!

No, Yiddish is not German.

Three hundred years ago a Yiddish word was indeed a German word; but once upon a time the Poles and the Russians also spoke almost one language! What didn't once exist!?

There remains now another question: what do we need our own language for at all? Why irritate the ear of the town citizen with our otherness? We demand equality, after all — so why don't we make ourselves equal?

Well, the question is no question at all. Because a language is a matter of primary necessity. If a man were alone in the world, a kind of Robinson Crusoe, he could spare himself the art of speech entirely, because he would have no one to talk to. But when two people live together, instead of making themselves understood with gestures and grimaces, they make it easier with the mouth, through words. Now, since I live among Jews, since father and mother speak Yiddish, the shopkeeper woman speaks Yiddish, the shammes in the synagogue and the broker in the street and [?] the newspaper-seller and the life-insurance agent all speak Yiddish — I will hardly be a madman and suddenly start speaking Polish to them?

You will ask, then: why must we sit together in one Jewish gang? Why not spread out, one Jew among ten gentiles, and really speak the language of the surroundings?

Well, first of all one would have had to settle a couple of million Jews in the villages among the twenty million gentile peasants. Surely that would not have pleased our Endek friends. And in town, too, one would have had to place a few Jews among the policemen — I do not mean that two policemen should lead one Jew to the lock-up, but that among ten policemen one should be a Jew; among ten post officials and finance officials and komorniks [bailiffs] and notaries, and in the starostwo [county office] and in the voivodship office and in the officer corps, always one in ten should be a Jew. For myself I would pick a modest post of vice-commissioner in a sick fund, and perhaps I would be a feuilleton writer on a Polish newspaper, like some Słonimski or a Julian Sokołow [so printed].

But when I sit in the synagogue courtyard, where the paving stones speak Yiddish, how can I suddenly start speaking another language?

And to come back to the point: even if all the miracles happened and the handful of little Jews in Poland were scattered, spread out over all the corners and nooks of the country — we already have an example in the German Jews, for whom the miracle really did happen, and now they must learn Yiddish in Paris[?] on the Pletzl and Hebrew in Tel Aviv!

Meaning that no Jew in the world is insured against wandering one day into a Jewish alley, where he will have to pray minchah with a congregation and join in the "Kedushah" with a genuine Jewish tune.

And then that bit of Yiddish will come in very handy.

A. Gum.
Our Cry to the World — Let Us Root Ourselves in the Mother-Earth!

[Article — the catastrophe of German Jewry; the words of Dr. Chaim Zhitlowsky.] Dr. Chaim Zhitlowsky reacted to the misfortune of the Jews in Germany in his own profound and original way, in an article.
He repeats his old idea that one must repair the roof not only when the "house is burning"; that Jewish society must apply its entire energy in this direction — that the Jewish people should stand with both feet on the ground, "root itself in the mother-earth", so that no storm whatsoever could tear it out from there. He asks:
"Why have we not done this until now? Why are we not doing it now and do not want to think about it at all? To this there is, in my opinion, yet another sufficient excuse: because we have lived the whole time — and still live to this day — with illusions. With the illusion of a supernatural, divine redemption.
Later, when doubts began to tear apart [?] every illusion, the second one came about: the illusion of general human progress, of universal human justice, which will be poured out equally on us as on individual human beings — the illusion of Jewish "equal rights".
And when this illusion too began to totter, the third illusion sprang up: Eretz Israel, to which we will, as Herzl believed, transplant the Jewish communities of the entire world.
"Now we live, thank God, with all three illusions together. The largest part hopes: God will help! Fasts! "Repentance, prayer and charity"! Another part does not stop banging the cymbals and drums: "See how Eretz Israel is blooming! See what a radiant paradise is there, and see what a dark hell the lands of exile are"! And a third part, which knows that in that radiant paradise there is no room for all who need it — and because that part sees the heavy storm-clouds gathering over our heads everywhere, they warm up the formerly already half-frozen illusion of equal rights, let it boil up to steam-heat, and clamour once again, as in the forties of the last century: "Justice for every human being! Equal rights for Jews"!
"With that we may perhaps be able to prop up a little wagon, but what can we expect from it more than that [?] we can attain — even in Germany, and even if all four points of the American Jewish Congress were officially adopted — at most such a state as in Poland... What do you say about our Poland? Take it: the Polish government forbids by law all antisemitic organizations! Does one need a still nobler, still finer, still more conspicuous display of "justice toward Jews"? And — who will now still be so naive as to believe that this can improve our situation in Poland even by a hair? One can strangle and throttle us everywhere in good, kosher legality.
"So [?] — shall we stop having grievances against the non-Jewish world? No, nobody says that. No, not stop! Our human rights must not be touched. That claim we shall never give up; for it we shall always have to fight.
"But if we have still other grievances against the non-Jewish world, we shall be able to settle them with it only [?] then, when we can already stand on our own feet, when we are already so rooted in the mother-earth that no storm-wind can carry us away from it, that no downpour and no hail can break open [?] the roof over our heads. Only when we also become socio-economically equal to all other normal peoples will we be able, as equal peoples, to begin settling our international accounts.
"For this, however, we must first of all free ourselves from the three illusions. We must stop believing that in one of them, or in all three of them [?], could lie the answer to our [?] tragic problem.
"Only one claim, one demand can we now have toward the non-Jewish world, when we now hold under its nose the whole list of great men: the Heines and Börnes, with the Bergsons and the Einsteins, etc., etc., etc. — with this very list we can prove only one thing: that we are a people of culture blessed with very lofty cultural creative powers. We demand, we require, we beg: help us stand on our own feet; as a people, help us root ourselves in the mother-earth. Then your eyes too will be able to see clearly their greatness [?], and they will not be "too great in your eyes"!
"This is what should have been our cry to the world."
Notes of the Times. A Jewish Janitor...

A Jewish janitor... a Jewish janitor — it sounds like the song "Raisins and Almonds". Mothers will lull their children to sleep with it, grown-ups dream about it; it is an ideal, an unmistakable sign of civil and political equality. Who until now has had the privilege of becoming a Jewish janitor?

Jews have always striven to make their children into great scholars; they hired the best melamdim, the best teachers, went without enough food, without enough sleep, just to make something worthwhile of the children — and "something worthwhile" meant a doctor, a lawyer, an engineer, or, if it had to be less, at least a teacher, a bookkeeper. But a janitor? Upon my life, a joke! Had a Jew told his neighbour that he was thinking of making his child into a decent person and wanted to get him a post as janitor, people would have looked at the Jew with frightened eyes: had he perhaps gone soft in the head? A janitor, of all things!

And yet we have lived to see a time when the janitor's post beckons to many and enchants like a will-o'-the-wisp[?]. It's no small thing to be a janitor! Say, for instance, in So-and-so's house on Małachowskiego Street, with its large number of tenants — that is a sure livelihood, if not an ample one, and all without distraint officers, promissory notes, bailiffs (komorniks) and all the other "goodies" of the Jewish trading business.

Which Jew is granted that privilege straight away, and which Jewish landlord will go so far as to make the sacrifice of taking on a Moshe, a Shlomo or a Chaim as janitor? He will simply be unable, out of grief, to sit down to his midday meal when, looking out of the window, he sees that Shlomo, or Moshe, or Chaim — that same Jew who only recently dealt in textiles, or drilled pupils in a cheder, or even ground a barrel-organ with a descant — holding a broom in his hand, dressed in a blue apron just like Wojtek[?], and sweeping the street?

A Jewish janitor? It's only easy to say. It is a remarkably lofty ideal; it is the "And it shall come to pass in the end of days" of Jewish equality. When the time comes that Jewish landlords truly begin to feel heartache for their Jewish tenants who sit without a livelihood, and their hearts stop aching at the thought that So-and-so son of So-and-so, poor fellow, a man of good family, "a Jewish mensch", should stand with a broom in his hand and sweep the street — then a Jewish janitor will no longer be "music of the future". Then we will only have to wage, so to speak, the "political and national struggle" for the Jewish janitor; but among ourselves we will have settled it.

Today it is a matter of "raisins and almonds". Today only one side dreams of it — Jewish fathers without a livelihood, with a dozen little mouths pecking[?] at home.

A Jewish janitor!
A Jewish janitor...
What a beautiful illusion...

Moshe Mechuyav.
Rented a Dacha. (A Little Feuilleton).

Calmly, quietly, not at all as usual every year after Passover, my "missus" says to me these days:

— Well. Thank God, it's already after Lag ba-Omer — what's going to be this year with a little dacha?

At the words "a little dacha" I feel warm at heart: evidently, I think, she is adapting to the hard times and no longer demands grand things of me, just some dacha or other.

A difference of opinion develops between us: she says that since the rich will not travel this year to the Hitler-German spas, it will consequently be crowded even in our homely summer resorts, and one will have to[?] pay high prices because of them; therefore it is better to rent a dacha as early as possible.

I am against[?] this assumption: I have no faith in a boycott by the rich, I say; you see, the local Boycott Committee is working with all its strength to boycott all goods from the Hitlerite state, and still there are persons who pay no heed to it — like that one, for instance, who just bought a whole consignment of German goods.

— From such cases[?] — one draws no proof! — mine answers convincingly.

I don't want to give in, and I concede that in general the rich, or the formerly rich, will take their "cure" this year in other, friendly towns — there are still, thank God, other similar places for them to travel to — so there is no reason to fear inflated prices.

— All right, rent or don't rent — mine is already getting angry — but a flat we may surely rent; it is some kind of summer life, isn't it?...

So I have no choice, and alas[?]...

In the clean air of Będzin there floats, it seems, a "Teutonic"[?] spectre of gloom and melancholy, which the Hitlerite epidemic has carried over here — Jews have lost heart, the [—] are not renting anything to do something for their health, to enjoy the beauty of nature; very small is the number of those wishing to rent dachas.

The dacha owners, too, have changed their tune, forgotten the former salty prices, and ask much less.

There stands the owner with a Jew who has come to rent a dacha from him; the Jew offers a "price of the times"[?], and the Christian explains to him that even last year he took more for that same dacha.

The Jew bursts out: what are you comparing it to last year for? Back then Hitler was not yet chancellor, and today you read in the papers what a murderer he is! What terrible murders he commits against Jews!

— Yes, I've read it, word of honour, I've read it — he really is a true bandit (rozbójnik) — and the Christian, a simple-hearted man, sends three-storey curses to Hitler's address.

— But you are Jews, a clever people — the Christian goes on consoling him — you outlive your enemies; in Tsarist Russia you had many foes and you outlived them all; just so you will live to see Hitler's downfall too!

I agreed with this conclusion and gave a few złoty as a deposit on a dacha.

Mazel tov!

Yitzchak Chen.
Among Trees and Grass.

(From a Lag ba-Omer outing to Wojkowice) — by S. Libaszon [?].
Out into the field.
A Lag ba-Omer call. Out into free nature. Far from the city hubbub. On that day especially I badly wanted to run away somewhere, baraj [?] into the Mountains of Darkness, to become a primeval man and find myself cut off from the
— "civilized world"...
• • •
Lag ba-Omer of old.
The rebbe went out with us to the field behind the town. Every boy was "armed" with a bow and arrows, with which we waged the "war"; none of us was wounded; just for fun we got the rebbe's permission
— in honour of Lag ba-Omer.
Last Sunday they also showed us, the town dwellers, a "mock war" [an air-defence drill], but there is no comparison. That joke chills the blood in the veins; the yellow clouds of smoke frighten so terribly and announce that there are coming
— bloody times...
• • •
After an hour of dragging along behind "grandpa's" old nag, we finally reach the forest.
The Christian coachman, whom we never stop asking
— is it still far? — comforts us, and with his whip he points out to us the fluttering blue-and-white flag of the Będzin "Hakoach".
• • •
On entering the forest I began to search.
I looked for: the heads of the music section and of the board of "Hakoach", the members of the Keren Kayemet committee in Będzin, the Zionist and national public figures, and in the end
— I did not find a single one of them...
I also [—] looked for someone, I looked for
— the forest... For my mind could not grasp why the outing had to take place ansh [?] 12 kilometres from town: such "natural treasures" can be found even at our "Arimkes" [?] and in natural areas — found nearer than Wojkowice Kościelne...
• • •
A buzzing, a din, a mixture of voices, a mixture of languages; one gets the impression of being at an international Eastern Fair.
— "A glass of kvass for groszy!" — the soda-water sellers make the air ring; they have to shout loudly so that their voices reach the buyers, because there is no lack of parties here, nor of dancing girls; and when "Gordonia" sings and dances "Kadima", the Betar boys and girls shout even louder and stronger
— "Long live Jabotinsky" [Żabotyński niech żyje]..
Besides soda water and other articles, even ping-pong, one also gets here
— hot sausages [parówki]...
The dealer in the "warm and hot ones" advertises his article in an original way. Instead of shouting like everyone else, he swallows the sausages, and after every "bite" he throws a piece of wood [?] into the special comfortable stove
— hot sausages...
• • •
"No joy without sorrow." At every Jewish celebration one "swallows" down a bitter drop. Of bitter drops we Jews have, it seems, more than enough... And when Dr. Rechtszaft, who "stands in for" [wyręcza] the Będzin Zionists, speaks about Lag ba-Omer, Hitler the murderer pops up, and as a sign of mourning the celebration in the open field is interrupted for one minute, no more. The doctor, who works in the field of sport, looks at his watch
— only one minute...
• • •
Set apart [?] from all the camps is the "obóz" [camp] of "Ha-Noar ha-Tsioni".
— Shomer pedigree...
They sing Hebrew, Yiddish and Polish songs; one is not particular about the content — as long as there is singing.
At first it puzzles me, it is incomprehensible to me: the "Anu olim" together with "Ja mam nosa" somehow do not stick together, a disharmony, but later it becomes clear to me.
It is because of the match with other organizations: the "Anu" is a Shomer one and the "Nau" [?]
— a Herzliya one...
• • •
I try to get into the "obóz" of the Będzin "Gordonia". At the "border" I meet a Gordonia girl with a "weapon" in her hand and I ask her:
— "Mahaneh Gordonia?"
— "Co pan sobie życzy?" [What do you wish, sir?]...
— Is this the "obóz" of Gordonia? — I ask in Yiddish.
— "Tu nie można wejść" [No entry here]...
We went away — I and my companion — ashamed, children of one people who
— do not want to understand one another...
• • •
The sun is setting. The "Hakoach" orchestra takes leave of the forest with several marches and a "hora"; the young folk break into a dance. The couples too, who had been busy at cards the whole day, hurry to dance
— "in honour" of Lag ba-Omer.. a wedding day in the days of the Omer count...
• • •
The road to Będzin is crowded with people riding back and walking. The older village inhabitants look with admiration at the merry Jewish crowd, but the young folk, their children, are already being brought up in a different spirit.
— "Hitler jedzie!" [Hitler is coming!]... — they shout after us.
But who pays attention to the yapping of little puppies? The great Jewish crowd accompanies the "wycieczkowcy" [excursionists] right into the town...
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Behar-Bechukotai)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Behar-Bechukotai
The Portion
—o—
a) "And for thy cattle, and for the beast that are in thy land" (25:7)
A sabbatical (shmita) year, and "if ye shall say, What shall we eat?" — out of fear of hunger. And here, in our time, the modern civilized world regards as the first means of rescue: "reduction" — dismissing people who have worked for you for decades. Instead of injustice[?], wrong, murder, it is called by a modern name: reduction.
And thousands of years ago, before European civilization, a Torah was given which held that even when the beast in the field is hungry in a year of famine, you must bring it out of the house something to eat; you may not "reduce" even the beast of the field... Hegyonot El-Ami.
—o—
b) "And ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family."
"Rav Yehuda says: to his possession and to his family he returns, but he does not return to the authority that was in his hand." Yalkut.
You can give the former slave back his home, his family, but not his personal freedom ("the authority that was in his hand"). It is hard, hard, after years of servitude, to be able to shake off the slavery that eats into the soul like rust. Havot Yair.
—o—
c) "And ye shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safety" (ibid., 19)
When you will have food to satiety ("and ye shall eat your fill") and you will sit quietly in the land, and the land will not need to spew you out because of your sins ("that the land spue not you out also, when ye defile it") — that is indeed a blessing: not to sin when the stomach is full... Tefillat Mordechai.
—o—
d) "And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee" (ibid., 35)
A.
The Torah says to the well-to-do brother: when "thy brother be waxen poor", then "his hand faileth with thee" — you are just as poor as he. One who has poor relatives is not to be envied for his wealth... Divrei Shaul.
B.
"That is what is written: Happy is he that considereth the poor." Midrash Rabbah.
Every commandment requires s i m p l i c i t y  (wholeheartedness). Only charity requires w i s d o m. In charity one must be clever — to give in such a way as not to shame the recipient. Arono shel Yosef.
* * *
An interesting episode is related by R' Yaakov HaLevi Lipschitz, secretary of the Kovno [Kaunas] rabbi R' Yitzchak Elchanan, of blessed memory.
R' Yitzchak Elchanan once comes to a famous rich man of Kovno for a donation for a respectable man who had come down in the world.
The rich man wants to know the name of the impoverished man. But R' Yitzchak Elchanan will by no means tell him. The rich man swears that he will reveal the name of the impoverished man to no one. But the Kovno rabbi will not agree to that either.
The rich man tries another way:
— I will give you ten roubles as a donation if you tell me.
Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan will not hear of it. The rich man goes further: I will give you twenty, fifty roubles — it does not help.
Finally the rich man jumps up:
— How much, Rabbi, do you expect to collect?
— Two hundred roubles.
— Then I give you four hundred, if you tell me in secret the name of the recipient. I will swear not to tell anyone.
— Not even for all the wealth in the world.
Seeing R' Yitzchak Elchanan's firmness, the rich man invites him into a separate room and tells him how far he, the rich man, has fallen, but he was ashamed to turn to people; yet seeing how R' Yitzchak Elchanan can keep a secret and will not reveal the name of a recipient even for all the wealth in the world, he asks him to help him too and to collect support for him...
—o—
e) "And ye shall eat your bread to the full... And I will give peace in the land."
Peace among Jews can only exist when "ye shall eat your bread to the full"; but when Jews have no livelihood, they inform on one another, quarrel and tear at each other.
Arono shel Yosef.
—o—
Haftarah.
f) "As the partridge sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; so he that getteth riches, and not by right."
The writers of parables compare wealth to winged creatures: it likes to fly away... Only with the one in whose home the wealth was born does it feel at home. Only with "the partridge that hatcheth not", the one whose wealth was born among strangers, "that getteth riches, and not by right" — from such a one it likes to fly away: "it shall leave him in the midst of his days". Kochav miYaakov.
—o—
Avot.
g) "He who gives and wants others to give — is pious" (5:13)
The piety lies in his giving before "others give": before he comes to demand of others that they give charity — he himself gives first... Alshich.
What Must One Know about Moving a Radio to a Summer Residence?

[Radio — reader information.] Summer is beginning and the public is already getting ready to leave for the dacha [summer cottage].
Many people take their radio sets with them, so as to have the opportunity there too of enjoying the radio broadcasts. We therefore find it necessary to give our readers a few instructions on what one must do with the radio when moving it to a summer residence, so as to be in order with the post office.
Normally the radio listener is obliged to notify the post office every time he changes his place of residence. An exception is made only for those who go away to a summer residence, but for no longer than 4 months. In this way the radio listener can continue to pay the normal monthly radio fee at the same post office as all year round.
As we see, no formalities whatever are needed for moving the radio set to another place during the summer months. One need only notify the post office of the temporary change of address. The radio installation that remains in town, however — for example the aerial and the earthing — must be secured so that nobody can make use of them during the summer months. It is best to lead the earth wire out to the far side of the window and there to join[?] it with the aerial and s o l d e r  it. In this way the radio inspector, should he come to the radio listener's permanent residence, will be assured that nobody can use the aerial.
—o—
[Economy — counterfeiting.] Counterfeit 5-rouble coins.
In connection with the fact that lately the strong, "pedigreed" currencies, such as the English pound and the American dollar, periodically waver, the so-called "stocking bankers" [people who hoard savings at home] have turned their favour and attention to the pre-war tsarist gold 5-rouble pieces.
This weakness has been sniffed out by certain money counterfeiters, and false gilded tsarist "fivers" have appeared in circulation. Inside they are lead, tin or something else, and on the outside gold — as long as the look and the weight are right.
Pioneer Motifs — Neta Landner

Neta Landner

Pioneer Motifs
(Dedicated to my children Sarah and Yitzhak in the Land of Israel.)

1.
By the Mediterranean Sea there is a corner,
wild, neglected for generations,
laid waste by Edom and Ishmael,
until the Children of Israel, Zion's children,
made a covenant anew
to unite with Mother Earth;
fire-altars have been set up,
priest-pioneers stand there, Maccabee children,
hammer and plough in hand;
an incense of blood, marrow and sweat
each one offers up with joy.
Eyes gleam with fever,
drunk with the passion of creation;
the hammer pounds by the highway,
asphalt rolled with drops of sweat,
sparks spray till smoke rises;
shoulder to shoulder, intertwined,
worker-pioneers, girl-pioneers
in the ring of the wild hora dance;
in the void the echo fades
from Ruhama in the south
to Metula in the north.

2.
Young hearts flutter in the Diaspora,
swept along by the fiery lava;
old homes vanish in smoke,
warm nests, gloomy, saddened;
father's and mother's hearts are broken;
frozen stays the bleeding earth
of the lonely, wretched mother;
the tear chokes the father in his throat:
"Oh, my only daughter,
washing laundry, milking cows —
what kind of purpose is that for you?!
Oh son, my only Kaddish,
knocking stones by the highway —
where is your strength for that?!
Over seas and rivers
how shall I swim to you?!"

3.
The children — their eyes cast down,
the heart wrung by their parents' grief;
hard, hard it is to leave the warm home;
the mother wants to comfort,
to receive the mother's blessing for the road;
the daughter clings to the mother,
streams of tears flow from both.
The children on the train, on the ship,
one desire, one prayer in their hearts:
faster, quicker, to be among the builders,
to greet sister and brother
in kibbutz, kvutza, in town, in village;
chests heave, song rings out:
"Anu olim artza, beshira uvezimra" ("We go up to the Land with song and melody")...
From the Book Table. A Polish Writer on Present-Day Germany

From the Book Table.
A Polish writer on present-day Germany

The well-known Polish writer Dr. Nowakowski has published a book under the title "Niemcy à la minute" ("Germany à la minute"). In this book the author conveys his impressions of present-day Germany, where, together with Jewish trade and Jewish existence, German culture too is going under — the culture that for generations was enriched by Jewish scholars and thinkers.

Here is what the author says about the German theatre:

The Jews in the German theatre.

"The purge is directed against the leading actors, and first and foremost against Jews. And if so, one can already boldly say the Rabbis' Kaddish for the German theatre (in the text it is 'Requiem', a Catholic prayer for the dead), for wherever one may act, wherever you may cast a glance, everywhere, and even in the most important positions, there are Jews, beginning with Reinhardt, Rekse [?], Goldmann, etc. Reinhardt is not merely a typical representative of the wonderful, beautiful epoch of the German theatre, but also the personification of the theatre itself over the last 30 years. The gap created by Reinhardt's departure no one will be able to fill. Reinhardt's place in the German theatre no substitute whatever will be able to take. In this case, as in many others, they threw out the baby with the bathwater. In Hitler's opinion the Jews have not developed any creative power that could give the world something new, original; as proof, in Hitler's opinion, may serve the fact that Jews are found in the front rank in art. 'The Jewish actor is only a well-trained monkey that imitates what he has seen somewhere, and only thanks to the Jewish press has the Jewish actor acquired — although he is only a bungler — such an honoured place on the world stage.' With Hitler, however — says Mr. Nowakowski — it is hard to argue. He is a good judge of theatre, because he himself is no bad actor. The Jewish actors, however — says Mr. Nowakowski — are also no children at play in the matter of theatrical art, and in particular those who play on the German stage are excellent. And in general, theatrical art is a field in which the Jews go their own, well-trodden ways. The theatrical genius and the theatrical art no one will take away from them, not even Hitler in person.

Hitler can, however, drive out all Jewish and left-wing actors; and that is perhaps the most comical thing in the whole story. What do actors have in common with politics? What do the political convictions of the prima donna, or of the comedian, matter to me as a spectator or as a theatre director? Or, for example, the radical views of this or that cabaret girl? Let them belong, in good health, to whatever political grouping their heart desires. Only one condition can we set them: to play well; talent — that is the basis, but the rest?!

Here in Poland people say that some actors are Bolsheviks, especially those who demand an advance (zaliczka) too energetically. I too suspect that Junosza-Stępowski is a radical reactionary, even a clandestine monarchist, but it concerns me as much as last year's snow. He is such an excellent actor that for all I care he may belong even to the Angel of Death's party; ours belong everywhere to the 'Brydż' or the 'Railway' party. And it is a very rare [?] case that an artist gets an 'engagement' thanks to his membership in the 'Strzelec', for example. I know a few such cases, which, however, were crowned with a not overly excellent artistic result.

The theatre is today such a small part of cultural life, its role grows smaller from day to day because of the sound film, and yet here too Hitler has made his brutal fist felt; and indeed, taking the present German theatre as an illustrative example, one can imagine what changes will occur in other areas of political and cultural life as well, which are much more important in practice than the theatre and less [—] for other reasons.

A new Hebrew-Polish dictionary.

A complete Hebrew-Polish dictionary by A. Benaori [?] has appeared on the book market (published by the A. Gitlin publishing house, Warsaw). The dictionary contains about 15 thousand Hebrew words, expressions and phrases; it also includes newly created words with which the Hebrew language has been enriched in connection with the development of the Jewish Yishuv in the Land of Israel.

Nowadays such a practical dictionary is truly a very useful handbook for everyone who wishes to perfect himself in the Hebrew language, or uses it in speech and writing.
The silent sorrow of the German Jews.

S. Rosenfeld.

Much has already been written about the great political, economic and spiritual catastrophe [khurbn] that the Jews in Germany are now living through. They have been deprived of their right to exist, the right to work and the right to any human or civil right whatsoever. They have been deprived of their material property and, on top of that, of their spiritual property as well — their faith in German culture, German progress and German humanity; and they have also been deprived of the belief that whatever they are, they are — but G e r m a n s they are...
It makes no difference that they still persist in their obstinacy and do not stop persuading themselves and the Nazis that they are Germans. They themselves, one senses, no longer believe it. This is precisely what proves to us their insistence on their Germanness. One example:
Rabbi Lehmann, a leader of German liberal Jewry, has published in the "Jewish Bulletin" an article "On the Situation", in which he writes:
"The great political events in the country have no connection with the Jews as a religious community. For us Judaism is, and will remain, only a religion, which embraces all those who acknowledge Judaism, without distinction of people or race.
"We German Jews are a part of the German national body; we belong to it always, in good times and in bad. German nationality is our political nationality; our grandfathers fought for the liberation of Germany and we took part in the German wars; we fought for a new Germany; we a r e Germans — whether our enemies like it or not.
"We are Germans not because they acknowledge it or not, but because Germany is a part of our self: because our fate is bound up with their fate. We have no intention of leaving Germany and belonging [printed 'atsuhern'] to another nationality, of begging hospitality from others. Where we are, there we shall stay, and there we shall fight for our rights until our last breath. One must know how to choose the moment when to cry out and when to be silent; now for us is the time to be silent."
Who does not feel here, in this obstinate assertion "we are Germans", a cry of despair? Who does not sense here the terror of a drowning man stretching out his hands for a straw in the air?
Certainly it is felt, certainly it is sensed, and certainly it is a great sorrow; but that is not yet the whole sorrow, and it is not about t h a t that we shall speak here.
T h e sorrow I wish to stress here is far deeper still. It is the sorrow which the Jews of all ages, even in the bloodiest circumstances, never knew. It is, namely, the sorrow of a man who does not know and does not feel w h y he is being dragged to the gallows and why he is being hurled into the fire.
The Jews in the times of the Crusaders, of the Black Death, of the Haidamak uprising and of the Petliura pogroms knew that they were perishing for their faith; had they betrayed their people and declared themselves members of the s l a u g h t e r e r nations, they would have saved their lives and the lives of their loved ones. And since they did not do so, but stretched out their necks beneath the knife, they had the awareness and the comfort that they were suffering for their loyalty to their people and to their God; this gave meaning to their sufferings and sweetened their sorrow.
But with what shall the German Jew console himself? He hears that he is persecuted because he is a Jew; that he is tortured for his Jewishness. What sort of Jewishness is it, then, when a Jew there is none? What is that Jewishness to him, for which Hitler torments him? Does he feel it? Does it live in him? Does he live by it? N o and n o! He has, he says, a religion, and "the great political events have no connection whatsoever with the Jews as a religious community." To what, then, do they have a connection? To the naked Jew, to the Jewish human being — but apart from the religion, "with which — as Rabbi Lehmann asserts — Hitlerism has no connection whatsoever." After all [printed 'vegn'], there are no Jews there at all, only pure G e r m a n s — and it is these very Lehmannite Germans who are tortured, beaten and killed, and they accept all these sufferings with love: they put up with them — because "now is a time for silence" — and so go quietly to "kiddush ha-shem" [martyrdom, lit. sanctification of the Name]. For what "Name", then, are they sacrificing themselves here? Not for G o d ' s name — for nobody is touching Him; not for the name of the Jewish people — for to the Lehmanns such a thing does not exist at all. It turns out that they are sacrificing themselves for the name "G e r m a n"... The Lehmanns argue: "We are Germans" and "Germany is a part of ourselves", and Hitler argues: "The G e r m a n s — that is us!" and you have no share in Germany.
And when the Lehmannite Jew is dragged to the gallows or hurled into the fire b e c a u s e he is a... G e r m a n — can I imagine a greater sorrow than that? Can this false consciousness give [some?] meaning to their sufferings? Can it sweeten their sorrow? They must surely ask themselves: w h y are we suffering? In the name of what idea are we dying? In whose name do we bear these great torments?
And what, indeed, can we answer them? What answer can they give themselves that might ease their sorrow even a little? There is no such answer for them, and that is the greatest sorrow that can befall the lot of a hunted human being.
I recall a fact from the first Russian pogroms in the year 1881. The first pogrom took place in Elisavetgrad; unbridled assimilation was already strongly represented there among the intelligentsia. But [printed 'arer'] the pogromists made no distinction between Jew and Jew. So they made a pogrom in the house of a certain Doctor Gelbach. A son of the pogrom-stricken doctor, when he saw what had been done in their house, turned to his father with the question:
— Papa, are we Jews too, then?
— This innocent question — the father said afterwards — moved me more than the whole pogrom. I heard a bitter reproach in that question. All at once I felt that I had betrayed my child. For if I had not guarded him from being beaten, I should at least have warned him, so that he would know [printed 'fun'] and understand w h y he was being beaten...
And the German Jews did n o t guard thereby either themselves or their children. Surely the children of the Lehmannite Germans, too, asked their parents in astonishment: are we Jews too?
And what could those superstitious fathers answer them? Even less than that Elisavetgrad father could. For the latter at least felt during the pogrom that he had deceived himself, had betrayed his child, and he sought a way to get out of the false position into which assimilation had brought him. But the "liberal Jews" of Lehmann's cut — they are convinced even now that they are Germans. Even now they still pretend not to feel the betrayal they have committed against themselves and against their children. Even now they still cling to their "Germanism" — although they no longer have the peace of mind which assimilated "wicked men" count on, nor do they have the heroically illuminated sufferings of national righteous men, who k n o w what they are suffering for... They would still rather be fifty percent German than one hundred percent themselves. They do not even have the courage to learn a moral from their horrifying situation, and, standing already on the far side of the threshold of the flaming hell which their Germanness has kindled for them, they still do not forget to kneel before their tormentors and to sing their old song of flattery about "Deutschland über alles" — over them, too, the tormented themselves.
And with such a consciousness, sincere or forced, to go to torments, to pain and even to death —
can anyone imagine a greater sorrow?...
Hitler and His Two Girls

[Humour — satire on Hitler.]
On my editor's orders I smuggled myself into Germany and also [?] sneaked into Hitler's cabinet. The brown-shirted ataman sat in an armchair, and to his right and left — two girls at typewriters; one Hilda and the other Greta.
Hitler dictated and they typed. Hilda — decrees for the ministers, and Greta — information for the press.
Hilda! From tomorrow on only two and a half Jewish doctors and three and a half lawyers may practise in Berlin.
Greta! No decrees whatsoever have been issued against Jewish doctors and lawyers.
Hilda! The former head of the big department store Hermann Tietz is appointed deputy of the night watchman in the back yard of the store.
Greta! The report of the shameful atrocity propaganda about director Tietz is sucked out of thin air. He continues to hold the most respected [?] post in his business.
Hilda! The Jewish dead in the prisons are to be carried out at night and buried in a field behind the Jewish cemetery.
Greta! The atrocity propaganda claiming that Jews are tortured and tormented in German prisons is a shameful lie.
Hilda! All state banks are to withdraw the credits of Jewish merchants.
Greta! The German Jews have begun to boycott [?] the state banks.
Hilda! No Jews whatsoever are to be issued any foreign passports or visas.
Greta! The atrocity propaganda claiming that Jews are fleeing Germany is a complete fabrication.
Hilda! Distribute in all the larger cities of Europe and America a hundred thousand letters of reassurance with with [sic] forged Jewish signatures.
Greta! New York, Paris, London and Warsaw report that the letters of the Berlin Jews to their co-religionists have made a good impression and calmed people's minds.
Hilda! Send ten thousand secret agents out into the city to eavesdrop on the mood of the population, and at the slightest murmur [?] immediately arrest the malcontent and put him in chains.
Greta! The mood in Germany is elevated; the population demonstrates continually for the Führer with cries of "Heil Hitler!"
Hitler gave a yawn, and I slipped out of the cabinet.
Avi-Ver.
A Queen Who Dies for Her Sins

[Historical serial — Mary, Queen of Scots, part 6.]
The tragic story of Queen Mary of Scotland. Her loves and political intrigues.
6.
The people, however, could not calm down; the uproar over the murder of King Darnley (printed "Dargli") did not cease, and the guilt laid on Bothwell as the murderer was great. Above all, Darnley's father did not keep silent; with factual material he turned to the Privy Council, demanding that Bothwell be brought to trial as the murderer of his son.
And the interventions had effect. On 12 April Bothwell was brought before a court, and Darnley's father appeared as his accuser.
On the day of the trial Bothwell gathered around himself four thousand soldiers, who went about the streets and were ready to take up a fight against those who were hostile to their leader Bothwell.
The royal castle too was under his command, so that this had the effect that the trial against him would not take place. The accuser, too, was afraid to appear at the trial under such circumstances against the murderer of his son, and he wrote the judges a letter in which he excused himself that he was ill and could not come to the trial. The end, however, was that Bothwell was acquitted on the grounds of "incorrect evidence".
After that [?] trial Bothwell really got on his high horse: with the queen as his wife and with parliament — even behind him — he laughed at everyone and did whatever his heart desired.
The queen made him a duke and did everything he demanded of her. How far she was enslaved to her present husband is shown well enough by the fact that Bothwell, as a Protestant, forced Mary to marry him according to Protestant rite, and the officiant at the wedding was in fact a Protestant clergyman who had formerly been a Catholic bishop. This of course greatly vexed the Catholic Mary, but her love for Bothwell was so strong that she did everything for his sake. What the murdered Darnley had not achieved, Bothwell achieved with her, and she shared power with him.
But Bothwell's rule, and at the same time Mary's rule too, did not last long. The discontent among the people grew from day to day, the revolt began, and things could no longer be borne.
Bothwell and Mary, seeing before them the danger from the [gathered? —] mob, also from the military, began to flee and hide. They ran from one castle to another to protect themselves from an attack by the hostile camp.
The [—] mob chose a delegation from among itself, which informed Mary that no harm whatever would befall her if she separated from Bothwell. "We do not want to do anything to you," they argued, "only to save you and free you from Bothwell's hands."
But Mary rejected all proposals, because she was simply bewitched by Bothwell. She was so chained to him that she did not want to part from him. It once happened that Bothwell fled at a dangerous moment from his pursuers; she did not want to be without him and decided to run after him even if the worst should happen to her.
The revolt was in full swing. Mary and Bothwell still had supporters who were ready to lay down their lives for them and waged a fierce fight with the revolutionaries, but their fate was already sealed.
Bothwell's defeat came. In a clash between the two fighting sides the revolutionaries won a victory and besieged Bothwell's palace.
The revolutionaries then sent a special envoy to Mary demanding that she separate from Bothwell, or that Bothwell come out to a duel. Bothwell was already willing to agree to this, but Mary would not let him.
After a long deliberation it was decided that Mary should surrender and that Bothwell should be allowed to go free to his birthplace with several of his supporters.
Mary took a heartfelt leave of him, passionately embraced and kissed him. The soldiers could not bear to look at it. It angered them greatly; the blood of the innocently perished Darnley gave them no rest, and they began to shout:
"Death to the murderess and the whore!"
Mary was not frightened by these words; she remembered that she was a queen, and her courage awoke in her. Although she saw that she was helpless, she began in her helpless rage to threaten the soldiers that she would send all the revolutionaries to the gallows.
These dying-gasp [?] words no longer made any impression on the military. They laughed at her even more, and as a prisoner in the hands of the revolutionaries she was led away to Edinburgh, where she was lodged in the house of the mayor.

Continuation of the kehilla comedy.
Several months ago the presidium of the local kehilla council was elected. Mr. Nute Landner (Zionist) was elected chairman, and vice-chairman — Mr. Itshe Meir Kurland (Mizrachi).
And since the election has, for "reasons", not been confirmed to this day, another way out was found, one that should be "acceptable to God and to people"... Resolution of the House-Owners on Paying for Water

[Będzin — house-owners.] With the participation of some 150 house-owners, a meeting took place last Sunday on the “Góra Zamkowa”, chaired by the president, Mr. Gelbhar, at which a series of questions was discussed, above all the question of payment for water by the house-owners.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla.] On Tuesday afternoon a meeting of all the kehilla employees, from the rabbis down to the gravediggers, took place in the premises of the local kehilla...

[Sosnowiec — fraud.] On Małachowskiego Street a stranger ran up to Yeshaye Frenkel and asked Frenkel whether he had not found on the street money that he had lost. Frenkel explained to him that he had found no money at all, and to reassure him he showed the stranger his own 40 zł that he had on him. The stranger took the 40 zł into his hand and, after counting them, wrapped them in paper and gave them back to Mr. Frenkel. Membership drive of "Linat ha-Holim"

[Sosnowiec — Charity and health.] As is known, a short time ago an outpatient clinic was opened at the "Linat ha-Holim" society, where poor Jewish sick people receive medical help. The clinic is developing very well. Besides the doctors there so far, the young Dr. Gelbart and 2 nurses have also been engaged.

Can taxes secured by mortgages be annulled?

[Taxes.] In very many cases the tax authority has secured itself by a mortgage on the property of tax debtors.
Now the question arises whether the ministerial circular on remitting taxes will be applied to them.
It must be explained:
In principle it is not provided that taxes be remitted for persons who have some property or other and whose taxes are registered on the mortgage. Rather, the intention is to remit the taxes of those who are thoroughly ruined and [who] own absolutely nothing any more, and with whom a distraint (zajęcie) would find nothing; if one has property, the matter is not so.
But in the circular there is a point ["fact"] about remitting part of the overdue taxes, and even all of them, for those whom an auction and distraint would thoroughly ruin. From this one can see that the tax authority does not want to drive people to ruin.
Such tax debtors who have property, a house, a flat, and whose taxes are guaranteed by a mortgage, and whom the auction would surely break, may also apply with petitions to the tax authority, set out their economic situation and ask that the tax be annulled for them in full or in part, so that they will be able to pay.
We point out that those who are able, even under the worst conditions, to pay part of the overdue taxes should not ask for the whole sum to be remitted.

On Tuesday the workers of the Fitzner and Gamper factory went on strike. After the labour inspector declared to them that a conference would take place regarding their grievances, the strike, which had lasted 4 hours, was called off.
Zawiercie — L.O.P.P. propaganda evening

[Zawiercie — L.O.P.P.] Last Saturday evening, under the chairmanship of Mr. Spies, state instructor, a propaganda talk on the subject "The L.O.P.P. Week from 14 to 21 May" took place in the premises of the "Gemilut Hesed" loan fund. The speakers were Messrs. Liberman and the head of Public School No. 3, Mr. Lejzerowicz, who explained the significance of the campaign and called on those assembled to found an L.O.P.P. branch at the Jewish community.
Mr. Spies and the president of the Jewish community, Mr. Bornsztajn, also spoke on the same subject in the town synagogue (Stadt-shul).
Useful Information

[Useful information — law, taxes and social insurance.]
On collectors. The Minister of Social Welfare has confirmed the position of a special commission, which established that under Art. 2, point 6 of the decree on white-collar („mental“) employees of 16. 3. 28 and of the decree on employees' insurance of 24. XI 27, those collectors may be recognised as white-collar employees who issue bills and collect them, issue receipts, prepare special statements or forms, or are authorised to alter the prepared bills, grant reductions to payers and spread debts into instalments.
On the property tax. The Treasury Ministry has issued an ordinance immediately to cancel the property tax which, under the law on the extraordinary levy [danina], need not be paid.
New bill-of-exchange forms. Under the ordinance of the Treasury Minister of 14. 10. 32 on stamp duty, new stamped forms are being introduced, on different paper and in a different format than hitherto. Under the ordinance the existing forms could be used until the end of March 1933.
Under a circular of the Treasury Ministry of 3. 4. 33, bills of exchange on old forms are not to be challenged when the issue date of the bill is later than 31 March but not later than 30 April [kwiecień] 1933.
Nor are bills on old forms to be challenged that bear no dates or later ones, i.e. after 30. 4. 33, if one can prove (by books, declarations and the like) that the bill was signed before 1 May 1933. From that date, therefore, only new forms are to be used.
On shop assistants and dispatch clerks. The Supreme Administrative Tribunal has recently ruled that shop assistants and so-called „expedients“ [dispatch clerks] who have no educational qualification (6 classes of secondary school, or elementary school plus practice) need not be subject to the Insurance Institution for White-Collar Employees (Z.U.P.U.).
Dr. R. R—n.
Legal Answers

[Legal answers — readers' questions.]
Mr. Sh. L. — You can file with the court a request to have the matter examined judicially, i.e. an objection [sprzeciw] against the payment order [nakaz], but the court will not admit any witnesses against bills of exchange, and you will therefore not stop the enforcement of the payment order.
Mr. A—n — If within 7 days of the publication of the judgment you did not request the reasons for the judgment, you can no longer appeal after that deadline.
Mr. A. — In the district court, under the new procedure, representation by an advocate is compulsory, i.e. only advocates can file cases. You therefore cannot file the case in court yourself.
In general the matter is complicated, and without professional help you will achieve nothing.
Reader B. — The moratorium on mortgage debts does not apply to overdue interest, nor to current interest (but only 6 per cent).
R. R.
